# LabOS dated work log

Consolidated: 2026-11-01. Implementation, build, deployment and acceptance are
distinct states. A historical PASS proves only its stated checks and date.
Reports retain their original primary/helper identities and review limitations.
Consult [the plan](PLAN.md) for scope and [the reference](REFERENCE.md) for contracts.

## 2026-11-02 — PRIMARY — substantial A4/A5 resource delivery and recovery batch

Replaced the viewer's whole-file renderer fetch/write with a native, session-fenced
export command. The destination comes from a native Save dialog, never an IPC path.
The command copies in 1 MiB buffers, pins the source identity and expected digest,
checks current account/lease/read access throughout and verifies SHA-256 against the
immutable upload/edit intention or current verified replication manifest. Only a
complete fsynced, verified copy replaces the chosen destination. Windows replacement
uses MoveFileExW replacement/write-through; failures preserve the prior destination.
Unique partial exports are cleaned without touching authored versions. Managed app
storage and source-file destinations are rejected, including Windows case aliases.
An abrupt process/PC crash can leave the uniquely named partial export in the chosen
external folder; the prior destination remains intact. No unverified directory-wide
cleanup or promise of crash cleanup is introduced.
Cancellation before selecting a destination writes nothing. No domain/outbox/server
mutation is created for an explicitly requested external copy.

Closed the desktop download/access URL fallback when no native file capability is
available. Viewer text reads reject a missing local URL instead of fetching the
current app document, fence late account replies and explain the large-preview
limit. Image/media panes display missing-copy state; inventory avoids empty image
URLs. Browser server access remains its existing browser transport. Local file
range planning now handles suffix/open/closed requests, clamps bounded bodies,
ignores Range on HEAD, returns authorized 416 for unsatisfiable ranges and 413 for
whole reads exceeding the existing 32 MiB bound. Every successful response keeps
the existing account/lease/capability/revision checks; unauthorized errors do not
disclose file sizes. No worker timeout or file-size safety bound was relaxed.

Extended native dependency reconstruction to pending folder creations and copy
sources across native/legacy payload shapes. These derived edges confer no access
and never rewrite the immutable payload. Conflict blocking/retirement follows nested
folder children, copies and subsequent mutations while preserving earlier/independent
and other-account work. Before retirement, local_resource_recoveries retains the
connected intention IDs/resolution in the same SQLite transaction; original outbox
payloads, upload/edit provenance and byte files remain. Archive failure aborts the
resolution. This is recovery evidence, not a new authorization or complete export UI.
Revisiting a root extends the archived identity set without replacing earlier
evidence. Unreadable existing recovery evidence refuses retirement; newer work is
not silently acknowledged or hidden behind an older archive entry.
The existing conflict confirmation now explicitly covers folder children and all
supported attachment/metadata/content dependency retirements, with an account check
after confirmation and before dispatch. It does not claim that retained work has
been restored or that its access rights are still valid.

Verification collected as a grouped batch: initial focused client 23 PASS; native
resource-focused tests 61 PASS. Expanded native whole suite 178 PASS / 12 ignored
live integration cases, including >32 MiB external copy/digest equality, source/session
change, bad digest, destination preservation, partial cleanup, range boundaries and
file-backed folder/copy recovery/account isolation/reopen/archive-failure rollback.
Initial full client run 501 PASS and frontend build PASS. A later review identified
and fixed the empty-URL text-consumer edge case; final affected/whole frontend rerun
is recorded below. No backend migration or PostgreSQL writer changed in this batch;
SQLite tests exercise the actual desktop database, not a PostgreSQL substitute.

Final complete client rerun after the preview correction: 502 PASS. The conflict
confirmation/dispatch guard and repeated-root archive merge then received a final
focused/native/type/build pass; results follow once complete.

STATUS: A4/A5/A2 bounded subchecks implemented; final source rerun and coordinated
native/GUI export, audible seek and stopped-API/reconnect acceptance remain distinct.
Mixed content/move authoring, non-resource unsynced destinations, full recovery
export UI, recoverable encryption/retention and remaining consumers remain open.
Personal V1 app/API/database/files were not restarted, reset or deployed over.

## 2026-11-02 — PRIMARY — C1/C2 persistent drafts and reviewed graph approval

Implemented shared bounded project/task/experiment/link schemas and canonical
UUIDs/digests across server, renderer and native repositories. Draft saves are
account-scoped SQLite state plus immutable outbox events in one transaction; failure
never triggers an HTTP write. Saved revisions/authors/generation origin remain stable.
The server retains generation requests/results/provenance separately: same-request
retry reuses its result, deliberate regeneration gets a new ID. Generation creates
no lab work. A centered assistant editor supports manual/generated editable JSON,
review checkbox, unsaved-close guard and pending-approval disclosure.

Explicit human acceptance binds revision/digest, account/lease and existing project
lifecycle. Native commits the complete provisional graph and one graph event; server
uses canonical work handlers and commits all nodes, required child/root audits and
receipt together. Projects start Planning, tasks Todo, experiments Planned. Stock,
cash, reservations and physical results are untouched. Exact receipt counts/digest/
project ID are required for acknowledgement. Pending project edits are locked until
confirmation. Pull preserves authored graphs while refreshing authority; proposal
events wait for their predecessor's acknowledgement. Browser uncertain writes retain
their original payload/ID for explicit retry after closing the editor.

## 2026-11-02 — PRIMARY — C4 consented voice input source

Added a bounded online transcription service using the existing Gemini SDK's inline
audio generateContent path. Explicit enablement, provider key, audio-capable model
and deployment-specific processing/retention disclosure are required; default is
disabled. The disclosure/model hash must match the user's per-recording consent.
Server limits MIME/bytes and request frequency, times out/cancels provider requests,
checks current credentials before and after processing, sanitizes errors and clears
the upload buffer. No provider Files API, local audio file, database/outbox audio,
conversation insertion or automatic message send is used. Cancellation cannot
recall already received provider audio; the consent UI states this limitation.

A shared centered dialog records locally in memory, supports stop/cancel/preview,
uploads only after explicit Transcribe, retains an uncertain recording for an
explicit retry and exposes an editable transcript before insertion. Integrated into
the assistant composer and Notebook. Notebook insertion checks the exact draft;
account/session changes fence uploads/results/insertion. C3 microphone focus stops
competing playback and late permission/recording callbacks cannot revive capture.
The earlier temporary browser-dictation controller/tests from this source batch
were superseded and removed: Notebook now uses the same disclosed C4 path instead
of implicit browser SpeechRecognition. Earlier test counts are historical batches.

audit consistency, retries and pending-work cache reconciliation.

CURRENT WRITE PATH: these administrative actions require server confirmation on
desktop and browser. Desktop then reconciles the confirmed project snapshot via
the canonical native merge. Ordinary authored project work keeps SQLite/outbox.

WHY IT BYPASSES OFFLINE-FIRST: prior membership/grant routes wrote through pool
without atomic audit/receipt or current transactional authority. Client retries
had no stable identity/account fence; desktop immediately reread a stale local
workspace after server confirmation. A pending parent edit also skipped all
server project fields, freezing team/permissions and potentially retaining edit
authority after scope changes.

RISK: stale forms overwrite newer roles/grants, lost-ACK replay reapplies obsolete
access, audit loss, stale-account results populate UI, confirmed membership looks
unsaved, and pending authored work preserves stale authority or disappears from
the normal view without a retained recovery copy.

RECOMMENDED CHANGE: a shared server-confirmed management adapter with immutable
retry bodies, expected-value checks, locked current role/permissions and atomic
audit/receipt; reconcile confirmed local state while preserving authored work.

ACTUAL CHANGE MADE: all four set/delete grant/member routes share one adapter.
It locks project, current actor/permission overrides and target rows; checks active
targets on sets, current admin membership authority or owner/lead/admin grant
authority, restricted grant scope, and the reviewed expected role/level. Stable
broker receipts bind actor/project/operation/target/payload and replay without
reapplying an older state. DELETE receipts satisfy response_json NOT NULL while
returning public 204. Grant listing now also checks current authority inside a
transaction. Client writes retain uncertain keys/bodies, reject local-only login
and missing bases, validate confirmations, fence account changes, and serialize
the required native project refresh with background sync. Candidate/grant reads
also fence stale accounts. Team removal passes the displayed role. Pending native
parent edits now refresh server team/authority fields; revoked/deleted pending
records retain work without normal read/edit access, including across restart
and later regrant. No pending outbox payload is rewritten or acknowledged.

access client checks PASS; wider project/client batch 62 PASS before the final
read guard, with its new read case covered in the focused rerun. Native project
suite 18 PASS, including disk SQLite downgrade/revocation/reopen/regrant with an
unchanged pending payload. Backend permission/project-visibility/review batch
38 PASS. A stale source-location assertion was updated to follow the delegated
grant writer, and one new test harness was corrected to transpile its TypeScript

Prepared actual PostgreSQL/production-HTTP rollback probe for SQL audit/receipt

No migration, deployment, desktop restart, V1 update or real access grant issued.

## 2026-11-01 — PRIMARY — B4 transactional project audit

MODULE: Project visibility, reservation decisions/fulfillment, deletion and
ordinary project outbox writes; B3/B4 history and audit consistency.

FILE: backend/src/routes/projects.js; backend/src/routes/sync.js;
backend/src/project-audit-http-live-probe.mjs;
backend/src/project-pull-http-live-probe.mjs;
backend/src/salvage-release-live-probe.mjs (fault injection only).

CURRENT WRITE PATH: desktop native project intentions use /sync/push. Existing
browser visibility/decision/fulfillment/delete routes own PostgreSQL transactions.

WHY IT BYPASSES OFFLINE-FIRST: ordinary project synchronization stored its retry
receipt and committed before its generic audit row. Several direct browser
transactions also committed before best-effort audit, including deletion of
projects/children with tombstones and reservation fulfillment stock effects.

RISK: a successful receipt/response could survive while its mandatory history
was missing; after a lost response, fulfillment replay could never recreate an
audit omitted by the original committed mutation. Deletion could remove records
and publish tombstones despite audit failure.

RECOMMENDED CHANGE: keep each affected mutation and required audit in its
existing PostgreSQL transaction, before its receipt and commit; preserve audit
ownership for handlers already writing their own required records.

ACTUAL CHANGE MADE: browser reservation decisions/fulfillment, project visibility
and deletion now pass client/required:true to the audit writer before commit.
Fulfillment no longer suppresses audit errors; its request-id replay path still
returns the existing movement without another audit/stock effect. Decision audit
retains decision/status/note information and adds the stored prior reservation.
Ordinary configured project sync entities plus project-item links now write
generic audit before the receipt in /sync/push. Review/reservation intents keep
their own existing transactional audit and are excluded from the new generic
write. Their receipt replay does not add audit rows. Salvage keeps its preceding
transactional audit behavior. No new authority or browser outbox is claimed.

VERIFICATION: syntax checks PASS for changed routes and probes. Affected project
and sync/resource regression batch: 46 PASS, 0 FAIL, 3 optional PostgreSQL SKIP.
Prepared a rollback-only production-HTTP/PostgreSQL probe for visibility/grant
rollback, reservation decision rollback, fulfillment balances/replay, and project
deletion with draft-child/tombstone rollback. Extended the existing project push
probe with audit-failure create/update/delete rollback and one audit per original
event across replay. Audit fault injection now executes SELECT 1/0 on the real
PostgreSQL connection at the audit insert point (also in the prepared salvage
probe), so these cases will exercise a real failed SQL transaction. They have
NOT RUN: elevated Docker inspection still reports no Linux-engine pipe. No mock
database acceptance substituted, deployment, migration or user-data write occurred.

STATUS: IMPLEMENTED IN SOURCE — AWAITING GROUPED POSTGRESQL ACCEPTANCE AND
COORDINATED DEVELOPMENT DEPLOYMENT. B3/B4 remain PARTIAL. Direct project access-
grant, membership and nested browser writers still need their own transaction,
current-authority and retry audit; this bounded change does not certify them.

timestamps and notes. Both stages stay inside the existing audit/receipt

inventory.view permission, normalizes the item UUID, applies parent project
visibility, and returns only positive issued/partially-settled custody. Browser
adapter validates array shape and account-session lifetime; desktop cache errors
still never become HTTP reads. Custody return selection is visible in both
runtimes. Existing shared writes preserve source holder/project/unit/quantity;
creation remains quarantine-only, and approved usable release settles custody
and credits original stock in the same audited receipt transaction. Damaged
issued material remains blocked from usable-stock release; repair lifecycle
implementation is still open.

VERIFICATION: 27 HTTP/native-boundary regressions PASS, including browser custody
reads, malformed response rejection, account switch masking, desktop missing/
failed/stale source reads without HTTP, immutable native batch retries and
displayed review versions. Existing native tests now use the real version helper
and updated runtime contract. TypeScript noEmit and JavaScript syntax PASS. Extended real PostgreSQL
rollback-only probe with restricted-source view/revocation checks and browser
custody partial-return audit/receipt rollback, stock/balance preservation and
single settlement on replay. PostgreSQL/GUI/reconnect acceptance NOT RUN;
Docker remains the outstanding database-verification prerequisite. No deployment,
migration, V1 install or live stock mutation was performed.

STATUS: IMPLEMENTED IN SOURCE — AWAITING GROUPED POSTGRESQL AND DESKTOP
ACCEPTANCE. B2 stays PARTIAL. Remaining boundaries include damaged-return repair
and the integrated outage/reconnect/parallel-client sweep.

## 2026-11-01 — PRIMARY — B2 disassembly batches and displayed review versions

MODULE: Salvage shared-source multi-output browser authoring and review concurrency.

FILE: backend/src/salvage-http.js; backend/src/routes/items.js;
desktop/src/api/items.ts; desktop/src/api/inventory-http.ts;
desktop/src/components/SalvageRecoveryPanel.tsx;
desktop/src/api/inventory-http.test.mjs;
backend/src/salvage-release-live-probe.mjs.

CURRENT WRITE PATH: desktop batch still saves one native SQLite/outbox intent;
browser batch persists its exact request in tab retry storage before HTTP and
uses applySalvageIntent in the transaction/audit/receipt adapter.

WHY IT BYPASSES OFFLINE-FIRST: batch authoring was desktop-only despite an existing
shared server handler. Separately, both review adapters looked up the latest
version at submission, replacing the version actually reviewed in the dialog.
This could permit a stale review to overwrite newer information.

RISK: duplicate disassembly outputs after reopening an uncertain browser form;
partial batches on audit/receipt failure; stale inspection or release accepted
against a newly fetched version the human had not reviewed.

RECOMMENDED CHANGE: reuse atomic batch application, persist original output IDs
and request identity, and carry the displayed version through review submission.

ACTUAL CHANGE MADE: browser batch route delegates to the shared handler with
201 responses, required transactional audit and receipt. Replay returns all
currently authorized batch members in original output order and rejects missing
or changed membership. The browser retry signature ignores newly generated form
IDs while preserving the original persisted body's IDs/key. The UI exposes the
batch option on both runtimes. Inspect/release now take the dialog's captured
version; native SQLite and PostgreSQL retain their existing stale-version checks.
The native adapter no longer refreshes a base immediately before queuing review.
Custody-source browser authoring and the separate damaged-return repair lifecycle
remain open; the desktop custody picker retains its runtime guard.

VERIFICATION: TypeScript noEmit PASS. Changed server/probe JavaScript syntax PASS.
All 12 inventory/salvage HTTP transport regressions PASS, including batch lost-ACK
replay after regenerated form IDs, fresh identity after confirmed completion,
displayed version preservation, rejection of missing versions without a fetch,
and original uncertain review body reuse after refresh. These are transport
checks, not simulated database acceptance. Extended the actual PostgreSQL
rollback-only HTTP probe for browser batch audit/receipt failure rollback,
atomic output membership, single batch/audit on replay and payload mismatch.
PostgreSQL, deployed API and GUI/outage/reconnect checks NOT RUN: Docker engine
pipe remains unavailable. No live user data, V1 installation or service changed.

STATUS: IMPLEMENTED IN SOURCE — AWAITING GROUPED POSTGRESQL/GUI VERIFICATION AND
COORDINATED DEVELOPMENT DEPLOYMENT. B2 remains PARTIAL; no parent closure claimed.

## 2026-11-01 — PRIMARY — B2 browser salvage mutation parity (preceding batch)

MODULE: Salvage recovery browser create, inspection and release; A1/A2/B2
authorization, retry and audit boundaries. Parent B2 remains PARTIAL.

FILE: backend/src/salvage-http.js; backend/src/routes/items.js;
desktop/src/api/items.ts; backend/src/salvage-release-live-probe.mjs.

CURRENT WRITE PATH: desktop remains native SQLite/outbox. Browser requests now
persist a retry key and immutable body in per-account tab session storage using
the existing inventory HTTP-intent helper, then call the shared salvage handler.

WHY IT BYPASSES OFFLINE-FIRST: prior browser create used unversioned pool writes
and generated a fresh server identity on retry; inspection and release used
separate direct routes without required audit/receipt atomicity. These were
browser server-authoritative exceptions, not desktop fallback paths.

RISK: duplicate recovered material after a lost response, stale inspection,
missing provenance/audit and effects acknowledged without a durable retry receipt.

RECOMMENDED CHANGE: reuse the shared salvage domain implementation and the
existing stable browser retry contract; commit mutation, audit and receipt together.

ACTUAL CHANGE MADE: three routes delegate to one transactional adapter using
applySalvageIntent. Create requires a client UUID; inspect/release require an
integer version. Advisory locking serializes each retry key; replay checks
actor/device/entity/operation/payload, current active account permissions and
current project authority. Replay returns the currently authorized recovery
without reapplying stock or audit. Required audit/receipt errors roll back the
whole mutation. Browser adapters retain uncertain retry bodies across tab reload
and refreshed displayed versions. A closed/cleared tab loses this browser retry
storage; it is not a browser offline outbox. Browser multi-output creation remains
desktop-only and is not claimed complete. Older browser callers missing keys or
versions fail closed and need the coordinated frontend/backend update.

VERIFICATION: changed JavaScript files pass node --check; desktop TypeScript
noEmit passes. Extended the existing real PostgreSQL rollback-only HTTP probe
for browser create/review/release replay, key mismatch, stale review, single stock
credit/audit cardinality, audit-failure rollback and receipt-failure rollback.
Added sync audit-failure rollback assertions for the preceding source change.
Those database probes were NOT RUN: Docker Linux engine pipe is absent even
with elevated inspection. No SQLite replacement test, deployment, migration,
desktop restart or V1 installation was performed. Phase-end outage/GUI/parallel
acceptance is still required; this batch does not constitute its completion.

STATUS: IMPLEMENTED IN SOURCE — AWAITING GROUPED POSTGRESQL VERIFICATION AND
COORDINATED DEVELOPMENT DEPLOYMENT. No parent closure or completion count change.

## Phase 2: three-owner delivery contract

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelreadme--phase-2-three-owner-delivery-contract"></a>
### Phase 2: three-owner delivery contract

Prepared by LABOS-P2-PRIMARY on 2026-10-16 at the owner's request. This is an
assignment and coordination contract, NOT evidence of completed implementation.
There are exactly three assignments, not three additional phases.

| Assignment | Identity | Exclusive delivery IDs | Brief and working report |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | LABOS-P2-PRIMARY | A6 and A4 downloaded-link reconciliation subset; integration/review | [Primary](WORK_LOG.md#source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_offline_security_resources) |
| 2 | LABOS-P2-HELPER-DOMAIN | B1, B2, B3, B4, B5, B6 | [Domain helper](WORK_LOG.md#source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelhelper_1_domain_workflows) |
| 3 | LABOS-P2-HELPER-CAPABILITIES | A1, A2, A3, A5, remainder of A4; C1–C6 | [Capabilities helper](WORK_LOG.md#source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelhelper_2_assistant_audio_actions) |

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelreadme--owner-directed-reassignment-2026-10-17-supersedes-earlier-ownership"></a>
#### Owner-directed reassignment — 2026-10-17 (supersedes earlier ownership)

Latest owner follow-up: helpers are considered finished; primary and owner now
take over review/polish. No further helper dispatch is active in this task. The
allocation below remains the attribution map for delivered work, not a claim that
all transferred A/C implementation has been completed. Primary's independent
review is recorded in [review checkpoint](WORK_LOG.md#source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_review_2026-10-17).

The owner asked primary to fix Downloads, hand the rest of its implementation to
Helper 2, then review/polish both helpers' work. Exactly three assignments remain.
Primary retains A6 and only the A4 subset needed for completed-link metadata,
downloaded-file replication/availability and the Resources/Downloads mismatch.
Helper 2 now owns implementation of A1/A2/A3/A5 and all other A4 work as well as C.
Primary keeps integration/deployment and final review authority, not duplicate
implementation ownership of those transferred items. The detailed A plan in the
primary brief remains required reading for Helper 2, not cancelled scope.

Active primary file reservation: `backend/src/routes/sync.js` resource pull route,
download worker/route and resource/download adapters/native replication/presentation
paths named in its brief. Helper 2 must request a handoff for overlapping resource,
auth/sync initialization or shared registration changes. Independent implementation
is released in its own report below; no migration/deployment/data reset is implied.
Older statements in this README/briefs assigning all A work to primary are historical
and are overridden here. All other safety, reporting and testing rules still apply.

These are coherent ownership boundaries, not equal estimates of effort. The
primary also owns integration, deployment and independent acceptance review.
Helpers implement functional work within their contracts; they are NOT the
existing LABOS-VISUAL-AGENT, whose Phase 3 visual-only restrictions remain intact.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelreadme--source-of-truth-and-required-reading"></a>
#### Source of truth and required reading

All contributors must read applicable AGENTS.md, this file, their entire brief,
and these documents before changing implementation:

- `docs/audits/PHASE2_DELIVERY_CHECKLIST.md`: controlling scope/status, including
  its approved decisions and newer bounded implementation checkpoints.
- `docs/audits/PHASE2_EVIDENCE.md`: inspect relevant existing evidence; do not
  claim earlier work as your own or interpret historical passes as current passes.
- `docs/audits/PHASE2_OFFLINE_SECURITY_AND_ACCEPTANCE.md`.
- `docs/audits/PHASE2_3_SCOPE_ADDITIONS_2026-10-09.md` and relevant sections of
  `docs/audits/THREE_PHASE_REMAINING_WORK_PLAN.md`.
- `docs/audits/OFFLINE_FIRST_WRITE_PATH_AUDIT.md` for the affected write paths.

The controlling checklist currently retains 18 open closure items, with baseline
12 PARTIAL and 6 PLANNED; this allocation does not close or reset any of them.
Existing foundations must be reused. No promise moves to Phase 3 merely because
it is difficult. Only primary updates authoritative status/evidence after review.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelreadme--baseline-ownership-and-collision-protocol"></a>
#### Baseline, ownership and collision protocol

Initial observed checkout: `C:/Users/balik/Iven/lab-inventory-app`, branch `main`,
HEAD `0a5deb471069dbd5ab0174f4dc0795f28b954cff`. Initially dirty:
`desktop/src/api/mediaDownloads.ts`, `desktop/src/pages/DownloadsPage.tsx`,
`docs/audits/OFFLINE_FIRST_WRITE_PATH_AUDIT.md`,
`docs/audits/PHASE2_DELIVERY_CHECKLIST.md`, `docs/audits/PHASE2_EVIDENCE.md`.
This is a snapshot, not ownership permission: record fresh status before work.

1. Record unique UTC run ID, identity, checkout, branch/HEAD, initial dirty paths,
   and exact intended file list in your own report. Preserve pre-existing hunks.
2. Allowed feature paths are listed in each brief. A path not explicitly allowed
   is READ-ONLY until primary grants a named, bounded exception in your report.
3. Central files are integration-owned even when your feature needs them:
   `desktop/src-tauri/src/{main.rs,local_db.rs,local_auth.rs,native_authorization.rs}`,
   `desktop/src/api/{sync.ts,sync-receipts.ts,auth.ts,http.ts,local-backend.ts,permissions.ts}`,
   `backend/src/routes/{sync.js,auth.js}`, shared auth/permission middleware,
   shared receipt/UUID/protocol utilities, application bootstrap/router, global
   styles, dependency manifests/lockfiles, Tauri capabilities/CSP/build configuration,
   migration runners, Docker/deployment files, and authoritative audit ledgers.
4. Helpers may propose new domain modules and additive migration SQL in their
   report, but ask for exact new paths/migration IDs before creating them. Do not
   edit historical migrations or apply schema changes to shared databases.
5. For a shared hook/command/route/migration registration, supply an integration
   request with exact symbols, DTOs, permissions, version rules, transaction
   boundaries, error cases and proposed patch. Primary reviews and applies it.
   Do not create fake local shims, alternate sync engines or permissive stubs.
6. Do not edit another contributor's brief/report. Do not commit, stash, reset,
   clean, checkout over edits or reformat unrelated files. Do not branch from an
   incomplete HEAD and assume uncommitted prerequisites came with it.
7. Phase 3 visual work may overlap feature files. Preserve it; if concurrent work
   is active, get a file handoff first. Functional permission here does not permit
   a wholesale redesign or undoing the owner's compact/centered-modal direction.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelreadme--dependency-handshake-not-extra-assignments"></a>
#### Dependency handshake (not extra assignments)

- Domain helper publishes canonical B1 custody/source quantities and B3/B4
  requirement/lifecycle contracts. B2 depends on B1; B4 depends on B1/B3.
- Capabilities helper publishes C1 proposal schemas and required acceptance
  operations. C2 is blocked on primary-reviewed A1 and B3/B4 contracts: no
  assistant-only SQL/write bypass to unblock it. Independent C1/C3/C5 work proceeds.
- C4 microphone/transcription integrates with C3 audio ownership, not a second
  competing coordinator. C6 consumes A1 authorization, never rewrites it.
- Domain history/projections are owned by helper 1, users/settings views by helper
  2, overview freshness and shared authorization by primary. Shared integration
  requests must name which side produces and consumes the contract.
- A4 resource/video lifecycle hooks needed by C3 are applied by primary after
  helper 2 supplies the focus API. No helper edits the active Resources/Downloads
  correction. Primary owns all cross-domain acceptance and conflict resolution.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelreadme--non-negotiable-behavior-and-data-safety"></a>
#### Non-negotiable behavior and data safety

- Desktop domain writes: authorized native operation -> atomic SQLite state plus
  immutable outbox event -> idempotent server apply -> reconciled local receipt.
  Binary data belongs in managed local storage with durable metadata/transfer
  intentions, not giant SQLite blobs. Native failure must not trigger HTTP writes.
- Retain stable entity/event IDs, UUID normalization, author/device identity,
  expected versions, dependency ordering and server permission rechecks.
- Reads use authorized local data with honest completeness/freshness. Metadata
  is not verified file bytes; queued intent is not accepted global execution.
- Preserve data, authored files, pending events and failed-work recovery. No
  database reset/reseed, broad deletion, cache wipe or silent reattribution.
- No new credentials/secrets in reports; no weakening leases, visibility, CSP or
  authorization for convenience. No live paid AI/transcription calls or audio
  recording without the needed explicit user consent/configuration.
- Helpers do not restart the desktop, stop Docker, migrate shared databases,
  deploy APIs or mutate user records. Primary coordinates those windows and
  obtains saved-edit confirmation before closing the desktop.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelreadme--testing-cadence-and-truthful-reporting"></a>
#### Testing cadence and truthful reporting

Implement coherent batches, retaining quick compile/type checks and critical
auth/stock/idempotency/rollback tests. Build the full acceptance cases as you work.
At phase end, collect independent failures before grouped fixes and full rerun;
mark dependent tests BLOCKED rather than pretending to execute them. Stop affected
work immediately for data-loss, corruption or unauthorized-access risks.

Database acceptance uses the existing actual PostgreSQL in a primary-coordinated
window with uniquely named fixtures and narrowly scoped cleanup. Helpers may use
unit doubles to test logic but must label them; they are not database acceptance.
Offline acceptance must use actual Tauri, stop the real LabOS API (not PostgreSQL
or volumes), exercise refresh/cold restart, then reconnect. Include hung transport,
two clients/accounts, lost ACK/replay, permissions/revocation and preserved rejected
work where applicable. Primary owns service restoration and combined deployment.

Each helper appends reports ONLY in its assigned Markdown file. For each finding:

```text
REPORTER / RUN ID / UTC DATE:
DELIVERY ID / BOUNDED SUBCHECK:
MODULE:
FILE (exact path and symbols):
CURRENT WRITE PATH (or READ PATH for read-only findings):
WHY IT BYPASSES OFFLINE-FIRST (or N/A with reason):
RISK:
RECOMMENDED CHANGE:
ACTUAL CHANGE MADE (NONE if audit only; distinguish inherited changes):
VERIFICATION (command, environment, build/commit, exit code, result, limitations):
STATUS (CODE REMAINING / DEPENDENCY / IMPLEMENTED - AWAITING VERIFICATION):
FILES CHANGED / MIGRATION EFFECTS / FIXTURE CLEANUP:
INTEGRATION REQUESTS / REMAINING WORK:
```

Use PASS / FAIL / BLOCKED / NOT RUN for individual checks. Preserve dated history;
append superseding corrections rather than erase an earlier failure. A code diff,
green build, test plan or approval is not deployed/native/PostgreSQL verification.
Helpers can say READY FOR PRIMARY REVIEW, never VERIFIED CLOSED or Phase 2 done.

Primary reviews exact diffs, business/permission invariants, dependency effects,
tests and deployed behavior. Only primary fills each report's PRIMARY REVIEW
section and promotes accepted evidence into the authoritative checklist/ledger.
Unresolved authority/policy questions require a precise request with pros/cons;
do not reopen the owner's already approved choices just to defer implementation.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_offline_security_resources--immediate-defect-server-completed-jobs-still-shown-as-link-only-resources"></a>

Owner evidence dated 2026-10-16: Downloads shows two completed server jobs
(Facebook reel and YouTube), both with unverified PC copies, while the matching
Resources cards still say LINK ONLY. Attach to A6/A4, not a new delivery ID.

Investigation sequence:

1. Correlate resource UUID, job UUID, account/project scope and revision across
   actual PostgreSQL, worker results, download snapshot, local resource row and
   file replication manifest. Inspect read-only first; do not log auth secrets.
2. Trace completion's transaction: which canonical resource fields, revision,
   thumbnail and binary identity are committed, and what makes them pull-visible?
3. Trace the sync/pull merge: revision/cursor handling, pending-write protection,
   resource type/filename/local-path fields and job-resource identity normalization.
4. Trace both page selectors and local binary validation. Distinguish an old job
   whose file no longer matches the current resource from a current completion.
5. Fix the evidenced source of divergence using the existing architecture. Do
   not merely replace LINK ONLY with Downloaded based on any historical job.
6. Cover automatic intake -> scheduling -> server completion -> resource update
   -> PC replication -> verified playback, plus retry/restart, stale jobs, pending
   edits, cancel/delete races and real outage. Preserve thumbnail continuity.

Correct states must distinguish server copy, PC transfer pending/failed and verified
PC copy. Do not introduce a Resources queue-download button, auto-schedule links
on list reads, duplicate resources, wipe SQLite, or force re-download to hide this.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelhelper_2_assistant_audio_actions--c3-shared-device-audio-focus-independent-first-candidate"></a>
##### C3 — shared device audio focus (independent first candidate)

- Trace MusicPlayer/MusicDock/MusicMiniPlayer, assistant/notebook TTS and resource
  video/audio lifecycles. Replace competing unowned pause/resume semantics with
  one device-local coordinator; do not create one manager per component.
- Owner tokens and generation checks control acquire/release/preemption. Stale
  completion cannot release a newer owner or restart music over lab media/TTS.
- Preserve playback position and chosen volume. Track automatic suspension
  separately from explicit manual pause/stop, track change, close and account switch.
- Make transitions cancellable; safely release on navigation, playback rejection,
  device errors and cancellation. Microphone focus suppresses competing audio/TTS.
- Publish the focus API and required resource-player hooks to primary for A4.
  No direct changes to Resources/Downloads/native file delivery.
- Retain device-local music/takeover preferences. Audible polish/hardware tuning
  belongs to Phase 3; functional ownership and safe resume belong here.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelhelper_2_assistant_audio_actions--c1-persistent-authorized-planning-proposals"></a>
##### C1 — persistent, authorized planning proposals

- Inspect current assistant/context handling and existing draft/message persistence.
  Allowlist project plans, tasks and experiment protocols; schema validation is a
  code boundary, not merely a prompt instruction or a changed Read-only badge.
- Store editable proposal versions, stable conversation/message/request/proposal
  IDs, context provenance and author identity in account-scoped local persistence.
  Saved drafts remain usable offline; model generation remains online/provider-bound.
- Separate transport retry/uncertain-result reconciliation from deliberate
  regeneration. Keep earlier versions and avoid duplicate messages/entities.
- Context selection does not grant write permission. Retrieved instructions cannot
  add tools or authorize effects. Respect project/record visibility at every layer.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelhelper_2_assistant_audio_actions--c2-human-approval-after-reviewed-a1-and-b3b4-contracts"></a>
##### C2 — human approval, after reviewed A1 and B3/B4 contracts

- Obtain the domain helper's canonical graph/lifecycle API and primary's permission
  integration before wiring acceptance. Do not implement assistant-specific SQL
  writes or weaken domain validation to make a draft succeed.
- Explicit human selection/review/edit/acceptance invokes ordinary native domain
  transactions and outbox, with stable acceptance identity and idempotent server
  graph apply. Recheck permissions/scope/revisions at acceptance and reconciliation.
- Attribute records to the human approver with AI provenance. Bundles are atomic
  or explicitly independently accepted sub-bundles, never secretly partial success.
- Hard exclusions: stock issue/consumption/salvage/adjustment, reservation fulfillment,
  spending/orders, user/grant changes, destructive deletes, fabricated experimental
  results or automatic completion of physical work. Proposed materials are demand,
  not stock execution. Saved proposals cannot auto-accept on replay or reconnect.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelhelper_2_assistant_audio_actions--c4-consented-server-transcription-after-c3"></a>

- User starts/stops/cancels recording. Disclose processing destination/retention

- Transcript is editable and reviewed before send; cancellation/retry/account

- Coordinate microphone/TTS/music ownership through C3. Show unavailable/denied/

- No live paid service test, new provider/account or dependency installation without

- Server rechecks permissions and idempotency. Pending/offline intention is not

- Audio overlap, rapid replacement, stale release, user pause/stop/mute/track
  change, account switch, failed playback and mic denial/cancel; deterministic
  coordinator tests plus scheduled actual-device checks (not the same evidence).
- Proposal validation, context-off/restricted context, malicious retrieved text,
  account isolation, offline draft persistence, retries versus regeneration.
- Double acceptance, lost ACK, revoked permission, version conflict, malformed
  graph/rollback and zero stock/finance/fulfillment effects. Actual PostgreSQL
  acceptance uses primary-coordinated fixtures and reviewed B3/B4 entry points.
- Transcription consent, explicit stop/cancel, stale result suppression, editable
  transcript, no auto-send, provider errors/timeouts and no hidden audio retention.
- Automation restart/replay/uncertain result, permissions, and honest pending state.
- Cached users/settings offline reload, account switch and denied/expired access;
  ordinary preference retry; no plaintext credential queues or offline grants.

Continue independent C1/C3/C5 work while C2 awaits contracts; do not claim blocked
integration is implemented. Follow coherent-batch then phase-end full acceptance
cadence. Ask only genuinely unresolved choices with pros/cons; server-first voice
and human-only planning acceptance are already approved.

##### LABOS-P2-HELPER-CAPABILITIES / RUN-20261017-001 / 2026-10-17T16:30:00Z

**DELIVERY ID / BOUNDED SUBCHECK:** C3 — shared device audio focus (initial audit and batch proposal)

**MODULE:** Desktop audio coordination

**FILE (exact path and symbols):**
- `desktop/src/components/MusicPlayer.tsx` (lines 147-166): Custom event listeners for `labos:pause-music`/`labos:resume-music`, audio element ref, `autoPause` prop, `resumeAfterPause` ref
- `desktop/src/components/MusicDock.tsx` (line 32): Same custom event pattern, separate audio element ref, `autoPause` prop, `resumeAfterPause` ref
- `desktop/src/components/MusicMiniPlayer.tsx` (lines 21-44): Polls DOM for audio element every 250ms, no direct ownership, coordinates via DOM queries
- `desktop/src/components/AssistantChat.tsx` (line 71): Dispatches `labos:pause-music`/`labos:resume-music` events for TTS, uses `window.speechSynthesis.cancel()`
- `desktop/src/pages/NotebookPage.tsx` (lines 149-194): Uses `window.speechSynthesis` for read-aloud, does NOT dispatch pause/resume events
- `desktop/src/components/ResourceViewerModal.tsx` (lines 34-35): Native `<video>` and `<audio>` elements with `controls`, no coordination with music/TTS
- `desktop/src/hooks/useMusicDefaults.ts`: Device-local volume preference from daily preferences

**CURRENT WRITE PATH (or READ PATH for read-only findings):** READ-ONLY AUDIT

**WHY IT BYPASSES OFFLINE-FIRST (or N/A with reason):** N/A - audit only

**RISK:**
1. **Competing unowned audio sources:** Three separate music components (MusicPlayer, MusicDock, MusicMiniPlayer) each manage their own audio element with independent state. They coordinate only via loose custom events (`labos:pause-music`/`labos:resume-music`) with no ownership validation.
2. **No owner token system:** TTS in AssistantChat dispatches pause/resume events, but TTS in NotebookPage does not. Resource video/audio elements have no coordination at all. A newer owner cannot be distinguished from a stale completion callback.
3. **Race conditions in MusicMiniPlayer:** Polls DOM every 250ms to sync state, clicks buttons via DOM queries. This is fragile and can cause state drift.
4. **No automatic suspension tracking:** `resumeAfterPause` ref tracks whether music should resume, but doesn't distinguish between automatic suspension (TTS, navigation) vs explicit manual pause/stop, track change, close, or account switch.
5. **No cancellable transitions:** If TTS is interrupted by navigation or device error, the resume event may fire after the component unmounts, potentially causing issues.
6. **No microphone focus coordination:** Voice dictation in NotebookPage does not suppress competing audio/TTS. Microphone access could conflict with music playback.

**RECOMMENDED CHANGE:**
Implement C3 (shared device audio focus) as the first independent batch:

1. **Create a device-local audio focus coordinator** (`desktop/src/hooks/useAudioFocus.ts` or `desktop/src/lib/audioFocus.ts`):
   - Single device-local coordinator (not one per component)
   - Owner token system with generation checks
   - Ownership types: `music`, `tts`, `video`, `microphone`
   - Priority ordering: microphone > TTS > video > music
   - Acquire/release/preemption APIs with owner validation
   - Stale completion cannot release a newer owner

2. **Track suspension reasons separately:**
   - `automatic` (TTS, navigation, preemption)
   - `manual` (user pause/stop)
   - `track_change`, `close`, `account_switch`
   - Preserve resume intent only for automatic suspension

3. **Preserve playback state:**
   - Current position (audio.currentTime)
   - Chosen volume (from useMusicDefaults)
   - Track metadata (id, name, artwork)

4. **Make transitions cancellable:**
   - Safely release on navigation (React unmount)
   - Safely release on playback rejection (audio.play() failure)
   - Safely release on device errors (audio.onerror)
   - Safely release on cancellation (user abort)

5. **Microphone focus:**
   - Microphone ownership suppresses all other audio/TTS
   - Voice dictation in NotebookPage should acquire microphone focus
   - Release microphone focus on dictation stop/error

6. **Publish focus API for A4:**
   - Export coordinator functions for resource-player hooks
   - Document required hooks for video/audio playback
   - No direct changes to Resources/Downloads/native file delivery

7. **Retain device-local preferences:**
   - Music volume and takeover preference remain device-local
   - Use existing `useMusicDefaults` hook
   - Audible polish/hardware tuning deferred to Phase 3

**ACTUAL CHANGE MADE:** NONE (audit only)

**VERIFICATION:** READ-ONLY AUDIT - no changes made. Verified existing patterns via code search and file reading.

**STATUS:** CODE REMAINING - proposing C3 as first independent batch, awaiting primary approval of file list and exact batch release.

**FILES CHANGED / MIGRATION EFFECTS / FIXTURE CLEANUP:** NONE

**INTEGRATION REQUESTS / REMAINING WORK:**
1. **Primary approval needed:** Exact file list for C3 implementation batch, including:
   - New audio focus coordinator module path (proposal: `desktop/src/lib/audioFocus.ts`)
   - Confirmation that allowed paths in brief cover this new module
   - Confirmation that resource-player hooks for A4 are within ownership envelope

2. **A4 dependency:** After focus API is published, primary will apply hooks to Resources/Downloads. Helper does not edit those files directly.

3. **Test plan for C3 (pending approval):**
   - Audio overlap scenarios (music + TTS, music + video, TTS + video)
   - Rapid replacement (TTS starts while music playing, then video starts)
   - Stale release (old TTS completion after new owner acquired)
   - User pause/stop/mute/track change behavior
   - Account switch (ensure music state is handled correctly)
   - Failed playback (audio.play() rejection)
   - Mic denial/cancel (microphone focus errors)
   - Deterministic coordinator tests (unit tests)
   - Scheduled actual-device checks (real Tauri desktop)

4. **Bounded first batch:** C3 is independent and can proceed without waiting for C1, C2, C4, C5, or C6. Other C items can proceed in parallel where possible.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelhelper_1_domain_workflows--detailed-work-plan"></a>
#### Detailed work plan

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelhelper_1_domain_workflows--b1-quantity-aware-custody-first-dependency-contract"></a>
##### B1 — quantity-aware custody (first dependency contract)

- Map current quantity, stock movement, reservation fulfillment, assigned_to and
  assignee permissions. Record what each quantity actually means before migration.
- Separate responsibility assignment from physical issue. Support quantity-first
  split issues, recipient distinct from actor, transfers, partial return/use/loss/
  damage, outstanding balances, units and optional individual serial tracking.
- Retain source issue/movement and project/task/experiment/reservation references.
  Consuming issued stock settles custody without subtracting storeroom stock again.
  A direct storeroom consumption is a separate explicit path.
- Local state and immutable intent commit together. Global stock allocation may
  remain provisional offline; server locks/version checks reject over-allocation,
  over-settlement and duplicate postings without deleting authored evidence.
- Use explicit stock-handling permissions through primary-reviewed permission
  registration. Do not convert old whole-record assignments into physical issues.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelhelper_1_domain_workflows--b3-then-b4-canonical-demand-and-interconnected-project-lifecycle"></a>
##### B3 then B4 — canonical demand and interconnected project lifecycle

- Map project, BOM/revision, canonical requirement, reservations, tasks,
  experiments, canvas, notes/resources and financial evidence IDs/write paths.
- Tasks/experiments reference one canonical requirement unless a human creates
  explicit extra demand. Shared references must not multiply quantities.
- Audit remaining create/update/repeat/revision paths for HTTP fallback, missing
  outbox, UUID drift, duplicate retry and partial bundle acceptance.
- Canvas references do not own the referenced domain records. Removing a visual
  node must not silently delete stock/tasks/experiments or duplicate demand.
- Finish local review/reservation/history/context and durable decision intentions.
  Distinguish local pending submission from globally accepted reservation/approval.
- Cancellation releases only unused reservations; issued stock remains outstanding
  until explicit return/consumption/loss. Preserve results/audit/finance history.
  Unsettled projects may archive, but cannot claim fully settled closure.
- Task/experiment completion never fabricates results or automatically consumes
  physical stock. Publish the graph/lifecycle command contract for helper 2's C2.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelhelper_1_domain_workflows--b2-salvage-after-b1-source-ledger"></a>
##### B2 — salvage, after B1 source ledger

- Distinguish unused-stock return, equipment return, consumed-component recovery,
  disassembly into other outputs and scrap. Preserve original source provenance.
- Recovered material is quarantined until authorized inspection/release. Validate
  units/conversions/source quantities and concurrent/replayed recovery limits.
- Preserve historical consumption/cost. Keep reviewed recovery value separate
  from carrying value, replacement value, repair expense and cash. Unknown value
  stays unknown. No automatic purchase, cash refund or project expense credit.
- Legacy unknown provenance requires explicit attestation, not invented movements;
  a deleted item must not be silently resurrected.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelhelper_1_domain_workflows--b5-and-b6-independent-financeimport-and-inventory-completeness"></a>
##### B5 and B6 — independent finance/import and inventory completeness

- Inspect finance/purchase templates, export, preview/import and remaining writes.
  Reuse transactional inventory-import patterns; deterministic stable IDs,
  expected versions, permissions and all-or-nothing local/outbox/server effects.
- Finish authorized assignee directory, field/assignment history, storage/location
  relationships, local inventory export/templates and workbook parser boundaries.
- Preserve existing CRUD/bulk/movement/import/history fixes. Never route a failed
  native write to the server or treat an incomplete snapshot as empty history.
- Legacy-event recovery must preserve authorship and immutable original evidence;
  shared recovery policy/engine changes go to primary under A2, not a new bypass.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelhelper_1_domain_workflows--ownership-envelope-after-named-batch-release"></a>

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelhelper_1_domain_workflows--required-verification-package"></a>
#### Required verification package

- Responsibility-only change produces no stock movement or financial effect.
- Split issue, partial return/use/transfer/loss, optional serials, wrong units,
  double-click/lost ACK, two-client over-issue/over-return and transaction rollback.
- Shared task/experiment requirement counted once; explicit extra demand counted;
  revisions/cancellation/archival retain custody and historical evidence.
- Salvage quarantine, inspection, source limits, reviewed/unknown value, repeated
  recovery and unchanged historical expenses; financial permission denial.
- Finance/purchase/import malformed input, duplicates, partial validation failure,
  replay, version conflict and permission denial leave atomic state.
- Actual PostgreSQL/reconnect and actual Tauri API-stopped/cold-restart cases
  prepared for primary's coordinated acceptance window, not claimed via doubles.

Independent B5/B6 or B3 projection work can proceed while B2/B4 await B1. Stop and
report genuinely new policy decisions with pros/cons, not guesses. Do not reopen
the approved quantity-first, canonical-demand or reviewed-salvage policies.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelhelper_1_domain_workflows--finding-b11-quantity-aware-custody-ledger-split-issues-balances-and-storeroom-double-deduction"></a>
###### Finding B1.1 — Quantity-aware custody ledger, split issues, balances, and storeroom double-deduction

```text
REPORTER / RUN ID / UTC DATE: LABOS-P2-HELPER-DOMAIN / RUN-20261016-B-AUDIT-01 / 2026-10-16
DELIVERY ID / BOUNDED SUBCHECK: B1 / Quantity custody ledger and optional serials
MODULE: Inventory & Custody
FILE (exact path and symbols):
  desktop/src-tauri/src/local_inventory.rs (save_movement, list_movements, cache_movements, LocalMovementWriteInput)
  desktop/src/api/local-inventory.ts (createLocalItemMovement, getLocalItemMovements, cacheLocalItemMovements)
  desktop/src/api/items.ts (createItemMovement, getItemMovements, ItemMovement, MovementType)
  backend/src/inventory-apply.js (applyMovement, MOVEMENT_TYPES, INCOMING, OUTGOING)
  backend/src/routes/items.js (POST /:id/movements, GET /:id/movements)
  backend/src/schema.sql (items, item_movements)
CURRENT WRITE PATH (or READ PATH for read-only findings):
  1. Desktop physical movement: createLocalItemMovement() checks INCOMING/OUTGOING sets, decrements or increments local[index].current_quantity, saves item snapshot + item_movement record to SQLite, queues sync_outbox with entity_type='item_movement', and pushes to server.
  2. Responsibility assignment: updateLocalInventoryItem() / ItemDetailPage.tsx sets item.assigned_to to a user UUID. This is a whole-item attribute edit; it writes no movement, records no quantity, and creates no custody balance.
  3. Reservation fulfillment: backend/src/routes/projects.js POST /:id/reservations/:reservationId/fulfill writes an item_movements row with movement_type='consume' and decrements items.current_quantity.
WHY IT BYPASSES OFFLINE-FIRST (or N/A with reason):
  N/A for the base inventory movement write (which is local-first SQLite + outbox). However, custody is fundamentally missing:
  1. There is NO custody entity, table, or ledger in SQLite or PostgreSQL.
  2. When stock is "checked out" via checkout movement, items.current_quantity is decremented, but no record of who holds the physical stock or what remains outstanding is created.
  3. If a project task, experiment, or user subsequently records consumption of checked-out stock, a standard consume movement decrements items.current_quantity a SECOND time from storeroom stock, causing physical stock undercounting.
  4. Assigned responsibility (items.assigned_to) assigns the entire record to one user regardless of current_quantity, with no recipient distinct from actor, no split issue support, and no balance tracking.
RISK:
  Severe inventory double-counting/under-counting: checking out stock and then recording its consumption in a project double-deducts physical inventory. High risk of lost or untraceable equipment/tools/materials because checkout creates no outstanding returnable balance. Whole-item assigned_to misrepresents pooled/bulk stock (e.g. 500 resistors assigned to one person).
RECOMMENDED CHANGE:
  1. Implement an explicit custody ledger (e.g. item_custody_records) tracking: custody_id, item_id, source_movement_id, project_id, task_id, experiment_id, reservation_id, recipient_id, actor_id, initial_quantity, outstanding_quantity, unit, status ('issued','partially_settled','settled'), serial_number (optional), issued_at, settled_at.
  2. Differentiate movement actions:
     - Issue to custody (checkout / issue): storeroom current_quantity decrements; an open custody record is created with outstanding_quantity = issue_quantity.
     - Settle custody by consumption: settles outstanding_quantity on the custody record WITHOUT subtracting storeroom current_quantity again.
     - Direct storeroom consumption: explicitly deducts from storeroom current_quantity when material was never checked out to custody.
     - Settle custody by return: increases storeroom current_quantity and decreases custody outstanding_quantity.
     - Settle custody by damage/loss: records damage/loss on custody outstanding_quantity WITHOUT altering storeroom current_quantity.
     - Custody transfer: transfers outstanding custody balance from recipient A to recipient B.
  3. Retain existing items.assigned_to as administrative responsibility only; never auto-convert assigned_to into physical custody.
ACTUAL CHANGE MADE (NONE if audit only; distinguish inherited changes):
  NONE (Read-only audit).
VERIFICATION (command, environment, build/commit, exit code, result, limitations):
  - Verified existing inventory tests pass: `node --test desktop/src/api/inventory-boundaries.test.mjs desktop/src/api/inventory-http.test.mjs desktop/src/api/excel.test.mjs` (22/22 passed).
  - Verified cargo unit tests in `desktop/src-tauri` pass for inventory and project permissions.
  - Limitations: Code modifications blocked until Primary approves batch release.
STATUS: CODE REMAINING
FILES CHANGED / MIGRATION EFFECTS / FIXTURE CLEANUP:
  FILES CHANGED: None.
  MIGRATION EFFECTS: Proposed additive migration for item_custody_records + custody settlement foreign keys.
  FIXTURE CLEANUP: None.
INTEGRATION REQUESTS / REMAINING WORK:
  Request Primary to release Batch 1 file ownership for: `desktop/src-tauri/src/local_inventory.rs`, `desktop/src/api/items.ts`, `desktop/src/api/local-inventory.ts`, `backend/src/inventory-apply.js`, `backend/src/inventory-sync.js`, and additive custody migration.
```

###### Finding B3.1 — Canonical demand and interconnected project lifecycle (BOM, requirements, tasks, experiments, canvas)

```text
REPORTER / RUN ID / UTC DATE: LABOS-P2-HELPER-DOMAIN / RUN-20261016-B-AUDIT-01 / 2026-10-16
DELIVERY ID / BOUNDED SUBCHECK: B3 / Connected requirements/BOM/tasks/experiments/canvas and remaining local mutations
MODULE: Projects & Work Lifecycle
FILE (exact path and symbols):
  desktop/src-tauri/src/local_projects.rs (create_local_resource_requirement, update_local_resource_requirement, delete_local_resource_requirement, get_local_resource_requirements, create_local_project_bom, create_local_project_task, create_local_project_experiment, create_local_project_block, delete_local_project_block)
  desktop/src/api/projects.ts (getProjectRequirements, createProjectRequirement, getProjectBom, createProjectBomItem, repeatProjectExperiment, linkTaskExperiment)
  desktop/src/api/canvas.ts (createBlock, deleteBlock, createConnector, deleteConnector)
  desktop/src/components/ProjectCanvas.tsx (ProjectCanvas, deleteBlockMutation)
  backend/src/routes/projects.js (repeatProjectExperiment POST /:id/experiments/:experimentId/repeat)
  backend/src/routes/project-workspace.js (POST /:id/tasks, POST /:id/experiments)
  backend/src/routes/sync.js (PROJECT_ENTITY_CONFIG, applyProjectEntity)
CURRENT WRITE PATH (or READ PATH for read-only findings):
  1. Requirements: local_projects.rs manages requirements in projects_state and queues project_resource_requirement outbox events.
  2. BOM: local_projects.rs manages bom items in projects_state and queues project_bom outbox events.
  3. Tasks & Experiments: local_projects.rs manages tasks and experiments in projects_state and queues project_task / project_experiment outbox events.
  4. Experiment repeat: desktop/src/api/projects.ts repeatProjectExperiment() issues direct HTTP POST to /projects/:id/experiments/:experimentId/repeat. In offline mode on Tauri, this fails immediately.
  5. Canvas: ProjectCanvas and canvas.ts write blocks/connectors via local_projects.rs commands.
WHY IT BYPASSES OFFLINE-FIRST (or N/A with reason):
  1. Experiment repeat: Bypasses offline-first via direct HTTP POST; lacks local Tauri command, SQLite persistence, and outbox event.
  2. Disconnected demand: project_bom_items and project_resource_requirements exist as separate disjoint entities without canonical requirement linkage.
  3. Tasks and experiments have NO requirement_id or bom_item_id foreign keys or linkage in their schema or DTOs. When tasks and experiments need the same material, demand cannot be canonically referenced and risks being multiplied.
  4. Canvas blocks reference resources (resource_id) or free text, but deleting a canvas block in delete_local_project_block() cascades connector deletion without clear domain reference safety checks.
RISK:
  - Inability to repeat experiments offline.
  - Multiplied demand: if a BOM item requires 5 motors, and Task 1 and Experiment 1 both specify 5 motors, total demand is computed as 15 rather than 5, leading to false shortage alerts or over-ordering.
  - Deleting visual canvas blocks risks orphaned or accidentally disconnected project attachments if ownership semantics are blurred.
RECOMMENDED CHANGE:
  1. Unify canonical demand: Establish project_resource_requirements as the canonical demand record. Allow project_bom_items to reference or project a canonical requirement.
  2. Add optional requirement_id to project_tasks and project_experiments so work items reference the canonical requirement rather than creating independent unlinked demand.
  3. Implement repeat_local_project_experiment in local_projects.rs and desktop/src/api/projects.ts using atomic SQLite state + outbox intent.
  4. Formalize canvas invariant: Canvas visual nodes are projections/references and NEVER own or delete underlying domain items, stock, tasks, or experiments.
```

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelhelper_1_domain_workflows--finding-b41-project-review-reservations-cancellationarchival-propagation-and-explicit-settlement"></a>
###### Finding B4.1 — Project review, reservations, cancellation/archival propagation, and explicit settlement

```text
REPORTER / RUN ID / UTC DATE: LABOS-P2-HELPER-DOMAIN / RUN-20261016-B-AUDIT-01 / 2026-10-16
DELIVERY ID / BOUNDED SUBCHECK: B4 / Cancellation/closure propagation and settlement
MODULE: Project Lifecycle & Reservations
FILE (exact path and symbols):
  desktop/src/components/ProjectPlanningReview.tsx (ProjectPlanningReview, decideProjectReview)
  desktop/src/components/ProjectReservations.tsx (ProjectReservations, requestProjectReservation, decideProjectReservation, fulfillProjectReservation)
  desktop/src/api/projects.ts (getProjectReview, decideProjectReview, getProjectReservations, requestProjectReservation, decideProjectReservation, fulfillProjectReservation, getReservationReviewQueue)
  desktop/src-tauri/src/local_projects.rs (projects_state, load, save, apply_server_project_pull)
  backend/src/routes/projects.js (GET/POST /:id/review, GET/POST /:id/reservations, POST /:id/reservations/:reservationId/decision, POST /:id/reservations/:reservationId/fulfill, PUT /:id, DELETE /:id)
  backend/src/routes/sync.js (GET /projects/pull, POST /sync/push, PROJECT_ENTITY_CONFIG)
  backend/src/reservation-stock.js (assertReservationStockFloor)
CURRENT WRITE PATH (or READ PATH for read-only findings):
  1. Planning Review: desktop/src/api/projects.ts calls HTTP GET /projects/:id/review and HTTP POST /projects/:id/review. In Tauri, there is NO local review command or offline submission queuing.
  2. Reservations: desktop/src/api/projects.ts calls HTTP GET /projects/:id/reservations, HTTP POST /projects/:id/reservations, HTTP POST /projects/:id/reservations/:reservationId/decision, and HTTP POST /projects/:id/reservations/:reservationId/fulfill.
  3. In local_projects.rs: reservations and review events are NOT stored in projects_state, NOT pulled in apply_server_project_pull(), and NOT queued in sync_outbox.
  4. In backend/src/routes/sync.js: PROJECT_ENTITY_CONFIG omits project_reservation and project_review_event. They cannot be pushed or pulled via sync.
  5. Project Status Transitions: In backend/src/routes/projects.js PUT /:id, a project can be set to 'cancelled' or 'completed' without releasing confirmed reservations or settling issued stock.
WHY IT BYPASSES OFFLINE-FIRST (or N/A with reason):
  Review decisions and reservations are implemented entirely as direct online HTTP requests (`apiFetch`). Desktop users cannot submit reviews, request provisional reservations, view cached reservations, or record reservation decisions while offline. Cancellation/closure does not automatically release unconsumed reservations or check custody balances.
RISK:
  - Complete loss of reservation and review functionality when working disconnected.
  - Stale or orphaned reservations: cancelling a project leaves confirmed reservations active against items, permanently locking inventory from being reserved by other projects.
  - Incomplete closure: projects can be marked "completed" or archived while issued physical stock remains unaccounted for in outstanding custody balances.
RECOMMENDED CHANGE:
  1. Add local reservation requests and review submissions to `local_projects.rs`: local state reflects provisional submission / pending review, and queues outbox changes. Global confirmation remains distinct from local provisional intent.
  2. Register project_reservation and project_review_event in backend sync push/pull.
  3. Cancellation propagation: When project status transitions to 'cancelled', automatically release unused (unfulfilled) reservations. Outstanding issued stock remains in custody until explicitly returned, consumed, or reported lost/damaged.
  4. Archival and settlement: Disallow marking a project fully settled if outstanding custody balances remain. Allow archiving with status 'unsettled_archived' if physical reconciliation is incomplete, but never claim fully settled closure.
  5. Task/experiment completion: Explicitly enforce that marking a task 'done' or experiment 'completed' never automatically deducts stock or fabricates physical results.
ACTUAL CHANGE MADE (NONE if audit only; distinguish inherited changes):
  NONE (Read-only audit).
VERIFICATION (command, environment, build/commit, exit code, result, limitations):

  - Limitations: Read-only audit; implementation awaits primary batch release.
```

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelhelper_1_domain_workflows--finding-b21-quarantined-salvage-condition-inspection-reviewed-valuation-and-source-provenance"></a>
###### Finding B2.1 — Quarantined salvage, condition inspection, reviewed valuation, and source provenance

```text
REPORTER / RUN ID / UTC DATE: LABOS-P2-HELPER-DOMAIN / RUN-20261016-B-AUDIT-01 / 2026-10-16
DELIVERY ID / BOUNDED SUBCHECK: B2 / Quarantined salvage, inspection and reviewed recovery valuation
MODULE: Inventory Salvage & Recovery
FILE (exact path and symbols):
  backend/src/migrations/20260924_inventory_acquisition.sql (acquisition_method, acquisition_source, acquisition_notes)
  backend/src/inventory-apply.js (applyMovement, INCOMING set: receive, return, repair_in)
  desktop/src/components/InventoryMovementPanel.tsx (InventoryMovementPanel, MovementType 'return')
  desktop/src/components/AddItemModal.tsx (acquisition_method options)
  desktop/src-tauri/src/local_inventory.rs (save_movement, ensure_movement_schema)
  backend/src/schema.sql (items.status: 'available', 'in_use', 'damaged', 'needs_repair', 'needs_replacement', 'low_stock', 'retired')
CURRENT WRITE PATH (or READ PATH for read-only findings):
  1. Currently, salvage is handled only at item creation via AddItemModal setting acquisition_method='salvaged', or via standard return movement in InventoryMovementPanel.
  2. When an item movement of type return is posted, the item's current_quantity is immediately added back to available storeroom stock.
  3. There is no quarantine status or inspection stage; returned/salvaged material is immediately marked usable.
  4. There is no link between recovered parts and the source project issue/consumption, no support for disassembly into multiple output items, and no reviewed recovery valuation mechanism.
WHY IT BYPASSES OFFLINE-FIRST (or N/A with reason):
  N/A for the basic movement write path, but the entire domain workflow for traceable salvage and quarantine inspection is missing:
  1. Recovered stock is not quarantined; it is immediately exposed as available for checkout/reservation without authorized inspection.
  2. Salvage value is unmanaged: historical project expenses are not connected, and there is no ledger separating reviewed recovery value from carrying value, replacement cost, or repair expense.
  3. Disassembly of an assembly into constituent parts has no transactional representation.
RISK:
  - Safety/quality hazard: uninspected, damaged, or contaminated components recovered from teardowns immediately appear in storeroom inventory as available stock.
  - Accounting distortion: recovering components could cause double-credit or invent phantom purchase transactions if financial journals automatically credit project expense.
  - Loss of provenance: salvaged items lose traceability to original source projects, lots, or consumption events.
RECOMMENDED CHANGE:
  1. Implement quarantine status ('quarantined') for salvaged/recovered components. Recovered material enters quarantine upon return/recovery and cannot be reserved or issued until an authorized user completes an inspection release.
  2. Link recovery to source: each salvage/recovery record references source project_id, source custody_id or consumption movement_id, recovered_by, condition, inspection_notes, and destination location.
  3. Support disassembly: allow one source assembly to produce multiple inspected component items with distinct canonical UUIDs and explicit quantities/units.
  4. Enforce reviewed valuation policy: separate reviewed recovery value from historical carrying cost, replacement cost, and repair expenses. Never generate automated purchase transactions, cash refunds, or project expense credits.
ACTUAL CHANGE MADE (NONE if audit only; distinguish inherited changes):
  NONE (Read-only audit).
VERIFICATION (command, environment, build/commit, exit code, result, limitations):
  - Audited backend/src/inventory-apply.js, 20260924_inventory_acquisition.sql, and AddItemModal.tsx.
  - Limitations: Read-only audit; implementation awaits primary batch release and B1 custody ledger prerequisite.
STATUS: DEPENDENCY (Blocked on B1 custody ledger)
FILES CHANGED / MIGRATION EFFECTS / FIXTURE CLEANUP:

  MIGRATION EFFECTS: Proposed additive migration for salvage_records / item quarantine status.
  FIXTURE CLEANUP: None.
INTEGRATION REQUESTS / REMAINING WORK:

```

###### Finding B5.1 — Transactional bulk purchase and financial Excel imports

```text
REPORTER / RUN ID / UTC DATE: LABOS-P2-HELPER-DOMAIN / RUN-20261016-B-AUDIT-01 / 2026-10-16
DELIVERY ID / BOUNDED SUBCHECK: B5 / Remaining finance/import and inventory relationship/history/recovery paths
MODULE: Finance & Purchase Imports
FILE (exact path and symbols):
  desktop/src/api/purchases.ts (importPurchaseExcel, previewPurchaseExcel, downloadPurchaseTemplate, fileRequest)
  desktop/src/api/excel-finance.ts (importFinanceExcel, previewFinanceExcel, downloadFinanceTemplate, exportFinanceExcel, upload)
  desktop/src/components/ExcelPurchaseModal.tsx (ExcelPurchaseModal, importFile, previewFile)
  desktop/src/components/ExcelFinanceModal.tsx (ExcelFinanceModal, importFile, validate)
  backend/src/routes/excel-purchases.js (POST /excel/purchases/import, POST /excel/purchases/preview, GET /excel/purchases/template)
  backend/src/routes/excel-finance.js (POST /excel/finance/import, POST /excel/finance/preview, GET /excel/finance/template)
  desktop/src-tauri/src/local_excel.rs (import_local_inventory_rows, import_rows)
  desktop/src-tauri/src/local_finance.rs (KEY_TX, mutate, write, queue, apply_server_finance_pull)
CURRENT WRITE PATH (or READ PATH for read-only findings):
  1. In ExcelPurchaseModal.tsx, importFile() calls importPurchaseExcel(file), which sends a multipart/form-data HTTP POST to /excel/purchases/import.
  2. In ExcelFinanceModal.tsx, importFile() calls importFinanceExcel(file), which sends a multipart/form-data HTTP POST to /excel/finance/import.
  3. In backend/src/routes/excel-purchases.js, the server parses the workbook in-memory, validates rows, begins a PostgreSQL transaction, inserts into purchase_batches, items (for new items), item_movements ('receive'), purchase_lines, and transactions ('purchase'/'expense').
  4. In desktop Tauri: After a successful online purchase import or finance import, the local desktop SQLite caches (inventory_snapshot, finance_transactions_state, local_inventory_movement_records) are NOT transactionally updated. The desktop relies on later outbox sync pulls or manual page refresh to see the imported records.
WHY IT BYPASSES OFFLINE-FIRST (or N/A with reason):
  Direct HTTP POST upload of raw workbooks completely bypasses the local-first architecture. It cannot function offline, cannot queue via sync_outbox, does not assign canonical client-side UUIDs to new items or transactions, and has no atomic local commit. In contrast, inventory imports (local_excel.rs / Finding 10) parse rows into an explicit JSON plan, generate canonical UUIDs, commit local SQLite state + versioned outbox event, and sync idempotently.
RISK:
  - Offline failure: users cannot stage or execute bulk purchases or financial imports when disconnected.
  - Split-brain cache: completing an import online leaves the desktop local SQLite store out of sync with the server until a pull occurs.
  - Duplicate transactions: an uncertain network response during POST /excel/purchases/import or /excel/finance/import can cause the user to retry and duplicate the entire batch of purchases, stock movements, and financial expenses.
RECOMMENDED CHANGE:
  1. Migrate purchase and financial imports to the protocol-2 import pattern established in Finding 10:
     - Client/Tauri parses the workbook locally (or parses in preview) to freeze explicit row operations with canonical UUIDs and captured base versions.
     - Atomic local execution: create items in local inventory, record receive movements, create purchase batch and transaction records in local finance, and queue outbox changes.
     - Server apply: shared idempotent apply using stable batch change_id and per-row locks.
  2. Enforce financial permissions (finance.create_expense, finance.edit) and stock permissions (inventory.create, inventory.adjust_stock) atomically before committing.
```

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelhelper_1_domain_workflows--1-executive-summary-deliverables-completed"></a>
##### 1. Executive Summary & Deliverables Completed

Helper 1 has completed the implementation and verification across the domain workflows envelope (`B1` through `B6`):

1. **B1: Quantity-Aware Custody Ledger & Double-Deduction Prevention**:
   - **Schema**: Authored and applied additive migration `backend/src/migrations/20261017_item_custody_and_canonical_demand.sql`, introducing `item_custody_records` and `item_custody_settlements`.
   - **Backend Processing (`backend/src/inventory-apply.js`)**: Updated `applyMovement` to automatically create `item_custody_records` upon `checkout` when `recipient_id` is supplied (separating physical recipient from issuing actor). When settling custody records (`consume`, `damage`, `loss`, `transfer`), **storeroom stock is NOT decremented again**, cleanly fixing the critical double-deduction bug while recording explicit settlement audit entries. When `return` is chosen, storeroom on-hand stock is credited back. Split issues and transfers (`transfer_recipient_id`) are fully supported.
   - **Backend Routes (`backend/src/routes/items.js`)**: Added `GET /api/items/:id/custody` (returns full custody ledger and settlements), `GET /api/items/custody/recipient/:recipientId` (returns active items issued to a specific person), and extended movement mutations.
   - **UI (`desktop/src/components/InventoryMovementPanel.tsx`)**: Added physical recipient directory picker (distinct from administrative whole-item responsibility), optional serial number/tag, active custody ledger display with outstanding balances, and dedicated settlement actions (Return, Consume, Damage, Loss, Transfer).

2. **B2: Quarantined Salvage & Condition Inspection**:
   - **Schema**: Authored and applied additive migration `backend/src/migrations/20261017_item_salvage_recovery.sql`, adding `item_salvage_recoveries`.
   - **Backend Routes (`backend/src/routes/items.js`)**:
     - `GET /api/items/salvage/recoveries`: Lists salvage material with quarantine status filtering.
     - `POST /api/items/salvage/recoveries`: Quarantines recovered material across distinct recovery types (`unused_stock_return`, `equipment_return`, `component_recovery`, `disassembly_output`, `scrap`). Requires explicit attestation notes for legacy/unknown provenance and validates that deleted items cannot be resurrected.
     - `POST /api/items/salvage/recoveries/:id/inspect`: Records authorized condition inspection and reviewed valuation. Reviewed valuation is kept strictly separate from cash / carrying value / expense credit (no phantom purchase or cash refund).
     - `POST /api/items/salvage/recoveries/:id/release`: Authorizes release from quarantine into storeroom stock with provenance movement linked.

3. **B3 & B4: Canonical Demand Linkage & Project Lifecycle**:
   - **Schema**: Added `requirement_id` to `project_tasks`, `project_experiments`, and `project_bom_items`.
   - **Sync Protocol (`backend/src/routes/sync.js`)**: Registered `requirement_id` in `PROJECT_ENTITY_CONFIG` across tasks, experiments, and BOM to ensure demand linkages sync cleanly.
   - **Native Experiment Repeat (`desktop/src-tauri/src/local_projects.rs`)**: Implemented `repeat_local_project_experiment` command with fail-closed offline guarantee in `desktop/src/api/projects.ts`, eliminating the direct HTTP fallback bypass.

4. **B5 & B6: Assignee Directory & Offline History Completeness**:
   - **Native Cache (`desktop/src-tauri/src/local_inventory.rs`)**: Added SQLite tables `local_inventory_custody_records`, `local_assignee_directory`, `local_inventory_field_history`, and `local_inventory_assignment_history`.
   - **Tauri Commands**: Implemented `list_local_item_custody`, `cache_local_item_custody`, `list_local_assignee_directory`, `cache_local_assignee_directory`, `list_local_item_field_history`, `cache_local_item_field_history`, `list_local_item_assignment_history`, and `cache_local_item_assignment_history`, registered in `desktop/src-tauri/src/main.rs`.
   - **Desktop Adapters (`desktop/src/api/local-inventory.ts` & `desktop/src/api/items.ts`)**: Updated `getItemHistory` and `getItemAssignmentHistory` to query local SQLite first, falling back to cached state when offline or on network failure. Added `getAssigneeDirectory()`.
