## Primary — salvage source quantities and legacy provenance

Original source: `docs/handoffs/phase2-parallel/PRIMARY_SALVAGE_SOURCE_CLAIMS_2026-10-29.md`. Retained historical scope/status.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_salvage_source_claims_2026-10-29--primary-salvage-source-quantities-and-legacy-provenance"></a>
### Primary — salvage source quantities and legacy provenance

MODULE: B1/B2 inventory custody and salvage

FILES: `backend/src/migrations/20261029_salvage_source_movement.sql`,
`backend/src/salvage-release.js`, `backend/src/routes/items.js`,
`backend/src/salvage-release-live-probe.mjs`, `desktop/src/api/items.ts`.

CURRENT WRITE PATH: existing authenticated HTTP salvage routes. Native salvage
snapshot/outbox path remains to implement. No native offline write claim.

RISK: distinct recovery rows could each credit the same consumed source;
source item identity alone is not proof of consumed quantity; custody returns
could credit stock without settling the original issue.

ACTUAL CHANGE MADE:

- Add optional source_movement_id with immutable-history FK and index. Existing
  recovery rows are preserved without invented provenance.
- Movement-backed creation derives source item/project from a consumption
  movement; mismatched references reject. Project-linked creation requires
  project edit access.
- Release locks the source movement and compares the sum of already released
  source quantities plus this claim against its original consumed quantity.
  Original consumption and finance entries are not rewritten. Pending proposals
  do not become accepted claims; excess release stays quarantined for review.
- Source item/project must match the original movement at release. Reviewed
  output quantity may differ from source quantity (disassembly yields).
- Historical source without a movement requires explicit attestation even when
  the item identity is known. Inspection supports adding those notes to old
  unreleased records; no automatic assignment of source provenance.
- Equipment/unused-stock returns with outstanding custody reject with an
  instruction to use custody settlement. Source inventory is locked before
  checking outstanding custody, serializing against issue writers.
- API types expose the source movement and inspection attestation fields.

VERIFICATION: production salvage service and authenticated HTTP routes on real
development PostgreSQL PASS partial/excess source claims, replay, mismatched
item, missing attestation, custody bypass, source derivation, project denial,
legacy attestation review, released inspection guard and nonfinite valuation.
Earlier balance/cost/scrap/failure rollback matrix also PASS. All fixtures and
movements absent after rollback. Migration applied only inside rollback test
transaction; it has not been deployed. This is sequential/savepoint evidence,
not independent committed-transaction race acceptance.

STATUS: source implemented; migration/API/desktop deployment pending. Native
salvage intents and receipts, offline reads/edits, full record visibility policy,
custody-aware quarantine return, multi-output recovery batches and simultaneous
release testing remain. Attested historical sources cannot have a machine-
verified quantity ceiling; human provenance review is the explicit exception.
No B1/B2 parent closure and no V1 changes.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_salvage_release_correctness_2026-10-29"></a>
## Primary — salvage release correctness

Original source: `docs/handoffs/phase2-parallel/PRIMARY_SALVAGE_RELEASE_CORRECTNESS_2026-10-29.md`. Retained historical scope/status.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_salvage_release_correctness_2026-10-29--primary-salvage-release-correctness"></a>
### Primary — salvage release correctness

Identity: primary implementation/review agent. This is a bounded B2 correction,
not completion of the offline salvage architecture.

MODULE: Inventory salvage inspection/release

FILES: `backend/src/routes/items.js`, `backend/src/salvage-release.js`,
`backend/src/salvage-release-live-probe.mjs`.

CURRENT WRITE PATH: existing desktop HTTP functions -> permissioned HTTP routes
-> PostgreSQL. Release now delegates to one transaction-owned service. Desktop
salvage does not yet have a native repository/outbox reader/writer.

WHY IT BYPASSES OFFLINE-FIRST: unchanged and still open. This batch repairs stock
and valuation correctness before duplicating behavior into native intentions.

RISK / ACTUAL CHANGE MADE:

- Invalid new item type `part` replaced with valid component type; equipment
  returns preserve the source type when available.
- Existing item balance is locked/read; stock and movement carry actual before
  and after quantities. PostgreSQL performs quantity arithmetic.
- Repeating release of an already released recovery returns its current record
  without a second credit or movement. Recovery row lock serializes that state.
- Scrap clears destination metadata and never creates stock or a receive event.
- Release rejects unapproved/uninspected/unusable material, retired destinations,
  mismatched known units, and damaged material directed into usable stock.
- Reviewed recovery value stays on the recovery; it is no longer mapped into
  replacement cost or a fabricated zero purchase cost. No cash entry is made.
- Inspection UPDATE now excludes released rows atomically, protecting against
  inspection overwriting a release after the earlier read. Numeric valuation
  must be finite. Incoming recovery quantities must fit the schema's positive
  three-decimal range.
- All release changes remain in the route's transaction; ledger failure rolls
  back the inventory change.

VERIFICATION: actual development PostgreSQL rollback probe passed existing/new
stock, true balances, sequential repeat, separate valuation, scrap, quarantine,
condition/unit guards and injected ledger failure. Syntax/whitespace checks
passed. Follow-up retired destination and stale scrap destination checks PASS.
All test records and movements are verified absent after rollback. No personal
data reset and no V1 writes.

STATUS: source implemented, not deployed. Live simultaneous committed release/
inspection races and HTTP permission tests remain separate from this service
probe. Native salvage intentions, stable create/inspect retries, source custody/
consumption links, over-recovery prevention and quantity settlement remain code
obligations. Release idempotence by recovery identity does not prevent two
distinct recoveries claiming the same source quantity. Do not mark B2 closed.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_salvage_output_batches_2026-10-29"></a>
## Phase 2 B2 — shared-source disassembly batches

Original source: `docs/handoffs/phase2-parallel/PRIMARY_SALVAGE_OUTPUT_BATCHES_2026-10-29.md`. Retained historical scope/status.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_salvage_output_batches_2026-10-29--phase-2-b2-shared-source-disassembly-batches"></a>
### Phase 2 B2 — shared-source disassembly batches

Identity / role: primary agent implementing and reviewing the batch contract.
This is not a helper completion report. B2 remains PARTIAL.

MODULE: Inventory salvage / disassembly.

FILE: `backend/src/salvage-intents.js`, `salvage-release.js`, additive migration
`20261029_salvage_source_output_batches.sql`; desktop `local_salvage.rs`,
`local_db.rs`, `api/items.ts`, `SalvageRecoveryPanel.tsx` and focused probes.

CURRENT WRITE PATH: one account-owned native SQLite outbox event with operation
`create_batch` contains stable identities for 2–25 outputs and one common source.
Generic sync applies all outputs, a batch row and its receipt in one PostgreSQL
transaction. Authoritative pull replaces pending projections. Each output then
uses the existing inspect/release intentions and version checks.

WHY IT BYPASSES OFFLINE-FIRST: the previous implementation had no batch contract;
independent output proposals each claimed source quantity, so dismantling one
assembly into different components could exhaust the source incorrectly. This
implementation adds no desktop API fallback or direct stock mutation.

RISK: double-counting a dismantled source, partial batch saves, retry duplicates,
or crediting uninspected outputs. Historical attestation cannot establish a
machine-verifiable ceiling. Concurrent releases must serialize on the original
consumption movement. Source quantities and recovered quantities can have
different units; output units do not redefine the source units.

RECOMMENDED CHANGE: one immutable common source claim per batch, atomic creation,
separate output inspection/valuation/release, ledger-backed stock and stable
idempotency. Never refund original consumption or create cash transactions.

ACTUAL CHANGE MADE:

- Added the batch table and recovery batch link without rewriting existing rows.
- First successful output release claims the batch source quantity once. Later
  output releases reuse that claim. Standalone and batch claims share the same
  aggregate consumption ceiling and row lock. Released output retries still
  return without adding stock.
- Source identity, project and quantity must match the immutable batch record.
  Outputs cannot override their common provenance. Scrap has no usable stock
  credit. Inspection/release still require current authority and expected version.
- Native batch creation writes one event atomically. Its pending projection shows
  every output as quarantined, with no fabricated approval or usable stock.
  Unknown ACK retries retain event/output identities and payload. Account, lease,
  cached project access and explicit domain permissions remain enforced.
- Added the desktop multi-output form with per-output name, quantity, unit and
  material/scrap disposition. All outputs remain individually reviewable.
- Browser batch authoring is explicitly unavailable for now; existing browser
  single-recovery paths remain. No browser-only direct-write workaround added.

VERIFICATION:

- Eleven adapter tests PASS, including uncertain ACK identity preservation and no
  HTTP fallback on batch failure. TypeScript check PASS.
- Real disk-backed SQLite scenario PASS for multi-output projection, retry,
  duplicate/mutated identities, provenance override rejection and reopen. An
  additional outbox-trigger failure assertion is included in the final build run.
  Development API was stopped during native verification.
- Actual development PostgreSQL + authenticated sync HTTP PASS: invalid late
  output rolls back all earlier outputs; receipt-insert failure rolls back batch
  and outputs; stable event retry and payload-mismatch rejection; individual
  inspection/release; scrap has no stock; standalone excess source claim denied.
- First HTTP probe failed on its assertion expecting `failed` for an invalid
  quantity. The API correctly returned `rejected` / `INVALID_QUANTITY`; corrected
  the expectation and reran the full matrix successfully.
- Real independent committed PostgreSQL transactions PASS: concurrent releases
  of two outputs each credit stock once while sharing one source claim; later
  excess claim denied. Existing single-recovery, shared-source, shared-item,
  stale-version, disabled-account and rollback concurrency cases also PASS.
  All owned fixture rows removed; rollback-only fixtures absent.
- Applied only the new additive migration to development PostgreSQL. The migration
  runner skipped all previously recorded versions. V1 DB/storage untouched.

STATUS: batch implementation and service/local verification complete; combined
API/Preview build results follow below. Native GUI/reconnect acceptance and
custody-linked return reconciliation remain. This does not close B2 or Phase 2.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_salvage_output_batches_2026-10-29--builddeployment-checkpoint"></a>
#### Build/deployment checkpoint

`sha256:d6faeb4e1e547ba312edbdbfdadd9b23b225bab60e5d231c8236a8e7d83a9be9`.
Authenticated HTTP and independent PostgreSQL concurrency probes also PASS from
the packaged image without a source mount; fixtures removed. Only development
`labos-labos-api-1` was recreated. Its image matches and health returns HTTP200,
API/database/storage OK. No V1 installation or restart performed.

Final disk-backed native run PASS including injected batch outbox failure: no

`resolve_conflict` warning remains. Explicit matching frontend/native origin:

## Primary — salvage offline workflow and inventory entry point

Original source: `docs/handoffs/phase2-parallel/PRIMARY_SALVAGE_OFFLINE_WORKFLOW_2026-10-29.md`. Retained historical scope/status.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_salvage_offline_workflow_2026-10-29--primary-salvage-offline-workflow-and-inventory-entry-point"></a>
### Primary — salvage offline workflow and inventory entry point

MODULE: B2 salvage, inspection and controlled stock release; shared A1/A3 synchronization boundaries.

FILE: `desktop/src-tauri/src/local_salvage.rs`, `desktop/src/api/items.ts`,
`desktop/src/api/sync.ts`, `desktop/src/components/SalvageRecoveryPanel.tsx`,
`desktop/src/pages/InventoryPage.tsx`, native command/conflict registration,
`backend/src/salvage-intents.js`, `backend/src/salvage-snapshot.js`,
`backend/src/routes/sync.js`, `backend/src/routes/items.js`,
`backend/src/migrations/20261029_salvage_source_movement.sql`.

CURRENT WRITE PATH: desktop -> native account/lease/permission checks -> SQLite
immutable outbox -> generic authenticated server push -> transaction containing
recovery/stock changes and idempotency receipt -> acknowledgement -> authorized
complete salvage pull. Browser retains the existing HTTP routes.

WHY IT BYPASSES OFFLINE-FIRST: previous desktop salvage adapters wrote directly
to HTTP and list reads required the server. There was no inventory recovery UI.
Native failure could not safely be treated as permission to attempt a second
server write.

RISK: repeated recovery credit, disappearing pending work, false offline approval,
restricted project disclosure, approval/release against stale inspection and
unrecoverable server-only workflows.

RECOMMENDED CHANGE: use one account-scoped native snapshot and immutable authored
intent journal; keep pending intent distinct from confirmed inspection/stock.
Recheck current permissions, project scope and expected recovery version on push.
Use existing generic transactional receipts rather than another retry transport.

ACTUAL CHANGE MADE:

- Account-scoped complete SQLite salvage snapshot survives reopening. Unknown
  initial data differs from a confirmed empty snapshot. Reads filter through
  current cached project visibility; partial/duplicate/noncanonical pulls reject.
- Create/inspect/release commands enforce current account, lease and domain
  capability. Project mutations require cached edit access. Inspection/release
  bind to the cached server version and actual cached project, not caller scope.
- Stable change/recovery IDs survive uncertain native acknowledgement retry.
  Atomic outbox insertion is the local persisted intent; a failed insert leaves
  no proposed record. Reusing an ID with a different payload rejects.
- Pending creates remain quarantined. Inspection/release requests do not pretend
  to be confirmed approval or stock. Acknowledged creates remain visible until
  a refreshed authoritative snapshot arrives. No native-error -> HTTP fallback.
- Server generic push dispatch rechecks active account, domain/project authority,
  source provenance and recovery version. Mutation and generic receipt share the
  transaction. Replays return acknowledgement, not historical private snapshots.
- Expected-version conflicts preserve authored work and require review rather
  than unrestricted keep-local retry. One outstanding action per recovery is
  deliberately enforced; inspection must synchronize before release is queued.
- Authorized snapshot endpoint shares the list's project visibility policy.
  Project-less ordinary laboratory records follow the repository's existing
  lab-wide read contract.
- Inventory now exposes a collapsible recovery section with centered native
  HTML dialogs for recording provenance, inspecting/valuing and confirming a
  release request. Permission-gated controls, account-fenced dialogs and pending
  statuses keep requests separate from accepted effects. No automatic cash credit.
- Source migration adds optional consumption reference and recovery version
  trigger without deleting existing rows or inventing historical provenance.

VERIFICATION:

- Seven frontend adapter checks PASS: native reads/filters, missing snapshot,
  SQLite error, stale account, browser read compatibility, stable uncertain-ACK
  identity, cached expected version, pending-before-initial-pull and no write fallback.
- Native real disk SQLite test PASS before final validation extension: complete
  versus unknown snapshot, scope filtering, failed outbox insert rollback,
  unchanged/change-ID replay behavior, reopening, acknowledgement-before-pull
  preservation and pending inspection without false approval. Development API
  stopped for native tests. Extended validation rerun tracked below.
- Actual development PostgreSQL/authenticated HTTP probe PASS: authorized pull,
  restricted project hiding before grant/after revocation, view versus edit,
  disabled account, source/quantity/custody safeguards, quarantine, valuation,
  one-credit retry, immutable payload mismatch, stale version, receipt failure
  rollback and retry. Outer rollback cleanup explicitly verifies fixture users,
  projects, recovery/items/movements and device receipts absent. Route savepoints
  are sequential; this is not independent committed-transaction concurrency proof.
- TypeScript PASS after query typing correction. Existing authorization suite
  initially 43 PASS / 1 stale source-location assertion failure. Replaced that
  assertion with direct receipt-privacy behavior; affected suite + receipt suite
  eight PASS. This was a test-location issue, not a relaxed privacy contract.

STATUS: substantial B2 implementation; integrated desktop acceptance still open.
Development-only API/Preview coordinated builds in progress at this checkpoint.
V1 app/containers/data are excluded. No Phase 2 parent is closed by this report.

Remaining B2 boundaries: independent concurrent release acceptance; shared-source
multi-output batch semantics; richer consumption-movement selection instead of
manual movement reference; custody-linked return reconciliation rather than
bypassing unsettled issues; full offline/reconnect GUI acceptance. Legacy source
attestation cannot provide a machine-verified consumption ceiling. Browser HTTP
creation still needs its own stable retry contract if browser parity is included.

Owner: primary agent. This is not a helper's completion report.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_salvage_offline_workflow_2026-10-29--final-validation-and-deployment-checkpoint"></a>
#### Final validation and deployment checkpoint

- Extended native test PASS with development API stopped: invalid approval,
  negative valuation, stale cached version and release before confirmed approval
  reject without queueing. Reopen/pending/failure-rollback matrix still PASS.
- Preview TypeScript + Vite production build PASS, 2,268 modules. Native Preview
  binary compilation is still running; no finished binary or GUI acceptance is
  claimed at this checkpoint.
- Development API image built successfully:
  `sha256:3712f9abc4a4ff29e83d956d8df004797811d9a9932bb1490aac57f1d0cb8ba8`.
  Only development API recreated. Startup applied the additive
  `20261029_salvage_source_movement` migration and started on port4000. API then
  stopped for native validation and is being restored afterward. Existing
  development PostgreSQL/storage volumes retained. No V1 mutation performed.
- Observed V1 API/database are stopped at the latest Docker inventory; this
  work issued no stop/recreate/reset command against them. Do not report their
  earlier healthy state as current or restart them as part of development work.

The first full Preview build completed at17:38:43 UTC (25,566,208 bytes).
Packaging review found the frontend development environment uses
`http://127.0.0.1:4000/api` while the native default spells loopback as localhost.
A native-only rebuild explicitly sets `LABOS_NATIVE_API_BASE` to the exact frontend
origin, reusing the verified frontend assets and the same Preview identity.
No origin equivalence exception or authorization bypass was introduced.
Restored development API health reports API/database/storage OK and container
healthy. API migration/deployment is complete; GUI acceptance remains open.

Final native-only Preview rebuild PASS (37.88s), with explicit matching
`LABOS_NATIVE_API_BASE` / `VITE_API_BASE_URL` development origin. Only the existing
unused `resolve_conflict` warning remains. The Preview package is built; it was

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_salvage_next_batch_2026-10-29--primary-next-salvage-implementation-boundary"></a>
### Primary — next salvage implementation boundary

Read-only inspection during coordinated project build. No salvage code changed
by this report; no helper work or verification PASS claimed.

MODULE: Inventory salvage, B1/B2/B6

FILE: `desktop/src/api/items.ts` salvage functions; `backend/src/routes/items.js`
salvage recovery/inspection/release routes; migration
`backend/src/migrations/20261017_item_salvage_recovery.sql`.

CURRENT WRITE PATH: desktop create/inspect/release calls API directly. No native
salvage repository or outbox branch exists in these API functions. Read also
depends on HTTP. Existing custody and inventory repositories are separate.

WHY IT BYPASSES OFFLINE-FIRST: ordinary authored recovery records and review
intentions cannot be durably saved through this path without the server.

unknown legacy provenance. Quarantined material must not increase usable stock.
Release must atomically validate state/permissions/remaining source quantities,
lock inventory, capture real before/after quantities, append stock provenance,
and record separately reviewed recovery value without fictitious cash refunds.
Repeated or lost-ACK requests must not credit stock twice. Use actual PostgreSQL
for schema, permission, rollback and concurrent release verification; stop only
development API for native offline persistence checks.

remaining migration history inspection required before implementation.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_salvage_desktop_acceptance_2026-10-29--primary-salvage-desktop-acceptance-checkpoint"></a>
### Primary — salvage desktop acceptance checkpoint

Owner: primary agent; actual separate V2 Preview, not V1. This is an acceptance
report, not additional implementation and not a helper completion claim.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_salvage_desktop_acceptance_2026-10-29--setup-and-observed-results"></a>
#### Setup and observed results

- Launched the built `desktop/src-tauri/target/debug/LabOS Preview.exe` with the
  separate `com.lab-inventory.app.preview` profile and development port4000 API.
  Installed V1 remained running and was neither closed nor updated.
- Existing Preview session restored as the cached admin; no automated credential
  entry or authentication change was performed.
- Read-only inspection of the actual Preview SQLite DB showed no pending outbox
  groups, an authorized downloaded salvage snapshot with zero recoveries, and no
  labelled acceptance intentions. Initial UI sync eventually reported synced.
- Created a consistent online SQLite backup with Node's SQLite backup API at
  `.tmp/preview-before-salvage-acceptance.sqlite`. Database inspection was read-only
  and did not print credentials, session secrets or unrestricted sync-state values.
- Actual Preview inventory page displayed inventory entries and the new
  Salvage & recovery / Review recoveries controls before the outage.
- Stopped only `labos-labos-api-1`; its state was confirmed `exited`. Existing
  development PostgreSQL stayed running and V1 was unchanged.
- Restarted only the Preview process launched for this read-only check. With the
  development API still stopped, a fresh Preview window's accessibility state
  displayed the cached dashboard: three active projects, eighteen overdue tasks,
  five low-stock entries, seeded project summaries and recent resources/notes.
  This verifies offline restored-session/cached-dashboard cold-start reads, not
  a newly authored mutation or a screenshot-based visual sign-off.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_salvage_desktop_acceptance_2026-10-29--tooling-failure-explicit-unverified-cases"></a>
#### Tooling failure / explicit unverified cases

The primary native helper initially timed out; bounded recovery recovered window
discovery. A later recovery-control click failed:

`point (6, -18) is outside window bounds { originX: 0, originY: 0, width: 12, height: 12 }`

Fresh selection and capture returned Preview accessibility text alongside a
screenshot of a different foreground application. The alternate native inspector
also returned a mismatched screenshot and rejected click geometry with:

`coordinate input geometry is unavailable`

No input was sent using the wrong screenshot. No terminal/UI injection, fake
window handle or authentication bypass was used. These are automation/tooling
failures; they do not establish that the recovery control itself is broken.

Remaining actual-desktop acceptance cases are NOT RUN:

1. Create a labelled two-output recovery offline through the form; confirm one
   outbox event and no stock effect, close the fully saved form and restart.
2. Reopen the recovery list offline; both quarantined outputs must remain visible.
3. Restore API; verify one server batch, two outputs and one receipt; repeat sync
   must not duplicate them. Verify acknowledged output projections reconcile.
4. Queue inspection offline, reconnect and pull; then queue release offline,
   reconnect and confirm the stock ledger's single shared source claim.
5. Select a real disposable custody issue, queue a partial return offline and
   restart; release only after confirmed inspection. Confirm one return movement,
   one holder settlement and one stock credit, then repeat reconnect.
6. Repeat with relevant authority/lease changes and preserve rejected work.

Existing SQLite, PostgreSQL HTTP, concurrency and adapter PASS evidence remains

## Phase 2 B1/B2 — inspected custody returns

Original source: `docs/handoffs/phase2-parallel/PRIMARY_SALVAGE_CUSTODY_RETURNS_2026-10-29.md`. Retained historical scope/status.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_salvage_custody_returns_2026-10-29--phase-2-b1b2-inspected-custody-returns"></a>
### Phase 2 B1/B2 — inspected custody returns

Identity / role: primary agent. Primary implementation and evidence, not helper
completion. No Phase 2 parent is closed by this checkpoint.

MODULE: Salvage returns / quantity-aware inventory custody.

FILE: `backend/src/salvage-custody-return.js`, `salvage-intents.js`,
`salvage-release.js`, `routes/items.js`, additive
`20261029_salvage_source_return_custody.sql`; desktop `local_salvage.rs`, shared
custody reader in `local_inventory.rs`, command registration, `api/items.ts`,
`SalvageRecoveryPanel.tsx`; existing salvage HTTP/concurrency/adapter probes.

CURRENT WRITE PATH: desktop saves a custody-linked quarantined recovery as one
immutable SQLite outbox intention. Generic server sync derives its original
item/project/unit from custody and creates the record transactionally. Inspection
and release retain their existing versioned intentions. Confirmed release reuses
the canonical inventory mutation/return writer to create the stock movement,
custody settlement and audit in the same transaction as the recovery state and
outer sync receipt. Authorized snapshots return the confirmed result.

WHY IT BYPASSES OFFLINE-FIRST: previous salvage return proposals had no custody
link and were blocked when issued units remained outstanding. Crediting stock
separately would leave the holder owing the same quantity and allow a later
ordinary return to credit it again. This change adds no desktop server fallback.

RISK: double return, settling the wrong holder, source quantity/unit changes,
partial rollback, serialized fractions and deadlocks with existing return writers.

RECOMMENDED CHANGE: preserve the issued identity and provenance; quarantine until
inspection; settle only the selected holder/quantity at release; reuse canonical
return accounting and lock ordering; preserve unsuccessful authored work.

ACTUAL CHANGE MADE:

- Added optional recovery source-custody and confirmed-settlement foreign keys.
  Existing records are preserved. Only development received this migration.
- Added an account/lease/permission/project-filtered native custody source reader.
  Missing cache remains unknown; there is no HTTP fallback. Local requests cannot
  combine custody with consumption or a disassembly batch, change original units
  or project, exceed cached outstanding quantity, or split a serialized unit.
- The form selects cached outstanding custody for equipment/unused-stock returns.
  Quantity and unit stay tied to the selected issue. A pending request leaves
  storeroom stock and the holder's outstanding quantity unchanged.
- Server creation derives and checks the actual source. Release rechecks live
  authority, identity, condition and remaining custody. It follows the canonical
  inventory advisory lock -> item -> custody order and uses the recovery UUID as
  the stable return-movement/settlement UUID.
- Usable return goes to the original active usable item; stock credits exactly
  once while custody becomes partially settled or settled. An explicit settlement
  link and canonical inventory audit preserve traceability. Receipt/ledger/audit
  failure rolls back the entire operation.
- Unlinked salvage cannot bypass outstanding custody. Historical consumption,
  reviewed salvage valuation, project expenses and cash remain unchanged.
- Browser authoring of this new link is explicitly unsupported; the old direct
  browser route rejects the new field rather than silently dropping provenance.

VERIFICATION:

- 13 focused adapter checks PASS, including cached source reads, linked payload,
  account switching and no fallback. TypeScript check PASS.
- Real disk-backed SQLite scenario PASS with development API stopped: hidden
  project custody filtered, excess/mixed claims denied, stable retry, quarantined
  projection and original outstanding balance unchanged. Existing batch/source/
  reopen/rollback checks still PASS.
- Actual development PostgreSQL + authenticated sync HTTP PASS: quarantine and
  inspection have no balance effect; release restores original stock and settles
  the holder once; repeat receipt adds no movement; receipt-insert failure rolls
  back movement, custody, stock, settlement and recovery. Canonical audit present.
- Partial returns preserve outstanding balances and transition through
  `partially_settled` to `settled`; exhausted custody and fractional serialized
  returns reject. Damaged material cannot credit usable stock. All rollback
  fixtures absent after the probe.
- Independent real PostgreSQL race PASS: inspected return vs ordinary canonical
  return serializes without deadlock, one stock credit and one settlement. Existing
  disassembly/source/stock/version/revocation/rollback races still PASS. All owned
  committed fixtures and their audit rows removed through scoped cleanup.
- Migration runner skipped existing recorded migrations and applied only the new
  custody-return links. Development API remained stopped during native tests.

STATUS: usable custody-return reconciliation implemented and service/local checks
PASS. Combined build/deployment results are tracked below. B1/B2 remain PARTIAL.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_salvage_custody_returns_2026-10-29--explicit-boundaries"></a>
#### Explicit boundaries

- Damaged/repairable issued units cannot become usable stock through this return.
  Their saved recovery remains for review; explicit damage/repair handling is
  required. This does not implement a separate repair-location/quarantine custody
  lifecycle or silently convert a serialized asset into a new stock identity.
- Cached history completeness, browser authoring/retry parity and native GUI
  outage/reconnect acceptance remain separate delivery boundaries.
- No V1 app, database or storage was updated or reset.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_salvage_custody_returns_2026-10-29--build-deployment"></a>
#### Build / deployment

Development API image build PASS:
`sha256:778c4b1821a7efe4fd3e74fa91d6fd6a08bdaaf4f9b7f5882b20cb44e92ccaba`.
The HTTP and concurrency matrices PASS again from that packaged image without
source mounts. Only development API was recreated; health returns HTTP200 with
API/database/storage OK and its image matches. Existing data and V1 untouched.

Preview's first frontend build passed before the final form polish. Bundle
inspection caught the earlier unit expression, so a final rebuild was completed.
Final TypeScript/Vite PASS (Vite 1m06s), native Preview PASS (1m09s); only the
existing unused `resolve_conflict` warning remains. Compiled bundle confirms

Native GUI/restart/outage/reconnect acceptance remains open. The earlier report's

## Primary — salvage read and mutation authority

Original source: `docs/handoffs/phase2-parallel/PRIMARY_SALVAGE_ACCESS_2026-10-29.md`. Retained historical scope/status.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_salvage_access_2026-10-29--primary-salvage-read-and-mutation-authority"></a>
### Primary — salvage read and mutation authority

MODULE: Salvage / project visibility / stock mutation permissions

FILES: `backend/src/salvage-access.js`, `backend/src/salvage-release.js`,
`backend/src/routes/items.js`, `backend/src/salvage-release-live-probe.mjs`.

CURRENT WRITE PATH: authenticated HTTP routes; inspection and release own
PostgreSQL transactions. Native salvage repository/outbox is still outstanding.

RISK: inventory permission alone previously allowed reading or modifying a
recovery linked to a restricted project. Inspection's separate read/update
also lacked transaction-bound project authority.

ACTUAL CHANGE MADE:

- Salvage list binds authenticated account/role into the shared linked-project
  visibility predicate before applying status/project filters. Restricted
  project names and records do not escape through this list.
- New transaction helper reloads active database user, current domain permission,
  project and membership/grant authority. It uses shared project access semantics.
  Existing user/project/override/membership/grant rows are read with share locks
  through the mutation client rather than a role supplied by the request body.
- Release rechecks authority before even returning an already-released record.
  A formerly authorized client cannot use replay to retrieve it after revocation.
- Inspection now owns its transaction and row lock; authority check and guarded
  update occur in that same transaction. Error paths roll back and release the
  client; existing business status/code errors remain explicit.

VERIFICATION: actual development PostgreSQL with production authentication and
HTTP router passed restricted owner-without-grant hiding, explicit filter hiding,
view-grant read with mutation denial, edit-grant inspect/release success, grant
revocation hiding plus release/replay denial, and disabled-account denial.
Earlier source quantity, legacy attestation, balances, valuation, scrap and fault
rollback matrices also passed. Test route transactions are savepoints inside
one outer rollback, not independently committed concurrent transactions. All
fixture users/projects/recoveries/items/movements absent after rollback. Syntax
and whitespace checks passed.

STATUS: source implemented, not deployed. Domain permission middleware remains
on public routes; this helper does not grant inventory authority from project
access. Native cached visibility/revocation and outbox handling still need code.
Creation currently retains its earlier project access check; its stable intent/
receipt transaction contract belongs to the next native/server integration.
No parent closure and no V1 data or application changes.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_project_edit_permissions_2026-10-29"></a>
## Primary — ordinary project edit permissions and concurrent changes

Original source: `docs/handoffs/phase2-parallel/PRIMARY_PROJECT_EDIT_PERMISSIONS_2026-10-29.md`. Retained historical scope/status.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_project_edit_permissions_2026-10-29--primary-ordinary-project-edit-permissions-and-concurrent-changes"></a>
### Primary — ordinary project edit permissions and concurrent changes

Owner: primary implementation/review agent.

MODULE: Projects / native writes / sync reconciliation / conflict recovery

FILES: `backend/src/project-edit-patch.js`, `backend/src/routes/sync.js`,
`desktop/src-tauri/src/local_projects.rs`,
`desktop/src/api/project-conflict-guidance.ts` and focused tests/probe.

CURRENT WRITE PATH: desktop project edit -> native SQLite snapshot and outbox
transaction -> authenticated sync -> PostgreSQL transaction and retry receipt.

WHY IT NEEDED CHANGE: native events carry complete project records. The sync
handler previously interpreted an unchanged budget as a financial mutation,
rejecting ordinary description edits by researchers. Applying every field in
the full record could also overwrite unrelated newer server values.

RISK: stuck ordinary edits, accidental stale-value overwrites, and budget
changes saved provisionally without the finance permission needed to sync them.

ACTUAL CHANGE MADE:

- For events with a before snapshot, derive the authored field changes on a copy
  of the record. Unchanged fields are omitted, including equivalent numeric
  budget/date representations. Original outbox payload and retry hash remain
  unchanged.
- Conflicting authored fields reject with PROJECT_EDIT_CONFLICT. Matching
  already-applied values converge. Lifecycle changes retain their existing
  revision checks. Legacy events without a before snapshot retain prior behavior.
- Actual native budget changes require finance.edit before saving local state
  or creating an event. An unchanged numeric budget remains an ordinary edit.
- Conflict UI blocks blind retries and explains preservation/review/reapply.
  Existing native recovery and authorization remain authoritative.

VERIFICATION: focused pure projection tests passed (three), alongside optional
date projection (one PASS / one separate PostgreSQL test SKIP). Production
authenticated HTTP/PostgreSQL probe initially passed ordinary prose replay,
actual budget denial for a researcher, and conflicting prose rejection. A first
fixture attempt incorrectly used an admin deny override (admins retain baseline
authority); fixed by using a researcher and refreshing its credential version.
Every probe run confirms fixture absence after rollback. Final extension also
checks a newer unrelated budget survives the prose edit. Final native/build
results: authenticated HTTP/PostgreSQL extension PASS including newer budget
preservation; all rollback fixtures absent. All 17 native project tests PASS
with development API stopped, including unchanged numeric budget acceptance and
denied changed budget leaving the outbox count unchanged. Eight conflict UI
tests PASS; TypeScript exit 0 and whitespace checks PASS. Development API restored.

STATUS: source implemented; coordinated API/Preview deployment and full desktop
acceptance remain. Independent concurrent transactions and legacy events lacking
before snapshots are outside the new field conflict guarantee. No phase parent
closed and no V1 changes.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_local_reservation_review_2026-10-29"></a>
## Primary — offline reservation review and project acceptance

Original source: `docs/handoffs/phase2-parallel/PRIMARY_LOCAL_RESERVATION_REVIEW_2026-10-29.md`. Retained historical scope/status.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_local_reservation_review_2026-10-29--primary-offline-reservation-review-and-project-acceptance"></a>
### Primary — offline reservation review and project acceptance

Identity: primary implementation/review agent. No helper contribution claimed.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_local_reservation_review_2026-10-29--change-and-boundaries"></a>
#### Change and boundaries

MODULE: Projects / reservation review

FILES: `desktop/src/api/projects.ts`,
`desktop/src/api/reservation-review-projection.ts`,
`desktop/src/components/ReservationReviewQueue.tsx`

CURRENT WRITE PATH: unchanged. Desktop decisions use the existing native
account-owned reservation intent and outbox writer. Server reconciliation owns
allocation authority. Browser decisions retain their existing HTTP path.

WHY IT BYPASSES OFFLINE-FIRST: the prior central queue reader always fetched
`/projects/reservations/review-queue`, although individual project reservations
already existed in native SQLite snapshots.

RISK: offline users could not inspect the queue; an empty/error screen obscured
cached requests. Deriving global availability from incomplete local records
could falsely promise stock unless clearly bounded.

RECOMMENDED CHANGE / ACTUAL CHANGE MADE:

- Desktop queue now reads existing authorized native project and inventory
  snapshots. It does not call HTTP when a native read fails or a snapshot is
  absent. Account changes suppress completed old-account reads.
- Missing inventory quantities stay unknown. Missing project reservation
  snapshots are counted separately from confirmed empty collections.
- Reusable assets count overlapping confirmed reservations; consumables count
  all confirmed reservations. Invalid quantities/dates produce unknown values.
- UI identifies the queue as a local subset, describes estimated availability,
  and preserves pending decision status without claiming confirmation.
- Repeated actions are disabled while a local decision is pending. Unknown stock
  disables confirmation. Rejection still requires a reason.
- Browser queue retains the server read, wrapped in the same snapshot envelope.
- Success messages no longer appear as errors; failed refresh retains available
  rows and offers Retry.

VERIFICATION: project/reservation boundary suite plus initial projection suite:
47 PASS, 0 FAIL. Final projection suite: 7 PASS, 0 FAIL (includes additional null
stock and missing-date cases). Tests execute actual TypeScript projection and
API orchestration with native-reader boundaries; they are not live database or
GUI acceptance. Existing production native readers were reused without changes.
TypeScript compile completed with exit 0 for the integration. Earlier Save repair compiled successfully and its
Preview binary rebuilt successfully in 3m 13s.

STATUS: implemented; integrated Preview deployment/GUI verification remains.
Current running Preview contains the header Save repair but not this new queue.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_local_reservation_review_2026-10-29--desktop-test-limitation"></a>
#### Desktop test limitation

With development API stopped, rebuilt Preview opened the seeded project from
its local data. Window-control geometry became invalid after maximizing:
scroll reported a 12x12 window while capture displayed the full application.
Fresh window selection and capture reproduced a 12x12 primary surface plus a
full application surface. Further input was stopped instead of claiming the
save/restart/reconnect batch passed. Development API was restarted afterward.
No V1 app, database or storage was changed.

Assistant header wording corrected from `Connected` to `Configured`, matching
the saved enabled/model capability it actually displays. It no longer claims
live connectivity from cached configuration. No generation or authority change.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_local_reservation_review_2026-10-29--remaining-acceptance"></a>
#### Remaining acceptance

Deploy the queue frontend with Preview; verify request/review offline, pending
decision persistence over restart, reconciliation/rejection on reconnect, and
cross-project competition with real PostgreSQL. Also complete the repaired
header Save offline/restart check when reliable window input is available.
No A/B/C parent item is closed by these bounded changes.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_task_experiment_pull_2026-10-28"></a>
## Task–experiment link reconciliation

Original source: `docs/handoffs/phase2-parallel/PRIMARY_TASK_EXPERIMENT_PULL_2026-10-28.md`. Retained historical scope/status.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_task_experiment_pull_2026-10-28--taskexperiment-link-reconciliation"></a>
### Task–experiment link reconciliation

Identity: primary agent implementation report, not helper work.
Scope: Phase 2 B3 / A5.

- MODULE: Task–experiment relationships.
- FILE: `desktop/src-tauri/src/local_projects.rs`.
- CURRENT WRITE PATH: Local link/unlink operations persist project state and outbox events; project pull reconciles server snapshots.
- WHY IT BYPASSES OFFLINE-FIRST: No direct server-write bypass found in this batch. The defect was reconciliation: a server row with a pending local event was excluded, then its local counterpart was also excluded because its ID existed on the server.
- RISK: A newly linked experiment could disappear during pull-before-ack ordering, despite its pending event still existing. Repeated pulls could keep the local collection incorrect.
- RECOMMENDED CHANGE: Preserve the current local representation for pending identities; absence locally means a pending unlink. Use authoritative server rows only for nonpending identities, respecting tombstones and deduplicating by ID.
- ACTUAL CHANGE MADE: Extracted the attachment relation merger into a shared helper and reused it for task–experiment links. The previously ignored task–experiment tombstone argument is now supplied to this merge. Attachment behavior remains covered by its existing regression tests. No event rewriting, acknowledgment fabrication or HTTP fallback added.
- VERIFICATION: Extended the actual project-pull disk regression with pending link and unlink events. The server returns both before acknowledgment. Two pulls must preserve exactly the local pending link and suppress the removed link; close/reopen must retain that result and all five pending events. Final run result follows below.
- STATUS: Implemented and focused native verification passed: all 15 project tests pass with `cargo test local_projects:: --locked --offline -j 1`; scoped `git diff --check` passes. Desktop/API acceptance and deployment are not claimed.

No personal database, V1 install, storage, service state or API deployment changed.
Next integrated acceptance: link/unlink offline, restart, reconnect with pull-before-ack and replay, then confirm eventual local/server convergence without duplicate associations.

Scope: A1/B3 project pull visibility. Verification only; no production permission change.

Added `backend/src/project-visibility-live-probe.mjs`, explicitly gated by
`LABOS_DEV_VISIBILITY_PROBE=rollback-only`. It exercises the same
`visibilityReadSql` predicate used by `/projects/pull` on actual development
PostgreSQL with three temporary projects and two existing user IDs. It does not
change existing users, credentials, projects or grants.

Eight cases PASS: owner and member project access; unrelated principal sees only
lab scope; admin sees all three; a restricted view grant allows the named user
only; grant revocation removes restricted access; membership revocation removes
project-scoped access. Owner status alone does not bypass restricted grants.
These are SQL principal parameters, not authenticated HTTP sessions.

All fixture project, membership and grant rows were confirmed absent after
ROLLBACK. Existing development DB was temporarily started then restored to its
original stopped state; V1/API containers were unchanged.

Added a source contract for domain permission before project query, authenticated
identity parameter binding and child IDs derived from visible projects. Focused
visibility suite: 10 tests PASS. Source inspection is not runtime middleware proof.

Run from repository root with development DB available:

```powershell
docker compose -p labos -f deploy/docker-compose.yml run --rm --no-deps -T -e LABOS_DEV_VISIBILITY_PROBE=rollback-only -v 'C:/Users/balik/Iven/lab-inventory-app/backend/src:/app/src:ro' --entrypoint node labos-api src/project-visibility-live-probe.mjs
```

Remaining: actual JWT/domain-permission HTTP acceptance, endpoint response
assembly, native cache revocation and offline/reconnect. No parent closure or

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_project_pending_deletions_2026-10-28--pending-project-child-deletions-primary-agent"></a>
### Pending project-child deletions — primary agent

Scope: Phase 2 A5/B3; primary implementation, not helper work.

- MODULE: Project child snapshot reconciliation.
- FILE: `desktop/src-tauri/src/local_projects.rs`.
- CURRENT WRITE PATH: Native child deletion removes the local row and records an outbox event. Project pull reconciles server child collections.
- WHY IT BYPASSES OFFLINE-FIRST: No direct-write bypass; the pull's pending-row retention rule could resurrect a stale server row when a local deletion awaited acknowledgment.
- RISK: Deleted tasks/experiments reappear during refresh before the server applies/acknowledges their deletion.
- RECOMMENDED CHANGE: For pending child identities, retain an incoming row only if its local counterpart still exists; subsequent overlay preserves that local row. Pending absence remains absence. Nonpending tombstone handling is unchanged.
- ACTUAL CHANGE MADE: Updated the shared child retention rule, including its existing composite item identity handling. No outbox deletion/rewrite, acknowledgment fabrication or server-write fallback.
- VERIFICATION: Added pending task and experiment deletions to the actual production pull regression. Two pulls include the stale server rows; both must remain absent locally, while existing pending edits, attachments and links survive. The fixture closes/reopens SQLite and preserves seven pending events. Final test result recorded below.
- STATUS: Source implemented; all 15 focused native project tests pass (`cargo test local_projects:: --locked --offline -j 1`), and scoped `git diff --check` passes. Other collections sharing the rule and full desktop/API convergence still require acceptance coverage.

Only temporary native test data is used. V1, personal databases, storage and services are unchanged. No phase parent closure or deployment claimed.

### Project finance availability — October 28

Identity: primary agent. A3/B3/B5 source follow-up, not helper evidence.

- MODULE: Desktop project financial summary.
- FILE: desktop/src/api/projects.ts; desktop/src/pages/ProjectFinanceView.tsx; desktop/src/api/project-reservation-boundaries.test.mjs.
- CURRENT WRITE PATH: No writes changed. Desktop summary combines local projects, transactions, inventory and project workspace. Browser summary remains HTTP.

- RISK: Misleading zero valuations or understated totals; composite responses could also span an account switch.

Confirmed empty allocations and explicit zero cost remain zero. Invalid ledger amounts/directions fail the summary rather than inventing spending figures. Missing/nonpositive budgets produce no percentage. Account checks run across composite reads. UI shows Unavailable for unknown row valuation and for the combined valuation total if any row is unknown.
- VERIFICATION: 34 project adapter regression tests passed, including five unavailable-valuation scenarios, confirmed empty/zero/known valuation, invalid ledger amounts and account changes. Mocked repositories/IPC; no real database or desktop outage test in this batch.
- STATUS: Implemented in source, desktop acceptance pending. This does not establish durable initial-sync completeness or close A3/B3/B5.

TypeScript no-emit and scoped diff whitespace checks passed.

No changes to stock, custody, expense history or financial authority. Allocated inventory value remains the existing allocation-times-current-unit-cost measure, not actual physical issue or historical expense. No V1 change, deployment, service restart or personal-data mutation.

- ACTUAL CHANGE MADE: Added pending_experiment_with_history and used it for matching pending experiment rows in the existing pull merge. Only history is copied; title, observations, other local fields and outbox events are unchanged. Missing/malformed history or a different ID does not overwrite the last local history. An explicit empty server array replaces the old history. Pending whole-project snapshots retain the existing defer policy.
- VERIFICATION: Added same-ID/foreign-ID/malformed/empty/repeated-merge tests plus an isolated file-backed SQLite save/reopen test through production save/save_checked/load. Test asserts authored fields, history and the original pending outbox payload survive reopening without ACK or extra event. Initial test launch was blocked by the approval service usage limit and did not execute; retry is in progress.
- STATUS: Source implemented; native test run PASS: 14 local_projects tests, including file-backed save/reopen and unchanged pending-event checks. Full apply_server_project_pull command, native session switching, running desktop outage/reconnect and coordinated deployment are separate acceptance gates. Scoped diff whitespace check also passed.

The SQLite test exercises desktop persistence, not a substitute for the already-run actual PostgreSQL server query check. No installed V1, personal data, service state or deployed artifact is changed.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_attachment_pull_convergence_2026-10-28--project-work-attachment-pull-convergence-primary-agent"></a>
### Project work attachment pull convergence — primary agent

Identity: primary implementation/review agent, not a helper report.
Scope: Phase 2 B3 project integration / A5 nested synchronization.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_attachment_pull_convergence_2026-10-28--finding"></a>
#### Finding

- MODULE: Project task and experiment attachments.
- FILE: `desktop/src-tauri/src/local_projects.rs`.
- CURRENT WRITE PATH: Native attachment mutations save the canonical project-level `attachments` collection with an outbox event. Server project pulls supply attachments nested inside tasks and experiments.
- WHY IT BYPASSES OFFLINE-FIRST: This is a read/merge mismatch, not a newly discovered direct server write. The pull previously updated nested collections without rebuilding the canonical collection used by local attachment readers.
- RISK: Confirmed attachments can disappear from local views; stale nested copies can disagree with pending detachments; refresh/restart can expose inconsistent data.
- RECOMMENDED CHANGE: Normalize server and legacy nested shapes into one canonical collection, merge pending changes by attachment identity, and derive nested views from that collection.
- ACTUAL CHANGE MADE: Normalize on load and incoming pull. Preserve an existing canonical list, including explicit empty lists. Deduplicate incoming IDs. Pending attachment rows retain their local representation; pending removals remain absent even when the server still includes them. Nonpending server absence and tombstones remove confirmed rows. Rebuild nested task/experiment attachment arrays from the canonical list, replacing the separate nested attachment merge.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_attachment_pull_convergence_2026-10-28--verification"></a>
#### Verification

Focused native tests cover nested normalization, explicit empty canonical lists, duplicate IDs, pending additions/removals, tombstones, authoritative absence and repeated merges. The on-disk SQLite regression exercises the actual production pull twice, preserves pending events/authored experiment fields, rejects a foreign account and closes/reopens the database to check persistence. Nested and canonical attachment views must agree.

Final focused run: `cargo test local_projects:: --locked --offline -j 1` passed all 15 native project tests, including the nested-view projection assertion. Scoped `git diff --check` passed.

This uses an isolated temporary desktop SQLite database, not the personal database. It does not claim real-server attachment push/pull or desktop UI acceptance. Prior PostgreSQL history evidence concerns history only, not attachment acceptance.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_attachment_pull_convergence_2026-10-28--status-and-remaining-acceptance"></a>

No Phase 2 parent is closed by this batch.

## B3/B4 child editing versus review — PostgreSQL verification

Original source: `docs/handoffs/phase2-parallel/PRIMARY_REVIEW_CHILD_CONCURRENCY_2026-10-27.md`. Retained historical scope/status.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_review_child_concurrency_2026-10-27--b3b4-child-editing-versus-review-postgresql-verification"></a>
### B3/B4 child editing versus review — PostgreSQL verification

Identity: LABOS-P2-PRIMARY. Primary verification, not helper implementation.

MODULE: Project review / connected plan mutations.

FILE: backend/src/project-review-child-lock-live-probe.mjs; existing
project-review-sync.js and 20261024_project_plan_revision.sql exercised unchanged.

CURRENT WRITE PATH: child SQL mutation -> parent plan-revision trigger/row lock;
review intent -> same parent lock -> current authority -> displayed-token check
-> atomic decision and audit.

WHY IT BYPASSES OFFLINE-FIRST: none demonstrated. This closes a bounded server
concurrency coverage gap rather than introducing another mutation path.

RISK: approval could otherwise race a child edit and accept an obsolete plan.

RECOMMENDED CHANGE: exercise actual PostgreSQL locks in both acquisition orders,
and call the production review helper with a stale token after a child mutation.

ACTUAL CHANGE MADE: added opt-in, two-connection rollback-only probe with bounded
lock/statement timeouts. No production logic changes or committed migrations.

VERIFICATION: October27, existing development PostgreSQL only. Actual API remained
stopped. Disposable compose runner mounted source read-only. All four cases PASS:
task update, experiment update, BOM insert, canvas-block update. Parent-first
locks blocked child SQL (55P03); child-first locks blocked the production review
helper (55P03). Each child mutation advanced the parent revision by one. A stale
token was rejected with REVIEW_VERSION_CONFLICT in a transaction observing the
child mutation. All transactions rolled back and original revisions were checked.
No existing BOM fixture was present: a generated BOM row was inserted only inside
test transactions, and its absence after rollback was asserted. Initial run had
three passes and one skip; final run covered all four without skips.

STATUS: BOUNDED CONCURRENCY CHECK PASS. B3/B4 remain open.

Limits: this is not a concurrent full HTTP request or committed transport replay
test. Deletes, cross-project reparenting, other child tables, permission-management
request races and live desktop restart/reconnect remain separate acceptance gates.
V1 containers, installed executable and personal data were not changed. Development
database restored stopped after testing, matching its initial state.

Identity / role: primary agent, A1/B3 follow-up. Not helper-delivered work.

- MODULE: Desktop project/workspace/task/experiment/BOM/attachment native adapters.
- FILE: desktop/src/api/projects.ts; desktop/src/api/project-reservation-boundaries.test.mjs.
- CURRENT WRITE PATH: UI -> shared localInvoke -> existing native command -> local transaction/outbox. Browser uses HTTP. Several specialized readers already had account-generation guards, but the shared adapter did not.
- WHY IT BYPASSES OFFLINE-FIRST: No newly discovered HTTP fallback after a rejected native write; the gap was session isolation of returned results. Undefined non-delete results were also accepted as successful responses.

- ACTUAL CHANGE MADE: Shared localInvoke now performs those guards. Browser transport unchanged. No automatic replay, rollback, new UUID, HTTP retry or pending-event deletion is triggered by the guard. A mutation committed before an account switch stays persisted; the renderer rejects its late completion and asks for refresh.
- VERIFICATION: 44 focused adapter/editor/refresh checks passed. New checks cover eight representative operations with absent and changed sessions, nullish create/delete results, native failures without HTTP fallback and unchanged browser create transport. These are mocked-IPC adapter regressions, not live account-switch desktop acceptance.
- STATUS: Implemented in source; coordinated desktop acceptance pending. TypeScript result recorded below when available.

Boundary: this renderer check is not a replacement for native account binding and commit-time permission checks, nor proof of their complete coverage. No native/server mutation policy was changed. Remaining online-authoritative membership/access-grant operations were not converted into offline grants. Experiment-history HTTP reads and financial-summary unavailable-section handling still require separate review; do not claim those were resolved here.

TypeScript no-emit and scoped diff whitespace checks passed.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_permission_writer_authority_2026-10-27"></a>
## A1/B3/B4 permission writer authority race

Original source: `docs/handoffs/phase2-parallel/PRIMARY_PERMISSION_WRITER_AUTHORITY_2026-10-27.md`. Retained historical scope/status.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_permission_writer_authority_2026-10-27--a1b3b4-permission-writer-authority-race"></a>
### A1/B3/B4 permission writer authority race

Identity / role: LABOS-P2-PRIMARY. Primary implementation and verification.

MODULE: Permission override replacement; project review authority concurrency.

FILE: backend/src/permission-replacement-authority.js, routes/auth.js,
permission-replacement-authority.test.js, permission-replacement-lock-live-probe.mjs,
project-review-authority.test.js.

CURRENT WRITE PATH: authenticated permission HTTP request -> middleware check ->
transaction -> locked actor/target authority recheck -> replace overrides ->
mandatory audit -> commit. This is an existing online administrative operation,
not a new desktop data-write fallback.

WHY IT BYPASSES OFFLINE-FIRST: no new bypass. Previous code locked only the target
and trusted earlier actor role/permissions, allowing stale actor authority after
concurrent demotion/disable or permission revocation. Replacement also omitted
implicit removals from its escalation check (removing a deny can restore access).

RISK: stale authorization or delegated permission escalation.

RECOMMENDED CHANGE: lock actor and target in deterministic order, re-read current
authority inside the write transaction, and authorize every changed override,
including removal. Retain atomic audit and administrator-role protection.

ACTUAL CHANGE MADE: shared transactional helper locks both users ORDER BY id FOR
UPDATE; rejects inactive/missing actor, missing management permission and admin
target. Reads actor permissions using the same transaction. Delegated managers
must hold each changed permission; unchanged target exceptions may be retained.
Route uses this helper before DELETE/INSERT, removes stale actor precheck, and
returns typed authorization errors rather than masking them as generic HTTP500.
No production data edits, migrations, server deployment or desktop update.

VERIFICATION: 16 focused Node tests PASS. Real development PostgreSQL probe PASS:
actor/target updates blocked while replacement authority locks held; reverse
actor-disable lock blocked authorization; observed disabled/demoted actors rejected.
All changes rolled back. Route syntax and diff whitespace checks PASS. Development
API stayed stopped; development DB restored stopped. V1 untouched.

STATUS: SOURCE IMPLEMENTED — bounded tests pass; deployment/full HTTP acceptance pending.

Remaining: full authenticated permission HTTP replacement/review concurrent request
integration, reciprocal manager request behavior, broader role/password/account
writers and real desktop reconnect. Helper/lock tests are not end-to-end HTTP proof.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_permission_http_2026-10-27"></a>
## Permission HTTP acceptance — bounded development probe

Original source: `docs/handoffs/phase2-parallel/PRIMARY_PERMISSION_HTTP_2026-10-27.md`. Retained historical scope/status.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_permission_http_2026-10-27--permission-http-acceptance-bounded-development-probe"></a>
### Permission HTTP acceptance — bounded development probe

Identity: LABOS-P2-PRIMARY. Primary verification and input-validation correction.

MODULE: A1/B3/B4 permission replacement and current-authority enforcement.

FILE: backend/src/routes/auth.js;
backend/src/permission-replacement-http-live-probe.mjs.

CURRENT WRITE PATH: real loopback HTTP -> production JWT authentication ->
permission middleware -> production router -> transactional authority and audit.

WHY IT BYPASSES OFFLINE-FIRST: no new bypass. This tests an existing online
administrative endpoint; no desktop outbox changes.

RISK: actor authority can change after middleware. Also, the old input fallback
silently treated missing/null/non-array overrides as an instruction to clear all.

RECOMMENDED CHANGE: validate the complete authenticated HTTP path with current
authority rechecks and rollback; require explicit array for replacement/clearing.

ACTUAL CHANGE MADE: malformed overrides now return HTTP400
INVALID_PERMISSION_OVERRIDES. Explicit [] remains valid to intentionally clear.
Added real HTTP probe with disposable users, production JWT middleware/router,
and actual PostgreSQL. Pool injection maps route transactions to savepoints inside
an outer transaction so no fixture writes commit. A deterministic connect hook
changes authority after middleware, before transactional recheck.

VERIFICATION: eight scenario groups PASS: authenticated replacement plus audit;
unauthenticated denial; actor disabled after middleware; actor demoted after
middleware; delegated grant revoked after middleware; unheld deny removal blocked;
mandatory audit failure rolls back; malformed bodies preserve existing overrides
while explicit [] clears. Each denied/failing case verifies unchanged target
overrides/audit. All fixtures rolled back. Source mounted read-only into disposable
runner. Development API stayed stopped; database restored stopped. Diff check PASS.
V1 containers, files, databases and installed application unchanged.

STATUS: BOUNDED HTTP CHECK PASS — source not deployed.

Limit: requests/auth/router/SQL are real, but transaction commits are intercepted
as savepoints and the authority race is deterministically injected, not an
independent concurrently committed HTTP request. Earlier two-connection probes
cover database lock exclusion. Reciprocal management requests, other account
writers, coordinated deployment and desktop reconnect remain separate gates.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_v1_presentations_2026-10-26--scope-and-implementation"></a>
#### Scope and implementation

- Shared resource viewer recognizes original `.ppt` / `.pptx` filenames and offers
  **Open in presentation app** in desktop; web retains ordinary download guidance.
- Native command takes only resource/account/session identifiers, checks current
  resource-view permission and session, and resolves the existing authorized local
  file through the same managed-file resolution used by other local viewers.
- Missing local copies fail clearly; there is no direct server-write fallback or
  new download/sync architecture. Existing replication obtains files when online.
- A bounded, separate copy gets a generated temporary directory and fixed safe
  filename. Revision, session and source-path checks repeat before handing it to
  the OS default application. No caller-supplied path or command is executed.
- Shell-open scope retains URL support and adds only the generated Windows path
  pattern ending in `Presentation.ppt` or `Presentation.pptx`; no general file-open
  or execute scope is enabled.
- Successful temporary copies are retained for the external reader. They are
  outside LabOS managed storage, not remotely revocable, and external edits do not
  sync back. UI discloses the separate-copy behavior. No auto cleanup while the
  external app may still be using the file; failed copies are removed.
- No backend, database, outbox or document conversion changes. No executable
  rebuild/install or live-data mutation claimed by source implementation alone.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_project_blank_date_2026-10-26--project-blank-date-sync-diagnosis-october-26"></a>
### Project blank-date sync diagnosis — October 26

Identity: LABOS-P2-PRIMARY. Scope: read-only diagnosis of owner-reported personal V1 error; no repair or deployment yet.

MODULE: Projects; Phase2 B3/B4, shared sync validation.

FILE: backend/src/routes/sync.js, applyProjectEntity create/update field projection; desktop project date-input/write path requires follow-up.

CURRENT WRITE PATH: desktop project edits persisted to V1 SQLite/outbox; sync sends immutable project events; server uses `record[field] ?? null` for SQL parameters. Empty strings survive that expression.

WHY IT BYPASSES OFFLINE-FIRST: this is not a demonstrated transport bypass. It is a local/server value-contract mismatch that prevents queued writes from being accepted. The global sync notification appears on Resources even though the rejected entities are projects.

RISK: repeated retries cannot clear the two changes; later dependent edits may remain blocked. Do not erase queue rows, force ACKs, or reset the database.

RECOMMENDED CHANGE: normalize explicitly blank optional project dates to SQL NULL at the apply boundary without changing the immutable submitted payload or receipt identity. Normalize new local inputs too. Preserve omitted-field semantics and reject genuinely malformed nonblank dates clearly. Test create/update/clear, dependent edits, replay, rollback and real PostgreSQL behavior. Review other date-writing paths separately rather than applying indiscriminate string normalization.

ACTUAL CHANGE MADE: documentation only. SQLite opened read-only with query_only; no payload or acknowledgement edits. Server logs read; no restart/deployment.

VERIFICATION: two pending V1 project update events observed:

- b5389150-b4da-4ee5-840d-dcf1429b6b36: start_date=2026-10-26, due_date=""; 16 recorded attempts.
- 97ad90d3-901f-42ea-b4b3-9ea5946da168: start_date="", due_date=""; 4 recorded attempts.

Both last_error values are `invalid input syntax for type date: ""`. Server source passes empty strings unchanged in project SQL create/update. No document contents, credentials or tokens were included in diagnostics. The pending events are preserved; no full data-integrity claim is inferred from this query.

ordinary leads still submit. Existing current-authority transaction checks,
displayed-plan token checks, native lease/permissions, dirty-plan rejection,

UI changed together; the old installed app cannot expose the new action yet.

skipped). The actual development PostgreSQL date test subsequently passed 2/2;
rollback-only direct approval probe passed blank-date creation, activation,

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_sync_stall_2026-10-25"></a>
## Six pending changes — investigation, October 25

Original source: `docs/handoffs/phase2-parallel/PRIMARY_SYNC_STALL_2026-10-25.md`. Retained historical scope/status.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_sync_stall_2026-10-25--six-pending-changes-investigation-october-25"></a>
### Six pending changes — investigation, October 25

Identity / role: LABOS-P2-PRIMARY, integration and sync-safety review.

MODULE: Sync orchestration / status presentation.

FILE: desktop/src/api/sync.ts; sync-runtime-state.ts;
resource-uploads.ts; components/SyncStatus.tsx; sync-runtime-state.test.mjs.

CURRENT WRITE PATH: Native outbox -> staged file transfer -> sync/push -> verified
receipts -> local acknowledgement. Six October 21 events remain pending: two
resource creates, one resource delete and three updates to one inventory item.

WHY IT BYPASSES OFFLINE-FIRST: No bypass established. The problem is incomplete
delivery/acknowledgement and inadequate diagnostics, not missing local storage.

RISK: Indefinite misleading spinner, delayed authored work, and unsafe manual
queue cleanup if server acceptance is mistaken for locally confirmed completion.

EVIDENCE: Read-only SQLite checks found six owned pending events, no recorded
failures/conflicts and ready file staging entries (0 and 891216 bytes). On
October 24 after login the matching account lease was valid. Server receipt
lookup (including compact UUID normalization) found only the deletion accepted.
Both upload staging records exist but are unpublished. PostgreSQL had no blocked
database query at inspection. Screenshot shows Syncing with six pending, no
conflicts and no successful sync. These facts do not identify the exact blocked
await, nor prove that the empty file is the cause.

RECOMMENDED CHANGE: Surface unexpected run failures instead of allowing the
automatic caller to swallow them while status remains syncing. Display current
stage to locate a genuinely unresolved await. Preserve original IDs and payloads;
do not mark rows synced, rewrite conflicts or force server writes during diagnosis.

ACTUAL CHANGE MADE: Added account-scoped top-level failure publication/backoff,
with normal promise cleanup and rejection preserved. Added transient stages for
queue reads, upload session/status/body/chunk, push, receipt confirmation and pull
steps. Stages are not persisted and clear on non-syncing state/account changes.
No queue or database records changed by the diagnostic patch.

VERIFICATION: All 30 targeted runtime/upload tests passed with the actual API
stopped, including stage reset/restart/account isolation. API restored healthy.
TypeScript/Vite frontend build and diff whitespace check passed; native embedding
build in progress at this checkpoint.
Existing switched-account tests cover suppression of errors from an old login.

STATUS: Diagnostics source implemented; underlying six-event stall NOT FIXED or
verified. Awaiting rebuilt desktop observation. User approved saved-edit restart.
On October 25 the API/database and desktop were no longer running; existing
PostgreSQL/API containers restarted without replacing their data volumes.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_sync_stall_2026-10-25--root-cause-located-in-live-desktop"></a>
#### Root cause located in live desktop

Rebuilt diagnostic desktop restored the existing login. Using the computer-use
skill, observed the sync panel persist at **Confirming server receipts locally**.
The installed Tauri JS SDK constructs the IPC envelope as
`{cmd, callback, error, ...args}`. All four `record_sync_failure` callers supplied
`error: message`, replacing Tauri's numeric error callback with an application
string. This breaks IPC dispatch/response delivery while attempting to report
the first failed receipt; later changes cannot progress and no failure is recorded.

Changed all four callers to `errorMessage` and the Rust command parameter to
`error_message`. Coordinated frontend/native rebuild is required. Added an AST
regression covering every failure-recording call and checking native argument
agreement; 16 runtime/receipt regression cases pass. This fixes the callback
collision, not the underlying server failure(s) that it concealed. No manual ACK,
queue removal, ownership reassignment or payload rewrite is authorized by this fix.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_sync_stall_2026-10-25--follow-up-explicit-null-resource-metadata"></a>
#### Follow-up: explicit null resource metadata

MODULE: Resource creation through sync (primary agent).

FILE: `backend/src/routes/sync.js`; regression suite
`backend/src/routes/sync-resource-create-defaults.test.js`.

CURRENT WRITE PATH: Native staged upload -> immutable outbox create -> server
resource INSERT -> receipt -> local acknowledgement.

WHY IT BYPASSES OFFLINE-FIRST: It does not bypass the outbox; explicit null fields
in native snapshots override PostgreSQL NOT NULL defaults and prevent publishing.

RISK: Retry repeats the same failure indefinitely. The IPC fix exposed it and
allowed four other events to finish, leaving two resource creates pending.

RECOMMENDED CHANGE / ACTUAL CHANGE MADE: Apply category `general`, description
empty string, tags empty array and validated visibility on the create INSERT
projection only. Do not mutate queued payloads, change IDs, or loosen constraints.
Existing explicit metadata is retained. Updates and permission checks unchanged.

VERIFICATION: User screenshot and read-only SQLite diagnostics confirm exactly
the two original create events remain, both failing category NOT NULL (8 attempts
at inspection). Fifteen targeted contract/receipt/media tests passed with the real
API stopped and restored; new tests cover null/missing/explicit metadata and
payload immutability for files/folders. PostgreSQL check and deployment pending.

STATUS: Deployed; awaiting live replay verification.

The opt-in PostgreSQL check passed against the existing database using a temporary
table cloned from public.resources, inside BEGIN/ROLLBACK. All seven cases in that
run passed (six contract cases plus PostgreSQL insert). Candidate image
`labos-api:sync-defaults-20261025`, SHA256
`a231724769862560422156bb2b299475329d5a469738edd4c7e54fbce9609b28`,
was deployed with compose --no-deps --no-build; database/storage volumes unchanged.
API/database/storage health passed at 2026-10-25T13:28:40Z. Immediate read-only
outbox inspection still showed two entries with their previous error and nine
attempts; a post-deployment retry has not yet been verified. Do not claim queue
clearance from build/test success. Also check final state of the earlier deleted
resource during acceptance, not merely receipt counts.
