<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_resource_ordering_2026-10-25"></a>
## Resource create/delete ordering — primary agent

Original source: `docs/handoffs/phase2-parallel/PRIMARY_RESOURCE_ORDERING_2026-10-25.md`. Retained historical scope/status.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_resource_ordering_2026-10-25--resource-createdelete-ordering-primary-agent"></a>
### Resource create/delete ordering — primary agent

Identity: LABOS-P2-PRIMARY; not helper work. V1 safety fix, not phase completion.

MODULE: Resources / synchronization.

FILE: `backend/src/routes/sync.js`; `sync-resource-ordering.test.js` and
`sync-resource-create-defaults.test.js` alongside it.

CURRENT WRITE PATH: Native resource/outbox -> staged bytes -> sync push ->
PostgreSQL transaction + immutable receipt -> native confirmation -> pull.

WHY IT BYPASSES OFFLINE-FIRST: No direct-write bypass. A failed create did not
prevent the same batch's later absent delete from receiving a successful receipt.
Retrying the create after that acknowledgement resurrected a deleted resource.

RISK: Empty outbox can hide incorrect final state and silently lost deletion intent.

RECOMMENDED CHANGE: Never treat absence without a deletion tombstone as proof
of completed deletion. Reject new creates for deleted identities, preserving the
queued work. Serialize different sync mutations for the same resource.

ACTUAL CHANGE MADE:

- Added normalized resource-identity transaction advisory lock for ordinary sync
  resource create/update/delete/attach paths (specialized edit_content/metadata
  paths retain their existing locking).
- Missing resource delete requires a tombstone to return already_deleted;
  otherwise retryable 503 RESOURCE_DELETE_WAITING_FOR_CREATE, with no success
  receipt. Existing desktop failed-receipt behavior preserves/retries the event.
- Create/create_copy rejects tombstones and this account's historical successful
  delete receipts, including older absent-delete acknowledgements. Foreign
  absent-delete receipts cannot poison another account's unused identity.
- Historical successful create receipt replay remains idempotent: it does not
  invoke a new INSERT or resurrect a deleted resource.
- No queued payload rewrite, manual ACK, schema migration, fixture seeding of
  live rows, or cleanup of the actual resurrected resource.

VERIFICATION:

- 19 targeted contract/receipt/media checks passed with actual API stopped and
  restored. Two opt-in PostgreSQL tests skipped in this unit run.
- Candidate real PostgreSQL run: all 12 tests passed (including those two).
  Temporary tables shadow live tables; outer transaction rolled back. The actual
  push handler uses nested savepoints, exercising receipt persistence and status
  classification, not HTTP/auth middleware. Sequence: failed create + delete ->
  both failed/no receipt -> unchanged retry -> create/delete synced -> repeated
  accepted receipts leave resource absent -> new create rejected.
- Also verifies null metadata defaults, UUID lock normalization, tombstoned
  absent delete, owned legacy deletion and foreign-receipt isolation.
- Node syntax and scoped diff whitespace checks passed.

STATUS: Deployed and healthy; live cleanup and full desktop acceptance
remain separate. Candidate `labos-api:resource-ordering-20261025`, SHA256
`030bdf774d21678136f760fb701e1e148e80a3d7b29478d00bd8c82fa2d45c05`.
No desktop rebuild needed. Existing backup remains at
`C:\Users\balik\LabOS-Backups\v1-pilot-20261025`.

BOUNDARIES: This fixes sync resource create/delete ordering, not a claim of an
entire-system tombstone audit. A missing delete with no create ever arriving now
remains pending safely; it is not silently discarded. Actual zero-byte resource
`ac7046e8-a331-4199-af71-0f0564add409` still requires the explicitly requested
repair approval or owner deletion. Nonzero image and all other files untouched.

Post-deployment: API/database/storage healthy at 20:57:41 UTC; read-only desktop
outbox inspection reports zero pending. All 23 rollback-only lifecycle checks
passed again on the deployed image. No claim that these replace desktop CRUD,
offline playback, full-app recovery or cleanup acceptance.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_review_queue_2026-10-24--queued-project-review-source-implementation"></a>
### Queued project review — source implementation

Identity / role: LABOS-P2-PRIMARY. Primary implementation, not helper work.

MODULE: B3/B4 project planning review intentions and synchronization.
FILE: desktop/src-tauri/src/local_project_review.rs; local_db.rs; local_projects.rs;
main.rs; desktop/src/api/projects.ts; ProjectPlanningReview.tsx;
backend/src/project-review-sync.js; project-review-snapshot.js; routes/sync.js;
project-review-sync-live-probe.mjs; adapter/native tests.
CURRENT WRITE PATH: Desktop review -> native authorization/SQLite transaction ->
account-stamped immutable outbox project_review/decision -> ordinary sync push ->
server permission/state check -> transactional decision/event/audit -> existing
sync idempotency receipt. Browser retains HTTP. No desktop HTTP fallback.
WHY IT BYPASSES OFFLINE-FIRST: The prior desktop decision called HTTP directly.
RISK: Unavailable offline reviews, premature local activation, duplicate decisions,
stale approvals and account-crossing pending work.
RECOMMENDED CHANGE: Preserve authored intentions independently from confirmed
project state, validate at both ends, reject stale state and replay exact IDs.
ACTUAL CHANGE MADE: New native command validates active account, cached editor and
lead/admin authority, decision/reason, confirmed review snapshot and project state.
It refuses duplicate pending reviews and pending local project work, then saves
only the outbox row. No optimistic activation or review-status rewrite. Existing
native project read overlays pending/rejected/awaiting-snapshot states, excludes
explicitly dismissed/accepted conflicts without deleting their payloads, and hides
acknowledged pending indicators after the snapshot version changes. UI separates
confirmed status and pending decisions. Conflict retry checks project authority;
stale-version conflicts cannot blindly overwrite. Server uses current active
actor, permissions, lead/admin rules, project lock and expected version; required
audit and decision share the existing sync transaction. Generic post-commit audit
is skipped for this already-audited entity. Receipts expose acknowledgement only.

VERIFICATION: TypeScript and native test compilation PASS. With actual Docker API
confirmed stopped: 37 JavaScript tests and 16 native tests PASS (4 new review queue,
12 existing database regressions). Native review fixtures use isolated in-memory
SQLite, not the user's live cache. Actual PostgreSQL rollback-only handler probe
PASS: missing actor rejected, mismatched token rejected, valid submit/approve and
two audit/event rows. First probe incorrectly expected transaction-local xmin/now
to advance; corrected to an explicit mismatched-token fixture. All fixtures
rolled back. API restored healthy. Syntax and diff whitespace PASS.

STATUS: Source only; NOT ready to declare full acceptance or deploy alone. New
native command requires coordinated desktop/API upgrade. Running application and
API have not been upgraded. No existing database/storage/pending changes removed.

- Restart/reopen persistence and full desktop pending/rejection/ack/pull UI checks.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_review_plan_version_2026-10-24"></a>
## Project review plan version and push replay

Original source: `docs/handoffs/phase2-parallel/PRIMARY_REVIEW_PLAN_VERSION_2026-10-24.md`. Retained historical scope/status.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_review_plan_version_2026-10-24--project-review-plan-version-and-push-replay"></a>
### Project review plan version and push replay

Identity / role: LABOS-P2-PRIMARY. Primary implementation and verification, not helper work.

MODULE: B3/B4 project planning review synchronization.

FILE: backend/src/migrations/20261024_project_plan_revision.sql;
project-review-snapshot.js; project-review-sync.js;
project-review-sync-live-probe.mjs; project-review-push-live-probe.mjs.

CURRENT WRITE PATH: Account-owned native outbox -> existing sync push transaction
-> current authority and expected plan revision -> decision/event/audit/receipt.

WHY IT BYPASSES OFFLINE-FIRST: No new bypass. The preceding project-row token did
not detect independent child edits, so an offline approval could reference stale
plan contents even when the parent project row had not changed.

RISK: Approval of changed demand or work; duplicate review events after retry;
partial approval if receipt persistence fails.

RECOMMENDED CHANGE: A monotonic plan revision advanced transactionally by relevant
parent/child changes, plus replay checks through the actual push handler.

ACTUAL CHANGE MADE: Additive plan_revision and triggers on project rows and eleven
plan child tables. Child writes touch the parent revision; moves touch both
parents. Timestamp-only child updates do not invalidate the revision. Experiment
and task child records resolve their project through their parent. Snapshot and
review validation now use plan-v1:<revision>. Old pending tokens are not rewritten:
they will require a fresh review on mismatch. Added an opt-in source-in-memory
push-handler probe using real PostgreSQL, with route transactions represented by
savepoints inside one rollback-only transaction. No deployed code changed.

VERIFICATION: Seven PostgreSQL scenario groups PASS:

1. Migration executes twice; child insert/update/move/delete advances revisions,
   while a no-op/timestamp-only update does not.
2. Nested experiment observations and measurements advance the revision; deleting
   their experiment also advances it.
3. Disabled actor rejected despite a stale admin role in the request context.
4. Actual push submit/replay creates one review event, audit and receipt.
5. Changed payload, device and user cannot reuse an accepted receipt.
6. BOM change rejects stale approval without creating event/audit/receipt.
7. Injected receipt failure rolls back approval; retry succeeds once; another
   new-ID approval is rejected by state validation.

All PostgreSQL fixtures and migration effects rolled back. With the actual Docker
API confirmed stopped, 8 JavaScript decision tests and 4 existing native review
queue tests PASS. Native tests used isolated in-memory SQLite. API restarted in
finally; the first immediate health request raced startup, subsequent health
request succeeded. JavaScript syntax and tracked diff whitespace checks PASS.

STATUS: Source implemented with focused verification; NOT deployed or full
workflow acceptance. PostgreSQL data, storage and pending changes preserved.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_review_plan_version_2026-10-24--still-open-before-workflow-closure"></a>
#### Still open before workflow closure

- Concurrent database connections/lock ordering, not simulated savepoints.
- Durable commit, transport response loss, desktop restart and delayed pull.
- HTTP transactional authority source follow-up is now implemented; see
  PRIMARY_REVIEW_AUTHORITY_2026-10-24.md. Remaining concurrency boundaries there
  still prevent declaring full workflow acceptance.
- Nested native dirty-work detection and integrated pending/conflict UI checks.
- Review coverage of additional plan-relevant relationships as part of B3/B4;
  eleven registered child tables are not a claim that every project-linked
  record or external resource-content change invalidates approval.
- Coordinated API migration/native build and desktop acceptance. None performed
  in this batch. Phase 2 remains open.

## Native displayed review version and durable queue

Original source: `docs/handoffs/phase2-parallel/PRIMARY_REVIEW_NATIVE_PERSISTENCE_2026-10-24.md`. Retained historical scope/status.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_review_native_persistence_2026-10-24--native-displayed-review-version-and-durable-queue"></a>
### Native displayed review version and durable queue

Identity / role: LABOS-P2-PRIMARY. Primary implementation, not helper work.

MODULE: B3/B4 native project review and pending decision persistence.

FILE: desktop/src-tauri/src/local_project_review.rs; desktop/src/api/projects.ts;
desktop/src/api/project-reservation-boundaries.test.mjs;
desktop/src/components/ProjectPlanningReview.tsx.

CURRENT WRITE PATH: UI displayed token -> native account/authority/state/token
validation inside SQLite transaction -> immutable account-owned outbox intention.
The ordinary sync pipeline remains responsible for delivery and acknowledgement.

WHY IT BYPASSES OFFLINE-FIRST: No transport bypass. The native command previously
selected the latest cached token at save time instead of receiving the version
the user saw. A background refresh could silently replace the reviewed version.

RISK: Queueing approval for a plan the user had not reviewed; losing or duplicating
pending authored notes across restart or repeated acknowledgements.

RECOMMENDED CHANGE: Require the displayed token at the native boundary and verify
durability using a file-backed SQLite database, not only in-memory fixtures.

ACTUAL CHANGE MADE: Required expected_token on ReviewIntentInput. Native save
rejects absent/empty/mismatched versions before writing the outbox. Adapter sends
the displayed token unchanged for desktop and browser; no HTTP fallback. Added
Refresh review control so a user can reload the snapshot without clearing their
typed note. Existing outbox payloads are not rewritten or discarded.

VERIFICATION: Native test compilation PASS. With actual Docker API stopped:
26 adapter tests, 6 native review tests and 12 local-database tests PASS (44 total).
New stale-display case verifies no row is queued until the matching fresh token
is supplied. New unique file-backed SQLite fixture closes/reopens after queueing,
uses the production mark_changes_synced helper twice, closes/reopens again,
verifies awaiting_snapshot without local activation, supplies a newer snapshot,
then closes/reopens and verifies the pending indicator clears while the original
payload and single outbox row remain. The disposable fixture was removed after
success; the user's SQLite database was never modified by this test. API restored
healthy. TypeScript and diff whitespace checks PASS.

STATUS: Source only; no desktop rebuild/restart or API deployment performed.
This is durable local queue/ACK coverage, NOT full live transport reconnect or
UI acceptance. The new required native argument requires coordinated frontend
and native deployment. Existing saved decisions and all user data are preserved.

- Live native desktop -> PostgreSQL push -> ACK -> pull across process restart
  and connection loss, including rejection and account switching.
- Nested dirty-work cases: inspected current nested create/update/delete helpers
  and confirmed they include project_id; dedicated regression coverage remains.
- Concurrent child-plan editing/approval and full permission HTTP integration.
- Coordinated source deployment, then desktop acceptance. Phase 2 remains open.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_review_browser_version_2026-10-24"></a>
## Browser review version and permission-writer serialization

Original source: `docs/handoffs/phase2-parallel/PRIMARY_REVIEW_BROWSER_VERSION_2026-10-24.md`. Retained historical scope/status.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_review_browser_version_2026-10-24--browser-review-version-and-permission-writer-serialization"></a>
### Browser review version and permission-writer serialization

Identity / role: LABOS-P2-PRIMARY. Primary implementation, not helper work.

MODULE: B3/B4 project review; permission override replacement.

FILE: backend/src/routes/projects.js; routes/auth.js;
project-review-push-live-probe.mjs; project-review-lock-live-probe.mjs;
project-review-authority.test.js; desktop/src/api/projects.ts;
desktop/src/api/project-reservation-boundaries.test.mjs;
desktop/src/components/ProjectPlanningReview.tsx.

CURRENT WRITE PATH: Browser review read returns a coherent versioned snapshot;
decision submits that version to the HTTP transaction. Native desktop retains
its existing local outbox path. Permission replacement locks the target account
before deleting or inserting overrides.

WHY IT BYPASSES OFFLINE-FIRST: No new native bypass. The browser HTTP route lacked
an expected version; an approval could act on a newer plan than the screen shown.
The existing permissions writer did not coordinate with review's account lock,
allowing insertion of a previously absent deny during a review transaction.

RISK: Stale browser approvals and concurrent override changes escaping row locks
on existing overrides.

RECOMMENDED CHANGE: Carry the displayed snapshot token; require it under the
project lock. Coordinate permission replacement through the target account lock.

ACTUAL CHANGE MADE: HTTP GET uses the single-statement review snapshot reader.
HTTP POST rejects missing/mismatched expected_token with REVIEW_VERSION_CONFLICT
after current authorization. Browser adapter refuses unversioned decisions and
submits the UI's loaded token unchanged. Errors leave the component note intact.
Permission replacement takes users FOR UPDATE before touching overrides and
rechecks target existence/admin protection after acquiring the lock. It therefore
conflicts with review's users FOR SHARE even when the override row is absent.

VERIFICATION: Nine real PostgreSQL handler scenario groups PASS, including missing
and stale browser tokens rejected with unchanged review/event/audit state and a
fresh-token success. Source-in-memory probe fixtures/migration rolled back. Two
real connections verify account FOR UPDATE (the permission writer's first lock)
blocks during review, along with project/account updates; all writes rolled back.
The actual permission HTTP route's lock-before-override order also has a source
regression assertion; the full permission HTTP request was not exercised here.
With actual Docker API stopped, 57 focused JavaScript tests PASS, including native
adapter no-HTTP-fallback behavior. API restored healthy. TypeScript, JavaScript
syntax and diff whitespace checks PASS.

STATUS: Source only, not deployed. Existing data/storage/pending work preserved.
Older browser clients without a token will fail closed after deployment and need
the coordinated frontend update. No migration committed by these tests.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_review_browser_version_2026-10-24--remaining-acceptance"></a>
#### Remaining acceptance

- Full concurrent plan-child edit/approval and permission-request integration,
  including actor-side permission-management authorization changes and lock order.
- Native displayed-snapshot versus latest cached-token behavior, nested dirty
  work detection, durable restart/reconnect, delayed pull and UI acceptance.
- Coordinated API/native/frontend deployment. Phase 2 is not declared complete.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_review_authority_2026-10-24"></a>
## Transactional review authority

Original source: `docs/handoffs/phase2-parallel/PRIMARY_REVIEW_AUTHORITY_2026-10-24.md`. Retained historical scope/status.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_review_authority_2026-10-24--transactional-review-authority"></a>
### Transactional review authority

Identity / role: LABOS-P2-PRIMARY. Primary implementation, not helper work.

MODULE: B3/B4 review authorization and sync safety.

FILE: backend/src/project-review-authority.js; middleware/permissions.js;
project-review-sync.js; routes/projects.js; project-review-authority.test.js;
project-review-push-live-probe.mjs; project-review-lock-live-probe.mjs.

CURRENT WRITE PATH: HTTP and outbox sync both lock the project, validate current
authority on the same transaction connection, then write decision/event/audit.
Sync retains its version and receipt checks. HTTP remains an online browser path.

WHY IT BYPASSES OFFLINE-FIRST: No new desktop bypass. HTTP previously checked
authorization before starting its transaction. Sync checked the account inside
the transaction but fetched permission overrides through the shared pool.

RISK: Stale role/permissions between middleware and the decision; authorization
reads outside the transaction; response projection using cached permissions.

RECOMMENDED CHANGE: Share current transactional authority between HTTP and sync.

ACTUAL CHANGE MADE: Shared helper checks active account, current role, overrides,
lead/owner membership and restricted-project edit grant. Existing rows are read
FOR SHARE. getUserPermissions now accepts an optional transaction client and
locked-read option; existing callers keep their original behavior. HTTP performs
the authority check after its project lock and uses freshly checked permissions
for response projection. No permission baseline changed. Added unit cases and
extended the actual route-handler PostgreSQL probe to test stale HTTP context.

VERIFICATION:

- Eight PostgreSQL rollback-only push/HTTP scenario groups PASS. HTTP terminal
  handler rejects disabled and demoted accounts even with cached admin context.
  The harness intentionally bypasses middleware; full HTTP auth transport is not
  claimed tested. All temporary migration effects and fixtures rolled back.
- Separate real PostgreSQL connections: competing project and account no-op
  updates hit lock timeout while review holds its locks, then succeed after
  rollback. Every attempted update rolled back. No fixtures were committed.
- Actual Docker API stopped: 30 authority, decision and permissions tests PASS.
  API restarted and health confirmed. Syntax and diff whitespace checks PASS.
- Expected HTTP rejections initially printed large data-URL stack traces from
  the in-memory harness; probe logging now summarizes the error code instead.

STATUS: Source only, not deployed. Existing data/storage/outbox preserved.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_review_authority_2026-10-24--remaining-boundaries"></a>
#### Remaining boundaries

Follow-up: browser tokens and target-account permission-writer locking are now
implemented in source. See PRIMARY_REVIEW_BROWSER_VERSION_2026-10-24.md for current
evidence and remaining integration limits; the bullets below record this batch's
original boundaries, not a claim that the follow-up was deployed.

- FOR SHARE protects existing rows, not insertion of a previously absent deny
  override or other predicate changes. Review authorization versus permission
  writers still needs a coordinated serialization-contract check.
- Two-connection test proves project/account row-lock exclusion, not full
  concurrent plan-child editing/approval with the new migration. Lock ordering,
  durable commit/reconnect, delayed pull and native UI acceptance remain open.
- Browser HTTP reviews do not yet send an expected plan snapshot token. Current
  authorization is now rechecked, but stale browser-screen approval is not solved
  by this change. Do not equate authority alignment with whole-workflow closure.
- Native dirty-work detection and coordinated desktop/API deployment remain.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_sync_runtime_isolation_2026-10-23"></a>
## Sync runtime status and retry isolation

Original source: `docs/handoffs/phase2-parallel/PRIMARY_SYNC_RUNTIME_ISOLATION_2026-10-23.md`. Retained historical scope/status.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_sync_runtime_isolation_2026-10-23--sync-runtime-status-and-retry-isolation"></a>
### Sync runtime status and retry isolation

Identity / role: LABOS-P2-PRIMARY. Primary implementation, not helper sign-off.

MODULE: A1 sync-session isolation and operational retry state.

FILE: desktop/src/api/sync-runtime-state.ts and test; desktop/src/api/sync.ts.

CURRENT WRITE PATH: Operational status/backoff only, persisted to account-keyed
localStorage v2 records. Ordinary native SQLite/outbox and server writes unchanged.

WHY IT BYPASSES OFFLINE-FIRST: No transport bypass. Previous operational status
and retry keys were installation-global; late error handlers could publish after
account switching, and an active sync promise could be returned to another login.

RISK: Cross-account error display/backoff contamination, stale same-account login
callbacks, and misleading completion from another account's in-flight run.

RECOMMENDED CHANGE: Scope operational persistence by account and updates by full
login generation/token identity. Never adopt unowned historical status into an
account. Keep one sync run at a time and reject new-login joining of an old run.

ACTUAL CHANGE MADE: Added account-keyed state store, session-checked publish/retry
schedule/clear, bounded persisted delay, corruption/storage-failure tolerance and
auth-event refresh. Tokens are used in memory for session checks, not persisted
in the status record. Old v1 status/retry records remain untouched but unread.
Sync captures its session before preflight, verifies it after the awaited legacy
queue read, and uses generation-aware session checks. Another login gets an
explicit retry-shortly error until the previous run finishes, not its promise.

VERIFICATION: TypeScript PASS. 25 focused tests PASS while Docker API was confirmed
stopped; original API restarted in finally. Tests include store restart/account
isolation, logout, stale generation, unowned legacy records, corrupt/unavailable
storage, bounded delays and actual sync.ts execution with mocked native preflight
and delayed pending-queue failure. These are not full native/HTTP/two-login GUI
acceptance. API/database/storage health and diff whitespace checks PASS.

STATUS: Source-only, awaiting the next coordinated frontend/native deployment and
integrated login/reconnect acceptance. No backend migration or data removal.
This is not encryption of localStorage, nor a complete native authorization audit.
No A1 parent closure claimed.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_sync_preflight_2026-10-23"></a>
## Fail-closed local sync preflight

Original source: `docs/handoffs/phase2-parallel/PRIMARY_SYNC_PREFLIGHT_2026-10-23.md`. Retained historical scope/status.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_sync_preflight_2026-10-23--fail-closed-local-sync-preflight"></a>
### Fail-closed local sync preflight

Identity / role: LABOS-P2-PRIMARY. Primary implementation.

MODULE: A1/A2 local queue preflight and legacy-owner protection.

FILE: desktop/src/api/sync.ts; sync-runtime-state.test.mjs.

CURRENT WRITE PATH: Normal native SQLite/outbox and server reconciliation remain
unchanged. Preflight reads the shared strict native-status adapter before reading
pending events or starting transfers/push/pulls.

WHY IT BYPASSES OFFLINE-FIRST: Previous count helpers caught local-read errors and
returned zero. Preflight consequently treated an unreadable owner-status count as
proof that no unattributed changes existed and continued.

RISK: Unsafe continuation when local ownership status is unknown; false empty
queue reporting; repeated immediate retries when local storage is failing.

RECOMMENDED CHANGE: Propagate missing/malformed/failed reads. Stop sync before
pending-event reads/server work, record a session-bound error and apply backoff.
An explicit retry must repeat preflight, never bypass it.

ACTUAL CHANGE MADE: Existing exported count helpers now delegate to strict
account/session-checked reads and no longer return zero on error. Conflict count
uses the account-bound conflict list. Preflight catches local-read failures only
after verifying the original session, publishes a specific failure, schedules
retry and returns without progressing. Positive unattributed counts continue to
pause sync; no adoption, deletion or modification of those records occurs.

VERIFICATION: TypeScript PASS; 28 focused tests PASS with actual Docker API
confirmed stopped, original API restarted in finally, health API/database/storage
OK. New tests cover failed/malformed preflight, automatic backoff versus explicit
retry, positive legacy count, and error propagation through all count helpers.
The sync tests execute sync.ts with mocked native responses, not full native/HTTP
or GUI acceptance. Diff whitespace PASS.

STATUS: Source-only, to deploy with the preceding runtime-isolation batch.
No migration/data reset, no parent A1/A2 closure or full offline certification.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_review_atomicity_2026-10-23"></a>
## Review decision transaction foundation

Original source: `docs/handoffs/phase2-parallel/PRIMARY_REVIEW_ATOMICITY_2026-10-23.md`. Retained historical scope/status.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_review_atomicity_2026-10-23--review-decision-transaction-foundation"></a>
### Review decision transaction foundation

Identity / role: LABOS-P2-PRIMARY; primary implementation, not helper work.

MODULE: B3/B4 planning review decision transaction.
FILE: backend/src/project-review-decision.js; backend/src/routes/projects.js;
backend/src/project-review-decision.test.js; backend/src/project-review-live-probe.mjs.
CURRENT WRITE PATH: Existing authorized HTTP route locks project, calls shared
decision helper, then commits. No desktop queue enabled in this batch.
WHY IT BYPASSES OFFLINE-FIRST: Desktop review decisions still call HTTP directly.
This prerequisite fixes atomicity before adding replay; it does not close that
bypass. Previously review committed before a non-required audit write.
RISK: Successful review without its required audit record. Contrary to an earlier
investigation note, the default audit helper swallows errors rather than failing
the HTTP request; this missing-audit risk is the verified defect.
RECOMMENDED CHANGE: Shared transaction-owned decision/event/mandatory audit write,
then authorized idempotent outbox application with expected-state checks.
ACTUAL CHANGE MADE: Shared helper validates decision/note/state and writes project,
event and required audit through the same client. HTTP route retains existing
authorization and project lock, commits only after audit succeeds, and returns
structured validation/conflict errors. No local state or outbox rewriting.

lifecycle increment, invalid reason and repeated-state rejection; forced audit
failure followed by rollback leaves neither decision nor event/audit. All fixture
writes rolled back. First probe attempt failed on module URL resolution before
database execution; corrected attempt passed. Eight helper tests plus 24 adapter
checks PASS with actual API stopped. API restarted; initial health request raced
startup, subsequent health OK. Syntax and diff whitespace PASS.
STATUS: Source-only; not deployed. Probe directly exercises the helper, not HTTP
authorization or concurrent requests. Native outbox intentions, transactional
authorization recheck, stale-snapshot/ABA protection, replay idempotency and UI
pending/conflict reconciliation remain open. Duplicate-state rejection is NOT

## Project recorded-history deletion protection

Original source: `docs/handoffs/phase2-parallel/PRIMARY_PROJECT_RECORDED_HISTORY_2026-10-22.md`. Retained historical scope/status.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_project_recorded_history_2026-10-22--project-recorded-history-deletion-protection"></a>
### Project recorded-history deletion protection

Identity / role: LABOS-P2-PRIMARY. Primary implementation and review, not helper work.

MODULE: B4 project lifecycle/history, with B2 salvage and B5 finance provenance.

FILE: backend/src/project-lifecycle.js; project-lifecycle-live-probe.mjs;
custody-sync-live-probe.mjs. Existing sync and browser project delete handlers
already call this shared guard under their transaction/project lock.

CURRENT WRITE PATH: Desktop delete intention -> SQLite/outbox -> server project
delete transaction; browser delete -> same server guard. This batch changes only
the authoritative deletion boundary, not the native queue or rejection recovery.

WHY IT BYPASSES OFFLINE-FIRST: No new write bypass. Existing deletion could detach
transactions/purchases/salvage via SET NULL and cascade-delete scientific evidence.
An outbox alone does not make these destructive server effects safe.

RISK: Loss of project provenance and experiment/results history, including records
linked only through an experiment rather than a direct project ID.

RECOMMENDED CHANGE: Reject hard deletion when recorded history exists; archive
instead. Keep empty projects deletable and retain existing inventory guard codes.

ACTUAL CHANGE MADE:
- Protect transactions (including zero amounts), purchase batches and salvage.
- Protect experiment execution markers, inline results/observations/conclusions,
  measurements, observations and revision history even if current results cleared.
- Protect findings, lab results and engineering calculations through direct project
  or experiment references; protect engineering test execution/results/conclusions.
- Lock existing experiments/tests NOWAIT before inspection. Busy writers return a
  retryable conflict rather than waiting on an inverted parent/child lock order.
- Return PROJECT_RECORDED_HISTORY_PROTECTED (409); no deletion or tombstone follows.
- No migration, stock/financial adjustment, automatic archive or data cleanup.

VERIFICATION:
- Existing real PostgreSQL, source injected in memory: 23 focused checks PASS;
  includes 11 added independent history cases. Fixture transaction rolled back.
- Expanded real PostgreSQL sync/browser-handler harness: 29 PASS, 0 FAIL;
  rollback verified. Includes financial sync rejection without receipt/tombstone
  and browser scientific-history rejection retaining measurements.
- JavaScript syntax checks passed. Expected browser rejection logging is now
  suppressed only for its specific error code in the harness to avoid data-URL
  stack noise; other errors still print. Existing pg concurrency warning remains.

STATUS: IMPLEMENTED — AWAITING DEPLOYMENT AND INTEGRATED VERIFICATION, bounded
server history guard only. No API update or desktop restart in this batch.
HTTP/auth middleware, native rejected-delete recovery, GUI and simultaneous-client
lock/contention cases not certified. No offline capability code changed, so this
batch did not stop the API or claim new desktop outage evidence. Direct child
deletion policies and broader B4 recovery/revision/review work remain open.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_project_delete_recovery_2026-10-22"></a>
## Native rejected-project deletion recovery

Original source: `docs/handoffs/phase2-parallel/PRIMARY_PROJECT_DELETE_RECOVERY_2026-10-22.md`. Retained historical scope/status.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_project_delete_recovery_2026-10-22--native-rejected-project-deletion-recovery"></a>
### Native rejected-project deletion recovery

Identity / role: LABOS-P2-PRIMARY; primary work, not helper acceptance.

MODULE: B4 project rejection/recovery; A2 authored-work retention.

FILE: desktop/src-tauri/src/local_db.rs.

CURRENT WRITE PATH: Local project deletion saves the complete project in its
immutable outbox payload and removes it from the visible local project snapshot.
Pending root changes block replacement by project pulls. Server rejection creates
a sync conflict; explicit resolution retires the deletion and permits a later
authorized project pull.

WHY IT BYPASSES OFFLINE-FIRST: No transport bypass. The previous generic resolver
allowed blind retries of protected history deletions and lifecycle conflicts;
retired deletion snapshots existed only in the outbox, without a recovery record.

RISK: Repeated permanent rejection and confusion about invisible projects; an
unsafe restoration from old payloads could revive obsolete access or overwrite
newer child work. A storage failure must not retire the only pending intention.

RECOMMENDED CHANGE: Block blind protected-history/lifecycle-conflict retry. Preserve
authored deletion evidence atomically before explicit retirement; await an
authorized server pull for live data rather than restoring old permissions.

ACTUAL CHANGE MADE:
- Keep local rejects PROJECT_INVENTORY_HISTORY_PROTECTED and
  PROJECT_RECORDED_HISTORY_PROTECTED deletions with archive/reconciliation advice.
- PROJECT_LIFECYCLE_CONFLICT requires review/new decision, not an automatic
  revision overwrite or identical stale retry.
- Accept server and Dismiss preserve account/device/change/project identity,
  original payload and resolution in an account-scoped recovery record within
  the same transaction that retires the deletion and resolves the conflict.
- Original outbox payload remains unchanged. Other pending child changes are not
  retired. No cached project/permissions are restored from recovery evidence.
- If recovery storage fails, the deletion and conflict both remain pending.

VERIFICATION: Native test compilation passed. Actual labos-labos-api-1 container
stopped and its running state confirmed false; all 8 local_db tests PASS, including
4 added tests covering protected retry, payload/authorship retention, account
isolation, storage-failure atomicity and disk SQLite close/reopen durability.
PostgreSQL/storage were not stopped or reset. API restarted in finally; health
endpoint confirms API/database/storage OK afterward. Diff whitespace check passed.

STATUS: IMPLEMENTED — AWAITING DEPLOYMENT AND INTEGRATED VERIFICATION for this
bounded native resolver behavior. No production binary rebuild/restart or API
deployment in this batch. These are native tests, not full GUI acceptance. Recovery
listing/export UI, dependent child reconciliation, authoritative reconnect/pull,
revocation scenarios and concurrent clients remain open. B4/A2 not closed.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_conflict_account_fence_2026-10-22--conflict-accountsession-boundary"></a>
### Conflict account/session boundary

Identity / role: LABOS-P2-PRIMARY.

MODULE: A1/B4 conflict inspection and explicit recovery resolution.

FILE: desktop/src/api/sync-conflict-client.ts and test; api/sync.ts;
src-tauri/src/local_db.rs; SyncStatus.tsx; SyncConflictsPage.tsx.

WHY IT BYPASSES OFFLINE-FIRST: No transport bypass, but previously the read could
return old-account data after an account switch, and commands did not specify the
account intended by the requesting UI.

RISK: Late conflict response disclosure or misleading resolution success under
another session. Global/page-level account-switch display lifetime is a separate
remaining acceptance obligation; these guards do not certify all rendered state.

RECOMMENDED CHANGE: Capture account/session, bind native commands to the expected
account, reject late responses and recheck mutation identity inside the transaction.

ACTUAL CHANGE MADE: Dedicated adapter binds expectedAccountId for both commands;
signed-out calls fail before IPC, changed sessions reject results, native failures
do not fall back to HTTP. Native list checks expected account before/after reading;
resolution checks it under the immediate transaction. Failed conflict refreshes
clear displayed conflict arrays. Existing native payload redaction is unchanged.

VERIFICATION: TypeScript and native test build PASS. With actual Docker API stopped,
11 adapter/presentation tests and 9 native local_db tests PASS. API restored and
health endpoint API/database/storage OK. Native tests include expected-account
mismatch with no retirement/recovery writes. Adapter checks model session switches;
they are not two-login desktop acceptance. Diff whitespace checks PASS.

STATUS: IMPLEMENTED — AWAITING DEPLOYMENT/INTEGRATED VERIFICATION. UI and native
commands must ship together (expectedAccountId is required). Existing desktop
executable launched on owner request, PID 9792, confirmed responding; it is the
October 21 build and does NOT contain this source batch. No working data reset,
production binary replacement or migration. Recovery listing/export still open.

reservation for non-returnable inventory. It rejects equipment/instrument/tool
consumption, recipient/serial ambiguity, and invalid remaining quantities. Stock
arithmetic uses thousandths; stock, reservation quantity, fulfillment history,
audit and receipt remain in the broker transaction. No custody record is created.
Existing checkout and settlement paths are preserved.

outer rollback verified. Three added checks cover consumption/replay/no custody,
receipt-write rollback, excessive quantity and returnable-item rejection. Initial
fixture assertion incorrectly expected no version change after deliberate item
type edits; fixture isolated with a savepoint, then full batch rerun successfully.
Syntax checks and diff whitespace check passed. Probe uses real handlers with a
request adapter, not HTTP/authentication middleware or simultaneous clients.

stable submission identity, stopped-API acceptance and live round-trip remain
open. API remained running for the PostgreSQL checks; no offline claim is made

- Added on-disk SQLite tests for request persistence across ACK/reopen, no premature
  stock authority, pending release issue blocking, duplicate review blocking,
  outbox-failure rollback, and rejected-review preservation/blocking.
- Added adapter tests proving native request/review paths do not fall back to HTTP.

34 native inventory tests and 4 project regression tests passed. One live-server
inventory test was deliberately ignored in the offline batch. First native compile

failed, outer rollback verified. Handler probe excludes transport/auth middleware
and independent simultaneous clients. Recovery-block clearing is implemented in
the project pull transaction, but its complete live UI lifecycle still needs
acceptance testing. No production data was reset or replaced.

round-trip acceptance, consumable fulfillment parity and wider Phase 2 acceptance

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_project_lifecycle_2026-10-21"></a>
## Project cancellation, archive and inventory settlement batch

Original source: `docs/handoffs/phase2-parallel/PRIMARY_PROJECT_LIFECYCLE_2026-10-21.md`. Retained historical scope/status.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_project_lifecycle_2026-10-21--project-cancellation-archive-and-inventory-settlement-batch"></a>
### Project cancellation, archive and inventory settlement batch

Identity / role: primary agent; not helper work.

MODULE: B4 lifecycle propagation, B1 custody, B3 connected reservation authority.

FILE: `backend/src/project-lifecycle.js`, migration `20261021_project_lifecycle.sql`,
project/sync routes, inventory apply, permission projection; desktop native project
and reservation writers, project API types and project overview/register pages;
PostgreSQL lifecycle and custody-sync probes.

CURRENT WRITE PATH: Native project patch -> SQLite project snapshot plus immutable
outbox -> transactional server lifecycle apply -> authoritative project pull.
Browser update uses the same lifecycle helper in its existing API transaction.

WHY IT BYPASSES OFFLINE-FIRST: No new bypass. Previously project status changed
without reservation propagation, archive status or a separate settlement summary.

RISK: Old offline lifecycle decisions can overwrite newer decisions; closing a
project must not fabricate stock returns or erase outstanding custody, tasks,
results, consumption or financial history. Receipt/audit failure must not leave a
partially released project. Reservation/project lock inversions must not wait forever.

RECOMMENDED CHANGE: Fence lifecycle changes with revisions, release unused
allocations only, retain physical history, and distinguish last server inventory
settlement from project status and from unconfirmed local intentions.

ACTUAL CHANGE MADE:
- Additive lifecycle revision column and status-constraint extension for archived.
  Trigger advances lifecycle revision on status changes, including other existing
  server writers. No data reset or automatic archive.
- Cancel/completed/archive transitions release confirmed unused reservations and
  reject still-pending requests; quantities/fulfillment and custody remain intact.
  Reopening does not resurrect reservations. Tasks/experiments are not auto-finished.
- Expected revision required for server status transitions; native revision is
  advanced provisionally, with pending marker and unknown settlement. Native save
  transaction rechecks the stored lifecycle base before replacing the project.
  Cached rows without revision must synchronize before a status change.
- Server helper uses NOWAIT reservation locks under the project lock; contention
  rejects for retry rather than waiting on an inverted reservation/project lock.
- Sync lifecycle audit and receipt are transactional. Browser project update and
  reservation request audits now participate in their write transactions.
- Browser request/confirmation/fulfillment check project state under transaction
  locks; new unreserved checkout/consumption also checks open project state.
  Existing custody settlements remain possible after closure.
- Authorized project detail/pull includes inventory-only settlement counts. A
  project with outstanding custody is unsettled even when archived. No cross-unit
  quantity total or financial-settlement claim is made.
- Overview exposes Archived, a pending lifecycle message, last-server inventory
  settlement and explicit physical-work boundaries. Register recognizes Archived.
  Form retains expected revision while editing; native patch fields are allowlisted.

VERIFICATION:
- Existing PostgreSQL focused helper batch: 12 PASS, rollback verified, including
  stale revision, rollback, cancellation, outstanding archived custody, reopening
  without allocation restoration and unchanged physical quantities.
- Full source-in-memory PostgreSQL sync/browser handler batch: 27 PASS, 0 FAIL,
  rollback verified. Includes receipt failure, duplicate replay, revision conflict
  and browser archive/settlement parity. HTTP/auth middleware not exercised.
- With Docker API stopped: 5 native project and 38 inventory tests PASS; two
  opt-in live cases ignored. Native test build succeeded. The transaction-level
  lifecycle-base check additionally compiles; dedicated competing-writer acceptance
  is still required.
- 7 reservation adapter checks PASS. TypeScript initially identified missing
  archived register labels/colors; fixed and TypeScript rerun passed. JavaScript
  syntax and diff checks passed. Existing harness emits a pg concurrency deprecation
  warning, not a failed check.
- API restored healthy. Migration and fixture data were applied only inside
  rollback-only tests, not permanently deployed. No working records replaced.

STATUS: Core cancellation/archive/inventory-settlement implementation exists in
source; awaiting coordinated API migration/native/UI deployment and integrated
acceptance. Do not mark parent B4 CLOSED. Full financial/results deletion protection,
other revision paths, queued project-plan review, detailed recovery presentation,
stale/in-flight snapshot ordering and concurrent-client lifecycle races remain
separate B4 obligations. This does not certify whole-project financial settlement.

DEPLOYMENT: Update API with the additive migration and rebuild desktop/UI together.
Preserve PostgreSQL/storage/SQLite/outboxes. Refresh project snapshots before
testing lifecycle edits on older cached rows. No restart or deployment performed
in this batch; request saved-edit confirmation before closing the desktop.

Original source: `docs/handoffs/phase2-parallel/PRIMARY_PROJECT_HISTORY_GUARD_2026-10-21.md`. Retained historical scope/status.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_project_history_guard_2026-10-21--project-inventory-history-protection"></a>
### Project inventory history protection

Identity / role: primary agent, not helper work.

MODULE: B4 project lifecycle; B1 custody provenance.

FILE: `backend/src/project-lifecycle.js`, `backend/src/routes/projects.js`,
`backend/src/routes/sync.js`, `backend/src/project-lifecycle-live-probe.mjs`,
`backend/src/custody-sync-live-probe.mjs`.

CURRENT WRITE PATH: Desktop deletion intention reaches transactional sync apply;
browser deletion uses the existing transactional project DELETE route. Both now
call the same guard after locking the project and before deleting anything.

WHY IT BYPASSES OFFLINE-FIRST: No new bypass. The defect is destructive lifecycle
behavior: custody project references use ON DELETE SET NULL, losing provenance.
Fulfillment references can instead cause opaque database errors. Explicitly
rejecting deletion preserves history and returns a meaningful conflict code.

RISK: Outstanding and settled custody, unreserved movements and reservation
fulfillment history must remain associated with their originating project.

RECOMMENDED CHANGE: Refuse deletion of projects with inventory history; preserve
them while cancellation, archive and settlement workflows are completed.

ACTUAL CHANGE MADE: Shared PROJECT_INVENTORY_HISTORY_PROTECTED (409) guard for any
project custody, stock movement or reservation fulfillment. Browser error response
preserves the conflict code. Sync rejection occurs before tombstones or successful
receipts. No stock adjustment, history deletion, schema migration or deployment.
Extended source-in-memory probe supports loading the current helper without
overwriting the deployed API.

VERIFICATION: Existing PostgreSQL, rollback-only fixtures: 6 focused checks PASS
(empty project allowed; outstanding custody; settled custody; unreserved movements;
fulfillment without custody/project-linked movement; no stock effects). Initial
fixture omitted mandatory movement quantity_before/after; corrected and full
focused batch rerun. Full real sync-handler batch: 25 PASS, 0 FAIL, rollback
verified, including protected deletion with no tombstone or success receipt.
JavaScript syntax and diff checks passed. No working data reset or replacement.
The handler harness bypasses HTTP/auth middleware. PostgreSQL emitted a query
concurrency deprecation warning from the existing harness; not a test failure.

STATUS: IMPLEMENTED, source-level PostgreSQL checks passed; deployment and browser/
native end-to-end acceptance pending. Does not certify deletion of projects with
other history (finance/results), child-record deletion, archive support, lifecycle
revision fencing, cancellation propagation, settlement computation or concurrent
multi-client races. These remain B4 work. Native deletion can still queue an
intention later rejected by the server; local conflict presentation/recovery must
be included in desktop acceptance. No B4 parent closure claimed.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_reserved_custody_server_2026-10-20--primary-reservation-backed-custody-server-foundation-2026-10-20"></a>
### Primary reservation-backed custody server foundation — 2026-10-20

Identity / role: primary agent; not helper or visual-agent work.
Scope: B1/B3 server allocation-to-custody coupling. **Partial delivery**, not
offline-first reservation completion, deployment, or Phase 2 closure.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_reserved_custody_server_2026-10-20--stock-issue-matching-allocation"></a>
#### Stock issue / matching allocation

- MODULE: inventory custody and project reservations.
- FILE: `backend/src/inventory-apply.js`.
- CURRENT WRITE PATH: existing immutable movement outbox -> sync broker ->
  inventory version/permission boundary -> transactional stock/custody writer.
- WHY IT BYPASSES OFFLINE-FIRST: the broker is not a bypass. The gap was that
  checkout protected the entire reserved-stock floor without recognizing its own
  reservation; local reservation projection/intent integration is still missing.
- RISK: legitimate reserved issues rejected; naive exclusion could consume other
  allocations or decrement inventory twice.
- RECOMMENDED CHANGE: validate identity, authority, state and quantity; atomically
  decrement only the matching allocation, create custody and fulfillment history,
  and use the existing audit/idempotency transaction.
- ACTUAL CHANGE MADE:
  - Reservation-backed movement requires checkout with a recipient, matching
    item/project, a confirmed remaining quantity and an open planning/active project.
  - Rechecks current active account, projects.edit and project editor authority.
  - Optional task/experiment/requirement references must agree within the project.
  - Quantity arithmetic uses the existing custody thousandths contract.
  - Only the matching fulfilled quantity is deducted from the reserved floor.
    Other reservations remain protected.
  - Movement precedes FK-dependent custody/fulfillment rows. The reservation
    quantity, fulfilled quantity and status update in the broker transaction.
  - Fulfillment request identity uses the movement UUID; exact outbox replay uses
    the existing receipt and does not repeat stock/custody/history/audit writes.
  - Original payload is copied before normalization; immutable receipt input stays
    unchanged. Settlement movement project comes from the stored custody record.
  - Returns restore physical stock but do not automatically reopen an allocation,
    undo consumption history or create any finance transaction.
- VERIFICATION: final **13 PASS / 0 FAIL** real PostgreSQL push-handler batch,
  including five new reservation groups plus the eight earlier custody/project
  groups. Checks cover matching/other allocations, partial/final issue, scope,
  quantity, recipient, active account/role, rollback at receipt failure and replay.
- STATUS: server implementation verified at handler/SQL boundary; native projection,
  reservation selector and full desktop acceptance remain CODE REMAINING.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_reserved_custody_server_2026-10-20--reservation-schema-and-direct-route-compatibility"></a>
#### Reservation schema and direct-route compatibility

- MODULE: reservation requests, decisions and direct consumption fulfillment.
- FILE: `backend/src/routes/projects.js`;
  `backend/src/migrations/20261020_reservation_remaining_quantity.sql`.
- CURRENT WRITE PATH: existing direct HTTP APIs; not converted to offline intents.
- WHY IT BYPASSES OFFLINE-FIRST: request/review/fulfillment still require server
  connectivity. This checkpoint does not disguise them as offline capable.
- RISK: requests omitted NOT NULL original_quantity; final fulfillment attempted
  zero remaining quantity against CHECK(quantity > 0). Opposite reservation/item
  lock order could deadlock with an inventory issue.
- RECOMMENDED CHANGE: preserve original quantity, allow zero only on fulfilled
  reservations, and align lock order before integrating native intent handling.
- ACTUAL CHANGE MADE: request INSERT includes original_quantity; data-preserving
  migration permits zero only for fulfilled status; decision/fulfillment acquire
  item before reservation and recheck item identity.
- VERIFICATION: actual existing PostgreSQL constraint inspected; migration applied
  only inside rollback probe; final issue to zero passed and original constraint
  definition was verified restored afterward. Route syntax checked. Direct HTTP
  routes and true multi-client concurrency have NOT been exercised in this batch.
- STATUS: source changes; migration NOT deployed. Lock-order/live HTTP acceptance
  remains awaiting verification.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_reserved_custody_server_2026-10-20--presentation"></a>
#### Presentation

- MODULE: project reservations.
- FILE: `desktop/src/components/ProjectReservations.tsx`.
- CURRENT WRITE PATH: unchanged.
- WHY IT BYPASSES OFFLINE-FIRST: unchanged online-only request controls.
- RISK: labeling all fulfillment as “consumed” misrepresents issued equipment.
- RECOMMENDED CHANGE: distinguish fulfillment from physical consumption/settlement.
- ACTUAL CHANGE MADE: summary says “fulfilled”; help text explains issue versus
  consumption and retains the explicit offline-unavailable notice.
- VERIFICATION: TypeScript check; no visual/native interaction acceptance claimed.
- STATUS: source-only wording update.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_reserved_custody_server_2026-10-20--test-boundaries-and-operations"></a>
#### Test boundaries and operations

`backend/src/custody-sync-live-probe.mjs` now accepts `reservationMigration` alongside
route, sync, apply, migration and script source. Uses real existing PostgreSQL and
current source loaded in memory. A request/response adapter invokes the actual
push handler; nested savepoints stand in for per-change transactions inside one
outer rollback transaction. Audit implementation's default connection is redirected
into that outer transaction. No actual HTTP/auth middleware, concurrent clients,
desktop SQLite reservation flow or outage acceptance is claimed.

The first expanded batch completed 11 PASS / 1 FAIL because the test inspected
movement data in an intentionally minimal receipt. Changed the assertion to query
the stored movement, without widening receipt exposure; reran the full batch,
then added denied-authority coverage and reran all 13 successfully.

Existing API and PostgreSQL were running when inspected and remain running.
No reset, reseed, persistent test accounts, storage changes, outbox retirement,
desktop restart or deployed API replacement. Test item/user/receipt cleanup and
constraint rollback were verified. No production migration applied.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_reserved_custody_server_2026-10-20--next-bounded-implementation"></a>
#### Next bounded implementation

1. Native reservation snapshots plus account/permission-bound provisional
   allocation changes in the same SQLite transaction as custody and outbox.
2. Preserve pending/rejected work across project pulls; reconcile accepted movement
   identities before allowing an older reservation snapshot to overwrite them.
3. Wire reservation-backed checkout into the project UI without direct API fallback.
4. Test the native flow with Docker API stopped, reopen/retry, then real PostgreSQL
   reconnect and competing-allocation checks. Reservation requests/review intents,
   lifecycle release/settlement and prior direct-route parity remain in Phase 2.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_reserved_custody_native_2026-10-20--atomic-offline-issue"></a>
#### Atomic offline issue

- MODULE: desktop inventory custody / project allocations.
- FILE: `desktop/src-tauri/src/local_inventory.rs`, `inventory_reservations.rs`,
  `inventory_custody.rs`; `desktop/src/api/local-inventory.ts`.
- CURRENT WRITE PATH: UI adapter -> native immediate SQLite transaction -> item,
  movement, custody, immutable outbox event and account-scoped allocation overlay.
- WHY IT BYPASSES OFFLINE-FIRST: the former custody path had no native reservation
  projection/validation. Reservation-only intent could also select the ordinary
  movement adapter, which did not retain that reference.
- RISK: lost reservation identity, repeated allocation while offline, or stock and
  outbox succeeding without a matching local allocation deduction.
- RECOMMENDED CHANGE: bind all effects to one transaction and fail closed on
  missing snapshot, project permission, quantity or work provenance.
- ACTUAL CHANGE MADE: canonical project/reservation/work references; leased
  account and project editor checks; planning/active project check; confirmed
  reservation/item/remaining-quantity checks; same-project task/experiment and
  canonical requirement agreement. Allocation overlays commit with custody,
  item, movement and outbox. Reservation-only intent routes to this writer and
  fails if recipient/checkout requirements are missing. No HTTP fallback.
- VERIFICATION: six new real disk SQLite tests, included in 30 passing inventory
  tests with Docker API stopped. Adapter boundary batch: 48 passing tests.
- STATUS: implemented, awaiting integrated desktop/reconnect acceptance.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_reserved_custody_native_2026-10-20--ack-refresh-and-rejection-reconciliation"></a>
#### ACK, refresh and rejection reconciliation

- MODULE: project pull, native allocation reads, explicit stock conflict recovery.
- FILE: `backend/src/routes/sync.js`,
  `desktop/src-tauri/src/inventory_reservations.rs`, `inventory_sync_state.rs`,
  `local_projects.rs`.
- CURRENT WRITE PATH: authorized project pull stores server reservation snapshots;
  native reads overlay authored issues not yet represented by fulfillment IDs.
- WHY IT BYPASSES OFFLINE-FIRST: project pulls formerly omitted reservations.
  Clearing deductions on ACK alone would expose stale remaining quantities before
  the corresponding project pull arrived.
- RISK: duplicate deduction when pull precedes ACK; resurrected allocation when
  ACK precedes pull; treating explicit rejection retirement as accepted stock work.
- RECOMMENDED CHANGE: keep authored overlays independent of ACK; subtract only
  issues absent from the server snapshot's fulfillment identities. Archive before
  explicit retirement, and block stock edits until authoritative reconciliation.
- ACTUAL CHANGE MADE: one PostgreSQL statement obtains reservation quantities and
  fulfillment movement IDs from the same statement snapshot, limited to readable
  project IDs. Local overlays survive ACK/restart and do not modify the cached
  server base. Included IDs prevent double deduction. Older snapshots without ID
  proof fail closed for issue. Underflow is surfaced as a reconciliation error.
  Conflict resolution archives/removes only affected pending overlays within its
  existing transaction; original outbox payloads remain. Archive failure rolls back
  retirement. Returns do not reopen allocations or credit project expenses.
- VERIFICATION: disk reopen, compact change IDs, normalization, stale snapshot
  after ACK, pull before ACK, atomic injected failures, denied scope/permission,
  released/closed allocation, returns, underflow and rejected-work recovery.
  Real PostgreSQL handler batch: 14 PASS, including coherent pull contents.
- STATUS: bounded source behavior verified; concurrent-client/real transport and
  integrated desktop acceptance remain open. Overlays are retained, not garbage
  collected; retention must not remove evidence needed to reject stale snapshots.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_reserved_custody_native_2026-10-20--cached-reads-and-presentation"></a>

  consumption controls. This subcheck changes reads, not those mutation contracts.
- WHY IT BYPASSES OFFLINE-FIRST: desktop reservation reads previously always used

- RISK: offline list unavailable; absent snapshot confused with empty allocation;
  late account response displayed under another login.
- RECOMMENDED CHANGE: native projected reads, explicit unknown state and account
  guards, with separate implementation of remaining mutation workflows.
- ACTUAL CHANGE MADE: desktop reads use the native project projection without
  HTTP fallback; web retains its HTTP read. Missing cache, denied IPC and session
  changes fail closed. Confirmed empty arrays remain distinguishable. Reservation
  query keys include account/session generation; list errors suppress cached rows.
  Local issue deductions and reconciliation errors are labeled in the list.
- VERIFICATION: five adapter tests plus TypeScript. No new visual acceptance claim.
- STATUS: source implementation, awaiting UI acceptance. The project checkout
  dialog is NOT wired yet. Request/review/consumption controls remain online-only;

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_reserved_custody_native_2026-10-20--verification-and-service-state"></a>

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_reservation_intents_server_2026-10-20--primary-implementation-reservation-intent-server-contract"></a>
### Primary implementation — reservation intent server contract

Identity: primary agent, not a helper delivery. Date: October 20, 2026.
Phase 2 IDs: B3/B4, supporting B1. Source-only; not deployed.

- MODULE: project reservation requests and confirm/reject/release decisions.
- FILE: `backend/src/routes/sync.js`; regression harness
  `backend/src/custody-sync-live-probe.mjs`.
- CURRENT WRITE PATH: new `project_reservation` events, operations `request` and
  `decision`, through existing push broker, immutable receipt and transaction.
  Desktop request/decision controls still use their old HTTP paths; not converted.
- WHY IT BYPASSES OFFLINE-FIRST: these operations previously had no sync apply
  contract. HTTP request generated a server identity; HTTP decisions and audit
  were not covered by the new immutable outbox receipt transaction.
- RISK: duplicate requests after uncertain success, repeated approvals, partial
  audit/state success, permission changes between offline authoring and replay.
- RECOMMENDED CHANGE: explicit stable reservation/change IDs; current authority
  checks; item-first locking; reservation, audit and receipt in one transaction.
- ACTUAL CHANGE MADE: new sync handler normalizes copies of IDs without mutating
  receipt payloads, validates dates/positive thousandth quantities/notes, stamps
  requester/reviewer from the current actor, and checks active database role and
  project authority. Requests require a lead/owner/admin with edit authority;
  decisions require admin. Closed projects cannot receive new requests or
  confirmations. Confirmation checks physical stock and existing allocations,
  retaining existing equipment-period overlap versus consumable rules. Release
  changes allocation status only, never returns stock or settles custody. Existing
  same-identity requests with a new change ID fail rather than silently succeeding.
  Audit is mandatory and transactional; post-commit duplicate audit is skipped
  for this entity. Receipts remain minimal acknowledgements, not cached authority.
- VERIFICATION: final complete real existing PostgreSQL handler batch **20 PASS /
  0 FAIL**, including six new request/review cases. Tests cover exact replay,
  receipt-failure rollback, no physical stock movement, foreign project, inactive
  account, current non-admin role, closed project, invalid quantities/dates and
  competing sequential allocations. Test rows and schema changes rolled back;
  syntax and diff whitespace checks pass. The first run exposed missing request
  context in the audit call; fixed and reran the complete batch (19, then 20 cases).
- STATUS: server contract implemented and focused checks passed; native request/
  decision outbox persistence, projection, UI wiring and integrated acceptance
  remain CODE REMAINING. Neither B3 nor B4 is closed.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_reservation_intents_server_2026-10-20--boundaries-and-next-implementation"></a>
#### Boundaries and next implementation

The harness loads current source into the running container without replacing
deployed files. It invokes real handlers against real PostgreSQL with nested
savepoints in one outer rollback transaction. This is not HTTP/auth-middleware
or simultaneous multi-connection testing. The pg concurrency deprecation warning
comes from project-pull Promise.all queries on the harness's shared connection;
no concurrent-client guarantee is inferred from this test.

No native/offline code changed in this batch, so no new stopped-API desktop test
is claimed. No restart, migration deployment, reset, reseed or user-data deletion.
Existing API/database remain running.

Next: save native request/review intentions atomically with their outbox events;
preserve them across refresh/restart/ACK and rejection. A queued confirmation must
remain an intention, never effective offline stock authority. Request IDs survive
retries; pending requests remain distinguishable from server-reviewed allocations.
Then wire existing controls to native commands and test with the API stopped,
followed by reconnect and actual competing-client verification. Existing direct
HTTP parity and consumption/lifecycle work remain open. No new owner decision.

Full implementation-ready and closed parent counts remain **0/18**; this records
a bounded implementation, not completion of the whole remaining Phase 2 plan.

   protects the full reserved-stock floor, including its own reservation.
2. Reservation request/review/fulfillment paths are still direct online APIs;
   complete the agreed local intent/outbox architecture, not error-to-HTTP fallbacks.
3. B3/B4 canonical demand aggregation, lifecycle/cancellation release, explicit
   outstanding-custody settlement and project archival/closure integration.
4. Browser direct task/experiment/BOM APIs currently omit canonical requirement
   write fields; align them with the same guards. Browser task/experiment link
   insertion also needs review against the mandatory project_id migration.
5. Project sync audit currently occurs after commit using best-effort audit. Make
   its transaction/receipt/audit guarantees explicit in the existing audit work;
   this checkpoint does not silently claim custody-level atomicity for projects.
6. Native callers that clone/repeat work and alternate project mutation paths
   still require full relationship coverage review. No exhaustive repository audit
   or existing-data repair is claimed by these bounded guards.

Next implementation: reservation-backed custody issue and local allocation
projection, followed by grouped acceptance. B1, B3, B4 and A1 remain PARTIAL.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_custody_sync_recovery_2026-10-19"></a>
## Primary custody sync replay and rejection recovery — October 19, 2026

Original source: `docs/handoffs/phase2-parallel/PRIMARY_CUSTODY_SYNC_RECOVERY_2026-10-19.md`. Retained historical scope/status.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_custody_sync_recovery_2026-10-19--primary-custody-sync-replay-and-rejection-recovery-october-19-2026"></a>
### Primary custody sync replay and rejection recovery — October 19, 2026

Identity: LABOS-P2-PRIMARY. Continuation of PRIMARY_CUSTODY_REPAIR_2026-10-19.md;
not a helper report and not whole-B1 or Phase 2 acceptance.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_custody_sync_recovery_2026-10-19--server-receiptrejection-verification"></a>
#### Server receipt/rejection verification

MODULE: B1 movement sync, receipt identity, transaction failure and replay.

FILE: `backend/src/custody-sync-live-probe.mjs`; exercises current source from
`routes/sync.js`, `inventory-sync.js`, `inventory-apply.js` and custody migration.

CURRENT WRITE PATH: actual push handler -> permission check -> receipt ownership/
payload check -> version/dependency validation -> stock/custody mutation -> audit
and idempotency receipt in the same transaction.

WHY IT BYPASSES OFFLINE-FIRST: no new bypass found in this tested path. Previous
raw-apply evidence did not test receipt replay or the sync handler transaction.

RISK: a lost reply could duplicate stock; a failed receipt write could leave an
applied movement without a durable acknowledgement; rejected dependencies could
leave partial settlement effects.

RECOMMENDED CHANGE: verify the production handler against existing PostgreSQL,
including failed transaction and replay; do not replace it with another writer.

ACTUAL CHANGE MADE: added a rollback-only probe. Production server code unchanged
in this follow-up. Sources load in memory; deployed files stay untouched. The real
route's BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK are mapped to nested savepoints on a real PostgreSQL
connection inside one outer transaction. Real SQL, constraints, version triggers,
audit and receipt logic run. Fixture users have non-login hashes and random IDs.
Only the exact custody DDL section is used; unrelated canonical-demand ALTERs are
not applied. An injected error at receipt insertion tests the handler's rollback.

VERIFICATION: **5 PASS, 0 FAIL**, rollback verified for users, item, receipts and
original custody table presence. Cases:

1. Replayed issue: one stock debit, custody row, movement and audit entry.
2. Chained return/transfer: predecessor receipts honored; replay changes nothing.
3. Changed payload, foreign device or foreign user cannot reuse the receipt.
4. Missing predecessor and excessive settlement leave no receipt/partial effects.
5. Receipt-write failure rolls back all domain/audit effects; identical retry
   succeeds once, and its replay is a no-op.

Limits: request/response transport and upstream authentication middleware are NOT
exercised. User context is supplied directly to the real handler. This is sequential
handler-level replay, NOT parallel HTTP/multi-device acceptance, real network ACK
loss or a deployed desktop-to-server round trip. Permission revocation mid-request
is not covered. Existing native/renderer checks remain separate evidence.

STATUS: handler-level replay/rejection transaction subcheck verified; deployment,
HTTP/native integration and concurrency acceptance remain open.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_custody_sync_recovery_2026-10-19--local-rejection-resolution-without-losing-authored-work"></a>
#### Local rejection resolution without losing authored work

MODULE: B1 connected inventory/custody rejection resolution; A2 preservation.

FILE: `desktop/src-tauri/src/inventory_sync_state.rs`, `local_db.rs`,
`inventory_custody_persistence_test.rs`.

CURRENT WRITE PATH: explicit Accept server/Dismiss retires the connected pending
inventory chain in a local transaction. Previously it left optimistic custody
balances active until a future refresh.

WHY IT BYPASSES OFFLINE-FIRST: not a transport bypass; local state could remain a
rejected projection with no pending event protecting/explaining it, then be used
as the basis for another stock operation.

RISK: stale custody settlement or new stock edits after rejecting their basis;
loss of visible recovery context once the unresolved-conflict list clears.

RECOMMENDED CHANGE: retain the authored chain and recovery context, invalidate its
active custody projection, and require server reconciliation before further writes.

ACTUAL CHANGE MADE: within existing resolution transaction, archive affected item
and custody JSON, owner, reason and connected change IDs in an account-scoped
`inventory_recovery_<uuid>` state entry. Original outbox payloads remain unchanged
and retained, but explicitly retired chains stop uploading. Remove only affected
active custody rows/completeness markers. Persist per-item reconciliation markers;
shared native version stamping refuses further writes against marked items. An
authorized server item/tombstone merge clears its marker. Wrong-account pulls
cannot clear it. Archive/write failure rolls the resolution back. No new network
fallback, automatic retry with fresh IDs, overwrite, ownership reassignment or
automatic recovery-package pruning.

VERIFICATION: native inventory batch **24 PASS, 0 FAIL, 1 IGNORED**, with Docker
API and PostgreSQL confirmed stopped. Includes prior 21 passes plus three on-disk
tests: immutable rejected retry/overwrite refusal; connected issue/return archival,
reopen persistence, write block, wrong-account pull refusal and authorized rebase;
injected archive failure retaining pending/conflicted work and active projections.
Renderer receipt batch **3 PASS** (missing/duplicate ACK, independent failures,
session switch). The ignored opt-in PostgreSQL two-client native test is not counted
as passing; the separate real PostgreSQL handler probe is described above.
Related native local DB regression batch **4 PASS**; local workbook import batch
**3 PASS**, including permission, stale-account and atomic outbox failure checks.

STATUS: local preservation/reconciliation write barrier implemented and targeted
tests passed, not deployed. Recovery data is retained in SQLite; a user-facing
recovery browser/export, retention policy, per-item reconciliation display and
full native/network round trip remain unfinished. The last item snapshot remains
readable until refreshed; the write barrier prevents using it as a new write base.
This does not close A2 or B1. Project/reservation/serial integration remains open.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_custody_sync_recovery_2026-10-19--runtime-and-preservation-record"></a>
#### Runtime and preservation record

Both existing containers were found stopped (exit 0); the first probe did not run.
Started those existing containers temporarily, ran the rollback-only PostgreSQL
probe, then restored both to stopped before native offline tests. No production
image replacement, permanent migration, stock edits, broad seeding or database
reset. Running desktop not restarted/replaced. Temporary SQLite test databases
contain only generated fixtures; their test-owned files are removed after checks.

Identity: LABOS-P2-PRIMARY. Continues the interrupted October 18 repair of helper
review H1-1/H1-2. This is primary-authored review/fix evidence, not a helper report.
Delivery ID B1 remains PARTIAL. No whole Phase 2 or custody workflow sign-off.
