<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_custody_repair_2026-10-19--desktop-custody-intent-and-quantities"></a>
#### Desktop custody intent and quantities

MODULE: physical issue, partial settlement and recipient transfer.

FILE: `desktop/src/api/items.ts`, `local-inventory.ts`,
`desktop/src/components/InventoryMovementPanel.tsx`,
`desktop/src-tauri/src/local_inventory.rs`, `inventory_custody.rs`, `main.rs`.

CURRENT WRITE PATH: previously the renderer's older movement adapter omitted
custody fields, applied storeroom consumption arithmetic to issued units, and
required a destination location even for transfers between recipients.

WHY IT BYPASSES OFFLINE-FIRST: outbox payload did not preserve the user's intent;
adding server custody tables alone could not establish local custody or balances.

RISK: missing custody, double stock debit, rejected transfers, and silent behavior
differences between newer frontend and older native builds.

RECOMMENDED CHANGE: dedicated native custody transaction, authoritative local
quantity validation, stable identities, account/permission checks and one outbox.

ACTUAL CHANGE MADE: custody intents use `save_local_inventory_custody_movement`.
Ordinary storeroom movement path remains separate. Missing native command fails
without HTTP fallback. The command checks the captured inventory base/account and
inventory.view/adjust_stock permissions, reads current custody within an immediate
transaction, derives quantities using thousandths, writes the item/movement/
custody projection and authored outbox event atomically. Recipient must exist in
the account's cached active directory; linked projects require cached access.
Checkout subtracts stock once; return credits only returned units; consume,
damage, loss and recipient transfer do not subtract stock again or move the
storeroom's location. New custody and settlement IDs derive from movement IDs;
duplicate local custody identities reject. Outbox predecessor/version stamping is
preserved. Pending custody-related movements prevent remote custody cache refresh
from overwriting optimistic balances. Old generic native writer refuses custody
fields instead of ignoring them. UI requires a checkout recipient and sends the
actual settlement type.

VERIFICATION: native pure-model tests cover issue, partial return, all settlement
types, serial unit quantities, three-decimal arithmetic, canonical IDs and
invalid/excessive settlements. Renderer tests confirm full DTO propagation to the
dedicated command, captured account, native receipt, unsupported-command/missing-
snapshot/account-switch failure without HTTP fallback. The follow-up below adds
on-disk SQLite failure injection and connection-reopen evidence. Account-revocation
races, conflict discard/reconciliation and deployed desktop cold restart/reconnect
acceptance have NOT been run for this new command.

STATUS: targeted custody command implemented; integrated verification pending.
This is not full B1 completion. Canonical demand/reservation effects, relationship
validation across tasks/experiments, full serial lifecycle and fine-grained stock
handler coverage remain part of the existing B1/B3/B4 work.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_custody_repair_2026-10-19--server-movementcustody-transaction-ordering"></a>
#### Server movement/custody transaction ordering

MODULE: PostgreSQL issue/settlement apply.

FILE: `backend/src/inventory-apply.js`; `backend/src/custody-live-probe.mjs`.

CURRENT WRITE PATH: existing inventory HTTP/sync transaction and idempotency
receipt call the common movement apply function. Previous helper implementation
inserted custody/settlement rows before their referenced stock movement.

WHY IT BYPASSES OFFLINE-FIRST: server ordering/validation defect, not a new write
transport. Proper outbox delivery still failed immediate foreign keys.

RISK: rejected issues/transfers/settlements; unknown settlement kinds defaulting
to consumption; transferred custody clearing storeroom location; rounding errors.

RECOMMENDED CHANGE: validate/lock first, insert movement before dependent rows,
retain immediate foreign keys and caller transaction/receipt, validate quantity
and transition semantics, and use stable identities.

ACTUAL CHANGE MADE: deferred dependent INSERTs until after movement INSERT;
explicit numeric SQL casts for partial settlement; thousandths for custody
balances; valid transition/recipient/serial/range checks; active-recipient row
lock; UUID normalization; stable new custody and settlement IDs. Old explicit
consume+damage/loss/transfer payloads retain their stated meaning, not an unknown
default. Recipient transfer preserves storeroom stock/location. Existing generic
checkout without a recipient retains legacy semantics; new custody UI requires
one. Existing receipt/transaction authorization wrappers are unchanged.

VERIFICATION: real existing PostgreSQL, not SQLite substitution. The proposed
custody-table DDL and random fixtures ran inside one transaction with bounded lock
and statement timeouts; all were rolled back. The old source reproduced SQLSTATE
23503; revised issue succeeded. First full run exposed SQLSTATE 42P08 in the
settlement numeric parameter; fixed and reran the whole batch with per-check
savepoints and dependency blocking. Final run: 8 PASS, 0 FAIL, rollback verified.
Tests include partial return, consumption, transfer, invalid/excessive settlement,
inactive/missing recipient rejection, fractional serial rejection, decimal zero,
legacy damage semantics and duplicate movement rejection. Raw SQL apply is tested;
this is NOT new middleware, receipt-replay or concurrency acceptance evidence.

STATUS: H1-2 targeted ordering/numeric defect repaired and verified on PostgreSQL;
awaiting coordinated deployment and broader B1 integration acceptance.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_custody_repair_2026-10-19--follow-up-native-persistence-and-cache-isolation"></a>
#### Follow-up — native persistence and cache isolation

Identity: LABOS-P2-PRIMARY; native verification, not helper acceptance.

MODULE: B1 custody transaction and account-scoped custody cache.

FILE: `desktop/src-tauri/src/local_inventory.rs`,
`desktop/src-tauri/src/inventory_custody_persistence_test.rs`.

CURRENT WRITE PATH: Tauri commands delegate to connection-based cores used unchanged
by tests. Each test opens a unique real SQLite file with the production local/outbox
schema and a disposable authorization fixture.

WHY IT BYPASSES OFFLINE-FIRST: no new transport bypass found. A cache identity gap
could associate a server record with the wrong item in the local read projection.

RISK: wrong-item balances; partial stock/custody commits without an outbox event.

RECOMMENDED CHANGE: exercise the real transaction, not only arithmetic/mocked IPC;
validate record/item identity during atomic cache replacement.

ACTUAL CHANGE MADE: extracted connection cores without changing command signatures
or adding fallbacks. Cache rejects wrong-item IDs, duplicate record IDs and existing
identities bound to another item; normalizes record/item UUIDs. Invalid responses
roll back the replacement and retain earlier records.

VERIFICATION:

- Initial full persistence batch: 3 PASS, 3 FAIL. One real defect: foreign-item cache
  acceptance. Two harness mistakes: checking actor_id instead of performed_by, and
  using an authorization-enforcing read to inspect an expired fixture. Corrected
  harness inspection without weakening the production lease check; fixed the cache;
  expanded and reran the whole native inventory batch.
- Final `cargo test ... inventory -- --nocapture`: **21 PASS, 0 FAIL, 1 IGNORED**.
  Includes eight new persistence tests and four custody arithmetic tests. Ignored:
  older opt-in live PostgreSQL/two-client test; not claimed as passing acceptance.
- Actual `labos-labos-api-1` stopped (confirmed false) for both runs. PostgreSQL
  stayed running. API restored in finally; API and DB subsequently confirmed healthy.
  SQLite tests verify the desktop engine, not a substitute server database.
- Cases: committed issue/partial return after connection close/reopen; author,
  version and predecessor persistence; injected snapshot/movement/custody/outbox
  failure with durable rollback; pending-safe cache/snapshot refresh; refresh after
  explicit ACK; wrong account, stale base, missing permission, expired lease and
  missing recipient refusal; duplicate movement/outbox rejection; malformed,
  duplicate and foreign cache rollback; stale competing local connection; failed
  transfer restoring both custody records, then successful transfer without a
  second stock debit.
- This does NOT prove lost-ACK server receipt replay, multi-device concurrency,
  Tauri IPC/UI integration or conflict discard/reconciliation. Earlier real
  PostgreSQL eight-case rollback probe remains separate evidence, not rerun here.

STATUS: native transaction/cache subcheck verified; B1 **PARTIAL**, not CLOSED.
Delivery table's stale PLANNED label corrected to PARTIAL to match implementation.
No deployment, migration, app restart, database reset or user stock edit. Integrated
replay/rejection and reservation/project lifecycle coupling remain open.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_silent_refresh_2026-10-18--findings-and-changes"></a>
#### Findings and changes

MODULE: Resource image/file access.

FILE: `desktop/src/api/resource-uploads.ts`.

CURRENT WRITE PATH: presentation cache populated by native read-only capability
checks; no authored database/server write.

WHY IT BYPASSES OFFLINE-FIRST: not an outbox violation. The cache was cleared
before every asynchronous read, briefly making still-authorized files unavailable
to renders elsewhere in the app.

RISK: image/availability flicker; overlapping reads could publish stale results.

RECOMMENDED CHANGE: atomic publication, session guards and latest-read ordering.

ACTUAL CHANGE MADE: retain the current session's capabilities while refreshing;
replace on success, clear on latest failure, discard superseded responses. Native
file requests still enforce authorization; no permission/lease relaxation.

VERIFICATION: deferred-read tests cover stable URLs, removed access, failure,
stale-result races and account changes. Existing upload tests remain passing.

STATUS: implemented; native visual acceptance pending deployment.

---

MODULE: Video previews in Resources, embedded panels and Downloads.

FILE: `desktop/src/components/VideoResourcePoster.tsx`.

CURRENT WRITE PATH: native authorized poster read -> in-memory blob URL.

WHY IT BYPASSES OFFLINE-FIRST: no write-path bypass. Every metadata sync emits a
poster-refresh event; unchanged bytes previously produced a fresh URL, reloading
the image. Same-account profile notifications also cleared the preview.

RISK: recurring blink, unnecessary decoding, and stale async preview publication.

RECOMMENDED CHANGE: preserve the URL for identical authorized bytes, retain strict
resource/revision/account boundaries, revalidate on profile events.

ACTUAL CHANGE MADE: byte comparison within the existing effect scope; unchanged
bytes keep their URL. Changed content replaces it; missing/denied reads clear it.
Session/revision changes never render the previous scope's image. Cleanup and
sequence guards prevent late loads reviving expired/replaced previews.

VERIFICATION: hook lifecycle tests cover no-op sync, profile refresh, changed
bytes, missing/denied reads, revisions, accounts, expiration and overlapping loads.

STATUS: implemented; actual no-blink native acceptance pending deployment.

---

MODULE: Background page refresh presentation.

FILE: `desktop/src/hooks/useManualRefresh.ts`; Resources, Downloads,
Collaboration, Projects, Users, Reports, Lab Intelligence, Financials, Ledger and
Project Finance pages; `desktop/src/components/ReadAvailabilityNotice.tsx`.

CURRENT WRITE PATH: unchanged query reads/invalidations; React presentation only.

WHY IT BYPASSES OFFLINE-FIRST: not a write-path violation. Query isFetching was
displayed as spinning icons, changing button labels and inserted Updating text
on every automatic poll, even when query data was unchanged.

RISK: distracting motion/layout changes; chart redraw animations replaying.

RECOMMENDED CHANGE: explicit-user refresh progress distinct from background
fetching; preserve real data/error and permission changes.

ACTUAL CHANGE MADE: shared manual-action busy hook on ten pages, fixed Refresh
labels for Downloads/Collaboration, and disabled report/finance chart animation.
Local read timestamp moved to the notice tooltip instead of changing visible
text every poll. Freshness disclaimer remains. Initial loading, read errors,
authorization, query keys, outbox and synchronization frequency are unchanged.
TanStack structural sharing already preserves unchanged data; no global policy
was added that could hide actual edits, deletions or permission failures.

VERIFICATION: manual-action/double-click/error lifecycle and actual QueryClient
structural-sharing tests (identical data, one changed row, deletion).

STATUS: implemented; visual acceptance pending deployment.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_inventory_read_guards_2026-10-18--account-bound-history-custody-and-directory-reads"></a>
#### Account-bound history, custody and directory reads

MODULE: inventory movements, field history, assignment history, custody, assignees.

FILE: `desktop/src/api/items.ts`; regression cases in
`desktop/src/api/inventory-boundaries.test.mjs`.

CURRENT WRITE PATH: reads load an account-scoped SQLite snapshot, optionally GET
the server, then persist the result through account-checked native cache commands.
These cache writes are server projections, not authored business mutations.

WHY IT BYPASSES OFFLINE-FIRST: previous helper paths could return old-account
rows after asynchronous reads, treat HTTP refusal as an offline fallback, swallow
cache failures, and return raw remote rows without checking the session again.
The older movement path also returned captured cache rows on transport failure
without rechecking native lease/permission after the network wait.

RISK: stale-account data exposure; denial disguised as successful cached access;
expired native authorization overlooked while a request was pending.

RECOMMENDED CHANGE: capture a session before reads, check every asynchronous
success boundary, distinguish HTTP refusal from connectivity failure, and reread
the native snapshot on fallback so native authorization is enforced again.

ACTUAL CHANGE MADE: five getters share an account-bound read helper. Unsigned
reads fail before IPC. Local-only/offline sessions return their authorized snapshot
without HTTP; a missing snapshot errors instead of claiming an empty list. HTTP
4xx errors, malformed responses and cache-write failures propagate. Transport/5xx
fallback rereads SQLite and rechecks the session. Successful refreshes validate an
array, cache with the captured account, then reread local state; this preserves
the existing movement cache's pending-safe merge. No retry IDs, outbox events,
business mutations, native permission checks or server routes were changed.

VERIFICATION: five-reader contract matrix covers native-read/request/JSON/cache/
post-cache session switches, same-account generation changes, network/5xx fallback,
lease expiry, 400/401/403/404/409/429, malformed JSON/data, missing versus empty
snapshots, disk failure, unsigned reads and captured cache account. Existing
inventory write-boundary and HTTP-idempotency tests remain in the batch.

STATUS: implemented source guard repair; native integrated verification pending.
Online calls still await their optional HTTP refresh. Decoupling those refreshes
from first local rendering, wider history projection and B6 coverage remain open;
this does not certify the whole offline-first inventory architecture.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_inventory_read_guards_2026-10-18--retained-query-data-and-false-empty-states"></a>
#### Retained query data and false empty states

MODULE: inventory history and movement panels.

FILE: `desktop/src/components/ItemHistoryPanel.tsx`,
`desktop/src/components/InventoryMovementPanel.tsx`,
`desktop/src/components/inventory-read-availability.test.mjs`.

CURRENT WRITE PATH: React Query reads; existing stock action handlers unchanged.

WHY IT BYPASSES OFFLINE-FIRST: retained data can remain in a failed query, while
missing snapshots were displayed as empty history or usable movement context.

RISK: stale records rendered after refusal; movement actions based on unavailable
custody/directory information; misleading no-history messages.

RECOMMENDED CHANGE: partition query keys by account/login generation, mask denied
query data, distinguish unavailable from confirmed empty, and retain retry paths.

ACTUAL CHANGE MADE: account and generation appended to query keys (no bearer token
in keys; existing invalidation prefixes preserved). Field/assignment history mask
the failed section while retaining the successful section. Movement panel hides
retained rows and action controls when any required read fails or initially loads.
Valid offline snapshots continue through the normal UI. No stock form values are
reset by this error presentation; existing component state remains mounted.

VERIFICATION: four server-rendered component tests cover failed retained rows,
partial history, missing/empty/loading distinction, action suppression and key
partitioning. This is real component rendering with query doubles, not native UI.

STATUS: implemented, awaiting integrated desktop acceptance.

<a id="source-docshandoffsphase2-parallelprimary_review_2026-10-17--h1-3-salvage-introduces-direct-server-mutations-and-incomplete-provenance-p1"></a>
#### H1-3 — salvage introduces direct server mutations and incomplete provenance [P1]

MODULE: B2 create/inspect/release recovery.

FILE: `desktop/src/api/items.ts` lines 235–266;
`backend/src/routes/items.js` salvage routes around lines 35–190.

CURRENT WRITE PATH: desktop directly POSTs create/inspect/release; server inserts
new recovery rows and credits stock without an authored local outbox flow.

WHY IT BYPASSES OFFLINE-FIRST: no native salvage transaction or durable local
intent; new recovery create has no supplied stable request identity/receipt.

RISK: offline failure and duplicate recovery on uncertain create/retry. Source
checks establish only item existence, not an original issue/consumption balance
or cumulative recovery limit. Separate recovery rows can credit the same source.
Inspection reads then updates without a row lock/status predicate, while release
locks the row: a delayed inspection can overwrite a released status.
The list selects `s.*` under inventory.view without separate project/valuation
projection. Recovery value is copied into replacement_cost and unit_cost is set
to zero, conflating the approved value boundaries.

RECOMMENDED CHANGE: ordinary local/outbox salvage operations with stable IDs,
source-ledger limits and scoped permissions; lock/validate transitions and source
quantities together. Preserve unknown cost and separate reviewed recovery value.
Filter financial/project fields independently; never fabricate a cash transaction.

ACTUAL CHANGE MADE: none; review only. No existing recovery records altered.

VERIFICATION: source inspection, not live race/security acceptance.

STATUS: CODE REMAINING; no B2 acceptance or deployment approval from this review.

revocation/permission denial. Exact user-visible race needs a targeted test.

RECOMMENDED CHANGE: shared account-captured read guard before every return, distinct
permission/lease failure handling, and local-first rendering independent of HTTP.

ACTUAL CHANGE MADE: none; review only.

### Primary-agent spot review and bounded follow-up

Author: PRIMARY LABOS IMPLEMENTATION AGENT
Date: 2026-10-16
Reviewed contributor: LABOS-VISUAL-AGENT / 20261015T204138Z-visual-01
Decision: CHANGES REQUESTED; not whole-phase or running-UI acceptance

<a id="source-docsvisual-agent-reportsphase320261015t204138z-visual-01primary_review--findings"></a>
#### Findings

Compared the handoff/blockers/verification reports with selected working-tree
diffs against the reported baseline. This is the requested small cross-check,
not exhaustive review of every visual hunk. No visual-agent backend/native/API
edits were identified in its declared inventory; the separate primary-agent
functional changes remain in those directories and must not be attributed to it.

1. `ItemDetailPage.tsx` adds editable `unit_cost` and `replacement_cost` inputs and
   new `setEditForm` handlers, despite the report describing read-only cards.
   This expands mutation surface and needs functional review. It is not accepted
   as a visual-only change.
2. `ItemDetailPage.tsx` and `AddItemModal.tsx` conflate replacement cost with salvage/
   recovery valuation. These are distinct approved concepts. Transaction direction
   alone also does not establish actual cash settlement; do not label every expense
   as "Actual Cash Outflow" or income as "Cash / Allocation Inflow".
3. `ProjectBomPanel.tsx` adds matching scores and ordering, and `NotebookPage.tsx`
   adds selection-based TTS/pause/resume/stop. Both change behavior. The blanket
   attestation that state/effects/handlers are unchanged is incorrect. These changes
   remain unaccepted functional proposals, not completed Phase 3 styling. Preserve
   their work pending ownership review; do not revert them wholesale.
4. `AssistantChat.tsx` adds local popover state/effects/navigation. A narrow UI-only
   exception is approved below, but reduced-motion CSS does not override explicit
   `scrollIntoView({behavior:'smooth'})`. Keyboard/focus behavior still needs checks.
5. Build success is not evidence that clipping, scrolling, focus or hardware audio
   works. Reports currently describe several such outcomes as verified without
   corresponding runtime evidence. Correct these to source-inspected/NOT RUN.
   Also, a dev desktop configured with `devPath: http://localhost:1420` can display
   new frontend code without a native rebuild; distinguish that from packaged UI.

<a id="source-docsvisual-agent-reportsphase320261015t204138z-visual-01primary_review--limited-follow-up-authorization"></a>
#### Limited follow-up authorization

The owner authorized granting bounded permissions to finish this contributor's
work. This addendum permits only:

- `AssistantChat.tsx` and its scoped `ui2.css` selectors: transient menu state,
  refs and listeners solely for open/close, focus return, keyboard navigation,
  outside-click dismissal and reduced-motion-aware scrolling. No network,
  conversation identity, persistence, context authority or message mutation changes.
- `ItemDetailPage.tsx` / `AddItemModal.tsx`: accurate presentation wording. Use
  "Replacement cost" for `replacement_cost`; no salvage-value claim. Use neutral
  "Income"/"Expense" labels unless stronger financial semantics are proven.
  Make the newly added detail valuation cards read-only by removing only this
  contributor's added edit branches/handlers; preserve existing authorized inputs
  elsewhere and all existing item data, handlers and guards.
- Existing visual-only CSS/markup in the contributor's declared files: bounded
  responsive/accessibility corrections and real visual verification. No new
  component data contracts or mutation behavior.
- Correct contributor reports, preserving history and explicitly acknowledging
  scope drift. List source inspection, build results and runtime checks separately.

Do NOT extend TTS, BOM ranking, batch reservations, voice transcription, proposal
acceptance, retries or backend/sync functionality. They remain primary-owned
functional review/dependencies. A batch reservation design must start from native
SQLite + outbox, not a new direct UI POST; no SQLite/PostgreSQL cross-store atomic
transaction is implied. Audio coordination does not automatically require native
OS changes: the correct boundary will be decided in Phase 2 C3.

DownloadsPage, VideoResourcePoster, DownloadResourcePreview, all APIs/native/backend
and authoritative audit/phase ledgers remain excluded. A commit is not a prerequisite
for collaboration, but explicit current file ownership/baseline agreement is.

Record follow-up edits with new change IDs in this run's contributor reports.
All remain AWAITING PRIMARY REVIEW. Do not edit this primary review to self-approve.
No merge, deployment, restart or data-changing UI tests are authorized here.

<a id="source-docsvisual-agent-reportsphase320261015t204138z-visual-01changelog--change-vis-06-notebook-selective-read-aloud-with-pause-continue-and-stop"></a>
#### Change VIS-06: Notebook Selective Read Aloud with Pause, Continue, and Stop

- Date: 2026-10-15
- Batch: Batch 5 (Project Context, BOM Match, and Notebook Polish)
- Files & Lines:
  - `desktop/src/pages/NotebookPage.tsx` : L3, L38, L147-L195, L358-L374
- Before vs. After:
  - Before: Read aloud button was a single toggle that read the entire note from the beginning using Web Speech API, or stopped playback. It could not pause/resume, and could not read only a selected portion of the note.
  - After:
    - Selective Reading: `handleReadAloud` inspects the body textarea selection (`bodyRef.current.selectionStart !== bodyRef.current.selectionEnd`). If text is highlighted, only the highlighted text is read aloud; if no text is highlighted, it falls back to reading the full note title and body.
    - Pause / Continue: When speaking, clicking the Read Aloud button calls `window.speechSynthesis.pause()` and displays a `Play` icon to indicate "Continue reading". Clicking again calls `window.speechSynthesis.resume()`.
    - Dedicated Stop Button: While speaking or paused, a dedicated `Square` stop button appears in the toolbar calling `window.speechSynthesis.cancel()` to cleanly terminate playback and reset states.
- Design Rationale:
  - Provides rich, accessible note review experience allowing researchers to listen to specific passages, pause during note-taking, and resume without losing place or re-reading the entire document.
- Preserved Behavior:
  - Note saving, tag editing, symbol picker, voice dictation, deletion, mutations, and query state remain completely untouched.
  - Uses standard Web Speech API without external dependencies or native permission escalations.
- Verification Reference:
  - `desktop/` production build `npm run build` passed (exit code 0, 10.94s).
- Review Status: VISUAL IMPLEMENTATION — AWAITING PRIMARY REVIEW

<a id="source-docsauditslabos_remediation_and_verification_2026-09-20--4-decisions"></a>
### 4. DECISIONS

<a id="source-docsauditslabos_remediation_and_verification_2026-09-20--decision-001"></a>
#### DECISION-001

**Date/Time**: 2026-09-20 18:05 UTC

**Problem**: Backend and Tauri duplicate detection use different parent-context fields for link resources.

**Evidence**:
- Direct API test created two resources with identical YouTube URL (dQw4w9WgXcQ) in same parent context
- Tauri duplicate check (local_resources.rs lines 237-239) includes: kind, normalized URL, item_id, project_id, note_id, AND parent_resource_id
- Backend duplicate check (resources.js line 31) includes: kind, normalized URL, item_id, project_id, note_id, but NOT parent_resource_id
- PostgreSQL schema has constraint ensuring exactly one parent (item_id OR project_id OR note_id OR parent_resource_id)
- No database-level uniqueness constraint exists for link resources

**Options Considered**:
A. Remove parent_resource_id from Tauri logic to match backend
B. Add parent_resource_id to backend logic to match Tauri
C. Introduce database-level uniqueness constraint as canonical enforcement
D. Combination of B + C for strongest guarantee

**Decision Made**: Option D - Add parent_resource_id to backend duplicate check AND add database-level partial unique index

**Reason**:
1. parent_resource_id is a valid parent context (folders can contain resources)
2. A resource in different folders should be considered different resources
3. Application-level checks are race-prone under concurrent requests
4. Database constraint provides definitive prevention regardless of application layer
5. Combining both ensures backward compatibility while providing strong guarantee
6. PostgreSQL partial unique index allows NULL values (for unattached resources)

**Files Affected**:
- backend/src/routes/resources.js (application-level check)
- New migration file (database constraint)

**Potential Consequences**:
- Existing duplicate resources in database may prevent migration
- Need to handle existing duplicates in migration
- Concurrent requests will now fail with constraint violation instead of creating duplicates
- API will return existing resource instead of creating duplicate (matching intended behavior)

**How Decision Will Be Verified**:
1. Create migration with safe handling of existing duplicates
2. Test migration on test database first
3. Verify API duplicate prevention after fix
4. Test concurrent duplicate requests

**Important Discovery**: Production database already contains duplicates from earlier audit test (URL: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ, count: 2, no parent context). Migration must handle this gracefully.

<a id="source-docsauditslabos_remediation_and_verification_2026-09-20--5-code-changes"></a>
### 5. CODE CHANGES

<a id="source-docsauditslabos_remediation_and_verification_2026-09-20--change-001"></a>
#### CHANGE-001
**File**: backend/src/routes/resources.js

**Before**:
```javascript
function parentFields(body) { return { item_id: body.item_id || null, project_id: body.project_id || null, note_id: body.note_id || null }; }
function validateAtMostOneParent({ item_id, project_id, note_id }) { return [item_id, project_id, note_id].filter(Boolean).length <= 1; }
```

**After**:
```javascript
function parentFields(body) { return { item_id: body.item_id || null, project_id: body.project_id || null, note_id: body.note_id || null, parent_resource_id: body.parent_resource_id || null }; }
function validateAtMostOneParent({ item_id, project_id, note_id, parent_resource_id }) { return [item_id, project_id, note_id, parent_resource_id].filter(Boolean).length <= 1; }
```

**Reason**: Add parent_resource_id to parent field extraction and validation to match Tauri local duplicate detection logic

**Decision**: DECISION-001

**Verification**: TEST-001 (duplicate prevention test)

<a id="source-docsauditslabos_remediation_and_verification_2026-09-20--change-002"></a>
#### CHANGE-002
**File**: backend/src/routes/resources.js

**Before**:
```javascript
const duplicate=await pool.query('SELECT * FROM resources WHERE kind=\'link\' AND lower(btrim(url))=lower($1) AND item_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM $2 AND project_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM $3 AND note_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM $4 ORDER BY (local_media_path IS NOT NULL) DESC, created_at ASC LIMIT 1',[normalizedUrl,parents.item_id||null,parents.project_id||null,parents.note_id||null]);
```

**After**:
```javascript
const duplicate=await pool.query('SELECT * FROM resources WHERE kind=\'link\' AND lower(btrim(url))=lower($1) AND item_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM $2 AND project_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM $3 AND note_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM $4 AND parent_resource_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM $5 ORDER BY (local_media_path IS NOT NULL) DESC, created_at ASC LIMIT 1',[normalizedUrl,parents.item_id||null,parents.project_id||null,parents.note_id||null,parents.parent_resource_id||null]);
```

**Reason**: Add parent_resource_id to duplicate detection WHERE clause to match Tauri logic and ensure folder-contained resources are checked correctly

**Decision**: DECISION-001

**Verification**: TEST-001 (duplicate prevention test)

<a id="source-docsauditslabos_remediation_and_verification_2026-09-20--6-databasemigration-changes"></a>
### 6. DATABASE/MIGRATION CHANGES

<a id="source-docsauditslabos_remediation_and_verification_2026-09-20--change-003"></a>
#### CHANGE-003
**File**: backend/src/migrations/043_resource_link_duplicate_constraint.sql (new file)

**Content**:
```sql
-- Add partial unique index to prevent duplicate link resources
-- This ensures that link resources with the same URL cannot be created
-- in the same parent context (item_id, project_id, note_id, or parent_resource_id)
-- The index is partial (WHERE kind = 'link') to only apply to link resources
-- NULL values are allowed for parent fields (unattached resources)

-- First, handle any existing duplicates by keeping the most recently created one
WITH duplicates AS (
  SELECT
    id,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
      PARTITION BY
        lower(btrim(url)),
        item_id,
        project_id,
        note_id,
        parent_resource_id
      ORDER BY created_at DESC
    ) as rn
  FROM resources
  WHERE kind = 'link' AND url IS NOT NULL
)
DELETE FROM resources
WHERE id IN (SELECT id FROM duplicates WHERE rn > 1);

-- Create the partial unique index
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX idx_resources_link_unique
ON resources (lower(btrim(url)), item_id, project_id, note_id, parent_resource_id)
WHERE kind = 'link' AND url IS NOT NULL;
```

**Reason**: Add database-level constraint to provide definitive duplicate prevention regardless of application layer, with safe handling of existing duplicates

**Decision**: DECISION-001

**Verification**: Migration applied successfully in test environment (043_resource_link_duplicate_constraint.sql)

**Recommendation**:
1. Apply migration 043 to production after database backup
2. Establish dedicated test environment with GUI support for Tauri testing
3. Implement automated integration tests for critical sync and download workflows
4. Test offline-first behavior comprehensively before declaring production-ready


## 2026-11-01 — PRIMARY — B3/B4 browser project work mutation batch

MODULE: project tasks, experiments, task-experiment relationships.

FILE: backend/src/project-work-http.js; backend/src/routes/project-workspace.js;
desktop/src/api/project-work-http.ts; desktop/src/api/projects.ts;
desktop/src/pages/ProjectDetailPage.tsx; focused tests and
backend/src/project-work-http-live-probe.mjs.

CURRENT WRITE PATH: desktop ordinary operations invoke native SQLite/outbox
commands and return before the browser transport. Browser operations use the
existing project routes through a shared server-confirmed HTTP adapter. Browser
retry identity is account-bound sessionStorage, not a durable desktop outbox or
automatically executed offline browser queue.

WHY IT BYPASSES OFFLINE-FIRST: the previous browser handlers performed direct
pool writes and a later separate best-effort audit, without retry receipts or
reviewed-value guards. They must not be used as native failure fallbacks.
Browser HTTP remains an intentional transport; it is not substituted for native
persistence. This batch does not convert every remaining nested writer.

RISK: duplicate task/experiment/repeat effects after a lost acknowledgement;
stale edits or link upserts replacing newer work; current permissions changing
after middleware; deletion removing records without pull tombstones; background
refresh replacing an open editor's reviewed base.

RECOMMENDED CHANGE: retain native/outbox paths; make browser mutations, audit,
receipt and tombstones atomic, with stable account-owned retry bodies, reviewed
editable values, normalized UUID/date fields and current transactional authority.

ACTUAL CHANGE MADE: replaced nine direct task/experiment/repeat/link handlers
with a shared transaction adapter, then extended it to five measurement/
observation create/update/delete handlers. These nested records bind to the
experiment within the route project, compare reviewed values and return explicit
project/experiment-scoped confirmations. Optional blank observation times become
null; numeric zero remains valid and invalid measurement values fail validation.
Create/repeat UUIDs derive from the immutable
retry key. Exact payload receipts reject changed-key reuse; uncertain retries
return the original result without reapplying it. Every replay rechecks authority.
Task/experiment edit/delete/repeat require the reviewed editable snapshot, rather
than silently fetching a new base. Forms preserve the snapshot with their drafts;
delete confirmations carry their reviewed row and failed saves retain input.
Links compare the reviewed relationship, retain stable UUID/project scope and
never upsert over a concurrent insertion. Deletion writes parent and cascaded
child tombstones atomically with required audit and a non-null receipt. Browser
transport refuses desktop runtime and offline-login tokens, fences account
changes and rejects malformed/wrong-scope acknowledgements. Editable-value
comparison is not a full version/ABA guarantee. Shared server/domain date and
observation-text contracts are preserved; sync handlers were not rewritten.

VERIFICATION: final combined client batch: 84 PASS, 0 FAIL. Final backend
boundary/validation batch: 33 PASS, 0 FAIL, 1 opt-in PostgreSQL SKIP. TypeScript
noEmit, route/adapter/probe syntax checks and tracked-file diff whitespace checks
PASS. Earlier focused runs overlap these counts and are not summed.
Added actual-PostgreSQL probe
LABOS_DEV_PROJECT_WORK_PROBE=rollback-only using production auth/routes, real SQL
and rollback-only fixtures. It exercises audit/receipt SQL failure rollback,
create/update/repeat replay, stale bases, link removal/re-add, cascade tombstones
and late role/disabled/permission changes, including replay authority. The probe
was syntax checked but NOT RUN: elevated docker info confirms the Linux engine
pipe is absent. No fake database was used as a substitute. Independent-client
concurrency, stopped-API desktop/reconnect and coordinated deployment remain
unverified. Existing databases, files, pending work and installed V1 were not
changed by this source batch.

STATUS: source implemented, integrated PostgreSQL/desktop acceptance pending.
B3/B4 parent closure states remain PARTIAL. Next: work attachments and their
transactional resource permissions; then the remaining fixed checklist.


## 2026-11-02 — PRIMARY — B3/B4 attachment transport and native/sync parity

MODULE: task/experiment resource links, browser writes and native outbox apply.

FILE: backend/src/project-work-attachment.js, project-work-authority.js,
project-work-http.js, routes/project-workspace.js, routes/sync.js;
desktop/src/api/project-work-http.ts, projects.ts;
desktop/src/pages/ProjectDetailPage.tsx;
desktop/src-tauri/src/local_projects.rs; focused tests and the existing
project-work-http-live-probe.mjs.

CURRENT WRITE PATH: desktop attach/detach stays in SQLite + immutable outbox,
then the normal authenticated push. Browser attach/detach stays server-confirmed
through four existing project routes. Both fresh server application paths now
call the same attachment domain handler inside their owned transaction.

WHY IT BYPASSES OFFLINE-FIRST: prior browser routes wrote attachments directly
without retry identity/audit/receipts; native validation accepted any locally
readable resource while the browser required a direct same-project resource.
The generic server sync writer had no corresponding resource-read/scope check.
No desktop-to-HTTP fallback has been introduced to address these gaps.

RISK: duplicate links after repeated/uncertain requests; deleting a sibling work
item's link by supplying its ID under another work URL; cross-project or revoked
resource attachment through sync; unaudited writes; attachment endpoints silently
changing; unlink retries removing later replacements.

RECOMMENDED CHANGE: preserve native outbox and immutable authoring, share current
server authority/scope validation, and make browser effect/audit/receipt/tombstone
atomic. Bind the reviewed resource ID and parent; prevent local duplicate pairs.

ACTUAL CHANGE MADE: extracted the existing locked project authority helper for
reuse. Shared attachment create/delete validates normalized UUIDs, exactly one
work parent, stored endpoint identity and current parent project. Create checks
current resources.view, locks the resource and restricted-resource grant, and
requires its direct same-project scope. New identities cannot resurrect matching
tombstones; duplicate pair inserts conflict rather than overwrite another link.
Browser create replays recheck current resource access; original retry bodies are
retained across refreshed reviewed values. Detach binds the reviewed resource,
requires current project edit authority, and permits cleanup without current
resource read access. It deletes only the link, records a tombstone, and cannot
remove a subsequently recreated link with a different identity. A previously
removed link needs a matching project-scoped tombstone for an already-deleted
acknowledgement. No physical file or resource deletion is invoked.

Native create/update now matches direct project scope, normalizes comparisons,
prevents duplicate pairs and refuses endpoint edits. Existing invalid pending
intents were not rewritten, dropped or marked synced. The canonical fresh sync
attachment writer now delegates to the same server domain handler. Existing
owned sync receipt replay still returns its minimal acknowledgement, not historical
resource contents or an access grant; it does not reapply the old effect.

VERIFICATION: final client project/editor/transport batch 86 PASS; backend
permission/review/validation batch 35 PASS, 1 opt-in PostgreSQL SKIP; native
local_projects suite 20 PASS, including persisted outbox/restart regressions and
new direct-scope/duplicate/endpoint checks. TypeScript noEmit, JS syntax and
tracked-file diff whitespace checks PASS. Expanded the rollback-only actual
PostgreSQL probe for attachment create/delete audit/receipt SQL failure rollback,
duplicate pairs, wrong-parent/expected-resource deletion, restricted grant/replay
revocation, cleanup and unlink/re-add retry. Probe syntax PASS; execution NOT RUN:
elevated docker info still reports the Docker Desktop Linux engine pipe absent.
No mocked database substituted for that acceptance. No API update, installed V1
restart, deployment or live data migration occurred.

STATUS: source implemented, PostgreSQL/desktop/reconnect/deployment acceptance
pending; parent checklist B3/B4 stays PARTIAL. Next independent boundary: browser
BOM and project inventory-link writes and their canonical demand/quantity guards.


## 2026-11-02 — PRIMARY — B3/B4 BOM and project item planning writes

MODULE: BOM demand and project inventory planning links; browser/native parity.

FILE: backend/src/project-planning-intents.js, project-work-review.js,
project-work-http.js, routes/project-workspace.js, routes/sync.js;
desktop/src/api/projects.ts, project-work-http.ts, project-plan-refresh.ts;
desktop/src/components/ProjectBomPanel.tsx, pages/ProjectDetailPage.tsx;
desktop/src-tauri/src/local_projects.rs; focused tests and the existing
project-work-http-live-probe.mjs.

CURRENT WRITE PATH: browser BOM CRUD and item-link set/remove use five existing
routes via the shared transactional HTTP adapter. Desktop continues SQLite and
immutable outbox. Server item-link application is now shared between browser and
native sync. Shared work reviewed-value projection was extracted from the HTTP
adapter to a reusable domain module, retaining existing exports for callers.

WHY IT BYPASSES OFFLINE-FIRST: the old browser writes had independent direct
pool mutations and later audit calls, no stable receipts and no reviewed bases.
Native planning events lacked reviewed-state tokens; quantity validation also
allowed values the NUMERIC(12,3) columns would round or reject. No native error
is converted to HTTP to work around these boundaries.

RISK: duplicate BOM lines/repeated item effects after uncertain outcomes; stale
demand/allocation overwrites or stale deletions; fractional/range mismatch;
confusing a planning allocation with physical issue; and atomic audit failure
when a composite project:item sync entity identity is inserted into a UUID audit
column. The latter was identified by inspecting the schema and write path;
actual PostgreSQL reproduction remains pending.

RECOMMENDED CHANGE: atomic effect/audit/receipt, reviewed demand and link bases,
current project authority, canonical requirement references, stable identity and
consistent quantity boundaries. Preserve existing authored events and physical
stock/reservation/custody/accounting semantics.

ACTUAL CHANGE MADE: added browser BOM CRUD and item-link set/remove to the common
adapter. BOM creates/retries retain stable UUIDs; edit/delete compares the complete
reviewed editable snapshot, normalizing PostgreSQL decimal representation and
ignoring joined stock display fields. BOM requirement pointers remain explicit
same-project references; the handler does not create a second requirement or
silently change canonical requirement quantity. Selected inventory references
must exist. Removed lines write the canonical project_bom tombstone. The BOM form
freezes its reviewed base while editing and passes the reviewed row on removal.

Shared item-link application locks current project/account authority, compares
reviewed quantity/notes when present, and changes only project_items. The browser
requires a reviewed base; null means no existing pair. New native events capture
their old values, and native persistence checks the cache again under its SQLite
transaction before committing the new snapshot and outbox event. Native BOM
edit/delete similarly carry a complete reviewed snapshot, checked during fresh
server application. UUID and quantity comparisons are normalized. Quantity limits
match nine whole digits and three decimal places, with floating-point tolerance;
zero is allowed for item links and not BOM demand. Native and form validation
reject unsupported values before persistence/submission. Item-link audit rows use
the item UUID; the original composite identity remains unchanged in the receipt
and sync audit metadata. No item movement, reservation approval, custody or cash
mutation is posted by these planning paths.

Compatibility limit: pre-existing immutable events without reviewed values keep
their prior compatibility behavior and therefore weaker conflict detection. No
pending event was rewritten, discarded or falsely acknowledged by this batch.
Expected-value checks are not full monotonic version/ABA detection. Item links
remain a composite identity and use the existing authoritative snapshot for
removal convergence, rather than misusing item UUID tombstones across projects.

VERIFICATION: 87 client project/editor/transport checks PASS; 37 backend
permission/review/planning checks PASS; 22 native project checks PASS, including
new disk SQLite stale-save rollback, unchanged cached state/outbox on rejection,
accepted intent payload and restart/integrity verification. TypeScript noEmit,
JS syntax and tracked-file whitespace checks PASS. Expanded actual PostgreSQL
rollback-only probe covers BOM/item audit/receipt failures, retry/stale bases,
unlink/re-add, real production sync push with composite entity ID and UUID audit,
and unchanged physical quantity/no item movements. Probe syntax PASS; NOT RUN:
elevated docker info reports Docker Desktop Linux engine pipe absent. No mocked
DB substitutes for that acceptance. No API/desktop deployment, installed V1
update, live data migration or reset occurred.

STATUS: source implemented, real PostgreSQL and running-desktop/reconnect /
coordinated deployment acceptance pending. Parent B3/B4 remain PARTIAL. Next:
canvas blocks/connectors and remaining canonical requirement writers.
